questions.stem: In Town A, 13 out of every 50 people ride bikes. In Town B, 24 out of every 100 people ride bikes. How many more people out of every 100 ride bikes in Town A than in Town B?
questions.solution: In Town A, 13 out of 50 is 26 out of 100. Town B has 24 out of 100. The difference is $26 - 24 = 2$ more people out of every 100.

questions.skill: Finding a part: percent of a quantity
questions.stem: Of the 200 students in the sixth grade, 45% play a sport. How many of the sixth graders do not play a sport?
questions.solution: 45% of 200 is $0.45 \times 200 = 90$ students who play a sport. The others number $200 - 90 = 110$. (Or: 55% of 200 is 110.)

questions.skill: Finding a part: percent of a quantity
questions.stem: A class has 40 students. 60% of them are girls. 25% of the boys wear glasses. How many boys wear glasses?
questions.solution: The boys are $100\% - 60\% = 40\%$ of the class, which is $0.4 \times 40 = 16$ boys. 25% of 16 is $16 \div 4 = 4$ boys.

questions.skill: Finding a part: percent of a quantity
questions.stem: A school has 400 students. 35% are in grade 6 and 40% are in grade 7. How many more students are in grade 7 than in grade 6?
questions.solution: Grade 7 has $0.40 \times 400 = 160$ students and grade 6 has $0.35 \times 400 = 140$. The difference is $160 - 140 = 20$ students.

questions.skill: Finding a part: percent of a quantity
questions.stem: Which of these amounts is the greatest?
questions.solution: 30% of 90 is 27; 45% of 70 is 31.5; 60% of 50 is 30; 20% of 120 is 24. The greatest is 45% of 70.

questions.skill: Finding the whole from a part and a percent
questions.stem: The dough for a loaf of bread is 40% flour by weight. The flour weighs 150 grams. How many grams does all of the dough weigh?
questions.solution: 40% of the dough is 150 grams, so 10% is $150 \div 4 = 37.5$ grams. The whole dough is 100%, which is $37.5 \times 10 = 375$ grams.

questions.skill: Finding the whole from a part and a percent
questions.stem: After Jo spent 35% of her savings, she had 78 dollars left. How many dollars did she have at first?
questions.solution: Jo has $100\% - 35\% = 65\%$ left, and that is 78 dollars. So 1% is $78 \div 65 = 1.2$ dollars and 100% is $1.2 \times 100 = 120$ dollars. (113 adds 35, 43 subtracts 35, and 27.3 is 35% of 78.)

questions.skill: Finding the whole from a part and a percent
questions.stem: Only 6% of the seats in a theater are empty. There are 9 empty seats. How many seats does the theater have?
questions.solution: 6% of the seats is 9, so 1% is $9 \div 6 = 1.5$ seats. All the seats, 100%, is $1.5 \times 100 = 150$.

questions.skill: Finding the whole from a part and a percent
questions.stem: Ana has finished 72 problems, which is 90% of her assignment. How many problems does she still have to do?
questions.solution: 90% is 72 problems, so 10% is $72 \div 9 = 8$ problems. She still has 10% left, which is 8 problems.

questions.skill: Finding the percent from a part and a whole
questions.stem: Pat got 34 questions right on a 40-question quiz. What percent of the questions did Pat get wrong?
questions.solution: Pat missed $40 - 34 = 6$ questions. $\frac{6}{40} = \frac{15}{100}$, so 15% were wrong. (85% is the percent right.)

questions.skill: Finding the percent from a part and a whole
questions.stem: Of 300 students, 120 chose pizza, 75 chose tacos and the rest chose salad. What percent of the students chose salad?
questions.solution: $120 + 75 = 195$ students chose pizza or tacos, so $300 - 195 = 105$ chose salad. $\frac{105}{300} = \frac{35}{100}$, which is 35%. (40% chose pizza, 25% tacos and 65% chose something other than salad.)

questions.skill: Finding the percent from a part and a whole
questions.stem: Marco ran 10 miles last week and 8 miles this week. This week's distance is what percent of last week's distance?
questions.solution: Compare this week to last week (the whole): $\frac{8}{10} = \frac{80}{100}$, so this week's distance is 80% of last week's.

questions.skill: Finding the percent from a part and a whole
questions.stem: A choir has 60 singers. 21 of them are in grade 6 and 15 are in grade 7. The rest are in grade 8. What percent of the singers are in grade 8?
questions.solution: $60 - 21 - 15 = 24$ singers are in grade 8. $\frac{24}{60} = \frac{2}{5} = \frac{40}{100}$, so 40% are in grade 8.

questions.skill: Greatest common factor
questions.stem: What is the greatest common factor of 12 and 18?
questions.solution: Factors of 12: 1, 2, 3, 4, 6, 12. Factors of 18: 1, 2, 3, 6, 9, 18. The greatest factor in both lists is 6.

questions.skill: Least common multiple
questions.stem: What is the least common multiple of 4 and 6?
questions.solution: Multiples of 4: 4, 8, 12, 16, ... Multiples of 6: 6, 12, 18, ... The smallest number in both lists is 12.

questions.skill: Prime factorization in exponent form
questions.stem: Which is the prime factorization of 20 written with an exponent?
questions.solution: $20 = 2 \times 2 \times 5 = 2^2 \times 5$. The options $2 \times 10$ and $4 \times 5$ use numbers that are not prime, and $2 \times 5^2$ equals 50.

solve.work: 20 = 2 x 2 x 5 = 2^2 x 5. 4 x 5 and 2 x 10 are not prime factorizations; 2 x 5^2 = 50.

questions.skill: Greatest common factor of two numbers
questions.stem: The factors of 8 are 1, 2, 4 and 8. The factors of 12 are 1, 2, 3, 4, 6 and 12. What is the greatest factor that 8 and 12 share?
questions.solution: The factors in both lists are 1, 2 and 4. The greatest of them is 4.

questions.skill: Greatest common factor of two numbers
questions.stem: Which is the greatest common factor of 16 and 24?
questions.solution: The factors of 16 are 1, 2, 4, 8, 16 and the factors of 24 are 1, 2, 3, 4, 6, 8, 12, 24. The common factors are 1, 2, 4 and 8, and the greatest is 8. (4 and 2 are common factors but not the greatest, and 48 is a common multiple.)

questions.skill: Greatest common factor of two numbers
questions.stem: What is the largest number that divides evenly into both 9 and 27?
questions.solution: 9 divides evenly into 9 ($9 \div 9 = 1$) and into 27 ($27 \div 9 = 3$). No larger number divides 9 evenly, so the answer is 9.

questions.skill: Greatest common factor of two numbers
questions.stem: Find the greatest common factor of 20 and 30.
questions.solution: The factors of 20 are 1, 2, 4, 5, 10, 20. The factors of 30 are 1, 2, 3, 5, 6, 10, 15, 30. The common factors are 1, 2, 5 and 10, so the greatest is 10.

questions.skill: Greatest common factor in a problem
questions.stem: Mia has 8 red beads and 12 blue beads. She makes identical bracelets using all of the beads, with the same number of red beads and the same number of blue beads on each bracelet. What is the greatest number of bracelets she can make?
questions.solution: The number of bracelets must divide both 8 and 12, so it is a common factor. The greatest common factor of 8 and 12 is 4. With 4 bracelets, each has 2 red beads and 3 blue beads.

solve.work: Bracelets must divide 8 and 12; GCF = 4 (2 red, 3 blue each).

questions.skill: Greatest common factor in a problem
questions.stem: Two ribbons are 15 inches and 20 inches long. Dan cuts both ribbons into pieces that are all the same length, with no ribbon left over. What is the greatest possible length of each piece, in inches?
questions.solution: The piece length must divide both 15 and 20, so the greatest length is the greatest common factor, 5 inches. (3 divides only 15, 10 divides only 20, and 60 is a common multiple.)

questions.skill: Greatest common factor in a problem
questions.stem: A floor is 6 feet long and 9 feet wide. It is covered with square tiles that are all the same size, with no gaps and no cutting. What is the greatest possible side length of a tile, in feet?
questions.solution: The side length must divide both 6 and 9. The common factors are 1 and 3, so the greatest is 3 feet. (1 foot would work but is not the greatest, 2 does not divide 9, and 54 is $6 \times 9$.)

questions.skill: Least common multiple of two numbers
questions.stem: The first multiples of 3 are 3, 6, 9, 12, 15 and 18. The first multiples of 4 are 4, 8, 12, 16 and 20. What is the least number that is in both lists?
questions.solution: The only number in both lists is 12, so the least common multiple of 3 and 4 is 12.

questions.skill: Least common multiple of two numbers
questions.stem: Which is the least common multiple of 3 and 9?
questions.solution: 9 is a multiple of 3 ($3 \times 3 = 9$) and of 9, and no smaller number is a multiple of 9. So the least common multiple is 9. (27 and 18 are common multiples, but not the least. 3 is not a multiple of 9.)

solve.work: 9 is a multiple of 3, so LCM = 9.

questions.skill: Least common multiple of two numbers
questions.stem: What is the least common multiple of 6 and 8?
questions.solution: Multiples of 6: 6, 12, 18, 24, 30, ... Multiples of 8: 8, 16, 24, 32, ... The first one in both lists is 24. (48 is also a common multiple but not the least; 14 is the sum; 2 is the greatest common factor.)

questions.skill: Least common multiple of two numbers
questions.stem: Find the least common multiple of 2 and 7.
questions.solution: Multiples of 7: 7, 14, 21, ... The first one that is also a multiple of 2 is 14.

questions.skill: Least common multiple in a problem
questions.stem: Light A blinks every 2 seconds and light B blinks every 3 seconds. They just blinked together. In how many seconds will they next blink together?
questions.solution: Light A blinks at 2, 4, 6, ... seconds and light B at 3, 6, 9, ... seconds. The first time in both lists is 6 seconds.

questions.skill: Least common multiple in a problem
questions.stem: Paper cups come in packs of 4 and plates come in packs of 5. Pia wants exactly the same number of cups and plates. What is the least number of cups she can buy?
questions.solution: The number of cups is a multiple of 4 and of 5, so the least is the least common multiple of 4 and 5, which is 20 (5 packs of cups and 4 packs of plates).

solve.work: Cups multiple of 4, plates multiple of 5; least common = LCM(4, 5) = 20 cups.

questions.skill: Least common multiple in a problem
questions.stem: A drum is hit every 5 beats and a bell rings every 10 beats. At the start they sound together. After how many beats do they next sound together?
questions.solution: The drum sounds on beats 5, 10, 15, ... and the bell on beats 10, 20, ... The first beat in both is 10.

questions.skill: Prime factorization in exponent form
questions.stem: Which of these is a prime factor of 30?
questions.solution: A prime factor is a factor that is a prime number. 10, 6 and 15 are factors of 30, but each can be divided further ($10 = 2 \times 5$, $6 = 2 \times 3$, $15 = 3 \times 5$). Only 2 is prime.

solve.work: 30 = 2 x 3 x 5. Only 2 among the options is prime.

questions.skill: Prime factorization in exponent form
questions.stem: The prime factorization of 18 is written $2 \times 3^n$. What is $n$?
questions.solution: $18 = 2 \times 9 = 2 \times 3 \times 3 = 2 \times 3^2$, so $n = 2$.

questions.skill: Prime factorization in exponent form
questions.stem: Which shows 28 written as a product of prime numbers?
questions.solution: $2 \times 2 \times 7 = 28$ and 2 and 7 are both prime. The others use 4, 14, 1 or 28, which are not prime.

solve.work: 28 = 2 x 2 x 7, all prime. 14, 28 and 4 are not prime; 1 is not prime.

questions.skill: Prime factorization in exponent form
questions.stem: Ben splits 24 into 4 and 6 to start a factor tree. Then he splits 4 into 2 and 2, and 6 into 2 and 3. How many times does the prime 2 appear in the prime factorization of 24?
questions.solution: The primes at the ends of the tree are 2, 2, 2 and 3. The prime 2 appears 3 times, so $24 = 2^3 \times 3$.

solve.work: 24 = 2 x 2 x 2 x 3; the prime 2 appears 3 times.

questions.skill: Reading and evaluating exponent form
questions.stem: What is the value of $2^4$?
questions.solution: $2^4$ means 4 factors of 2: $2 \times 2 \times 2 \times 2 = 16$. (8 is $2 \times 4$, 6 is $2 + 4$, and 32 is five factors of 2.)

questions.skill: Reading and evaluating exponent form
questions.stem: Which expression is the same as $5^3$?
questions.solution: The exponent 3 tells how many times the base 5 is used as a factor, so $5^3 = 5 \times 5 \times 5$.

questions.skill: Reading and evaluating exponent form
questions.stem: What is the value of $2 \times 5^2$?
questions.solution: Work out the exponent first: $5^2 = 25$. Then $2 \times 25 = 50$.

questions.skill: Using prime factorizations to find the GCF or LCM
questions.stem: The prime factorizations of 6 and 15 are $6 = 2 \times 3$ and $15 = 3 \times 5$. Which prime number is a factor of both 6 and 15?
questions.solution: Compare the two lists of primes: 2 and 3 for 6, and 3 and 5 for 15. The only prime in both is 3.

questions.skill: Using prime factorizations to find the GCF or LCM
questions.stem: Since $14 = 2 \times 7$ and $35 = 5 \times 7$, what is the greatest common factor of 14 and 35?
questions.solution: The only prime they share is 7, so the greatest common factor is 7. (2 and 5 each belong to only one number, and 70 is the least common multiple.)

questions.skill: Factoring a sum with the distributive property
questions.stem: Which expression equals $6 + 9$ written as a common factor times a sum?
questions.solution: 3 is a factor of both 6 and 9: $6 = 3 \times 2$ and $9 = 3 \times 3$. So $6 + 9 = 3(2 + 3)$, which is $3 \times 5 = 15$. Check that the others do not equal 15: 33, 24 and 60.

questions.skill: Factoring a sum with the distributive property
questions.stem: What number makes this true? $8 + 12 = 4(2 + ?)$
questions.solution: $8 = 4 \times 2$ and $12 = 4 \times 3$, so $8 + 12 = 4(2 + 3)$. The missing number is 3.

questions.skill: Factoring a sum with the distributive property
questions.stem: You rewrite $10 + 15$ as the greatest common factor times a sum. What is the greatest common factor?
questions.solution: The factors of 10 are 1, 2, 5, 10 and the factors of 15 are 1, 3, 5, 15. The greatest common factor is 5, so $10 + 15 = 5(2 + 3)$.

questions.skill: Factoring a sum with the distributive property
questions.stem: Which sum is equal to $4(3 + 5)$?
questions.solution: The distributive property multiplies 4 by each number inside: $4 \times 3 + 4 \times 5 = 12 + 20 = 32$. The others equal 17, 16 and 19.

questions.skill: Relating factors and multiples
questions.stem: Which number is a multiple of both 3 and 4?
questions.solution: 12 is $3 \times 4$ and $4 \times 3$, so it is a multiple of both. 18 is a multiple of 3 only, 8 is a multiple of 4 only, and 7 is neither.

solve.work: 12 = 3 x 4 = 4 x 3. 8 not multiple of 3; 18 not of 4; 7 neither.

questions.skill: Relating factors and multiples
questions.stem: Which statement is true?
questions.solution: $30 = 6 \times 5$, so 6 is a factor of 30 (and 30 is a multiple of 6). The reverse statements are false, and 30 cannot be divided evenly by 12.

solve.work: 30 / 6 = 5, so 6 is a factor of 30. 12 does not divide 30; the others are reversed.

questions.skill: Relating factors and multiples
questions.stem: What is the smallest multiple of 7 that is greater than 30?
questions.solution: Multiples of 7: 7, 14, 21, 28, 35. 28 is less than 30 and 35 is the first that is greater, so the answer is 35.

questions.skill: Greatest common factor
questions.stem: What is the greatest common factor of 36 and 48?
questions.solution: $36 = 2^2 \times 3^2$ and $48 = 2^4 \times 3$. Both contain $2^2$ and $3$, so the greatest common factor is $2^2 \times 3 = 12$.

questions.skill: Least common multiple in context
questions.stem: A bus leaves a stop every 12 minutes and a tram leaves every 15 minutes. Both leave at 8:00 a.m. How many minutes later will they next leave at the same time?
questions.solution: The answer is the least common multiple of 12 and 15. Multiples of 15: 15, 30, 45, 60. Of these, 60 is the first that is also a multiple of 12 ($12 \times 5 = 60$). So they next leave together 60 minutes later.

questions.skill: Factoring a sum with the distributive property
questions.stem: Which expression shows $24 + 36$ rewritten as the greatest common factor times a sum?
questions.solution: The greatest common factor of 24 and 36 is 12. Divide each number by 12: $24 \div 12 = 2$ and $36 \div 12 = 3$. So $24 + 36 = 12(2 + 3)$. Check: $12 \times 5 = 60$ and $24 + 36 = 60$.

solve.work: GCF(24, 36) = 12. 24 + 36 = 12(2 + 3) = 60. 6(4 + 5) also equals 60 but 6 is not the GCF; others do not equal 60.

questions.skill: Greatest common factor of two numbers
questions.stem: What is the largest number that divides evenly into both 45 and 60?
questions.solution: Factors of 45: 1, 3, 5, 9, 15, 45. Factors of 60: 1, 2, 3, 4, 5, 6, 10, 12, 15, 20, 30, 60. The greatest one in both lists is 15.

questions.skill: Greatest common factor of two numbers
questions.stem: Which pair of numbers has a greatest common factor of 6?
questions.solution: The greatest common factor of 12 and 18 is 6. The other pairs have greatest common factors of 12, 3 and 5.

questions.skill: Greatest common factor of two numbers
questions.stem: Find the greatest common factor of 32 and 56.
questions.solution: Factors of 32: 1, 2, 4, 8, 16, 32. Factors of 56: 1, 2, 4, 7, 8, 14, 28, 56. The greatest one in both lists is 8.

questions.skill: Greatest common factor in a problem
questions.stem: A floor is 14 feet long and 21 feet wide. It will be covered with square tiles that are all the same size, with no gaps and no cutting. What is the greatest possible side length of a tile, in feet?
questions.solution: The side length must divide both 14 and 21. The greatest common factor of 14 and 21 is 7, so the tiles are 7 feet on a side.

questions.skill: Greatest common factor in a problem
questions.stem: Lena has 36 red stickers and 54 blue stickers. She makes equal groups using all of the stickers, with the same number of red stickers and the same number of blue stickers in every group. What is the greatest number of groups she can make?
questions.solution: The number of groups must divide both 36 and 54, so the greatest is their greatest common factor. $36 = 2^2 \times 3^2$ and $54 = 2 \times 3^3$, so the GCF is $2 \times 3^2 = 18$. (9 and 6 are smaller common factors, and 90 is the sum.)

solve.work: 36 = 2^2 x 3^2, 54 = 2 x 3^3. GCF = 18 groups (2 red, 3 blue each).

questions.skill: Greatest common factor in a problem
questions.stem: A club has 40 sixth graders and 64 seventh graders. The club forms teams so that each team has the same number of sixth graders and the same number of seventh graders, and everyone is on a team. What is the greatest number of teams?
questions.solution: The number of teams must divide both 40 and 64. The greatest common factor of 40 and 64 is 8, so there are 8 teams, each with 5 sixth graders and 8 seventh graders.

questions.skill: Least common multiple of two numbers
questions.stem: What is the smallest number that is a multiple of both 9 and 12?
questions.solution: Multiples of 12: 12, 24, 36, ... Multiples of 9: 9, 18, 27, 36, ... The first number in both lists is 36.

questions.skill: Least common multiple of two numbers
questions.stem: Which is the least common multiple of 6 and 10?
questions.solution: Multiples of 10: 10, 20, 30, ... The first one that is also a multiple of 6 is 30. (60 is a common multiple but not the least, 16 is the sum, and 2 is the greatest common factor.)

questions.skill: Least common multiple of two numbers
questions.stem: Find the least common multiple of 7 and 9.
questions.solution: 7 and 9 have no common factor other than 1, so their least common multiple is their product: $7 \times 9 = 63$.

questions.skill: Least common multiple in a problem
questions.stem: Hot dogs come in packs of 10 and buns come in packs of 8. What is the least number of hot dogs Mr. Lee can buy to have exactly the same number of hot dogs and buns?
questions.solution: The number must be a multiple of 10 and of 8. The multiples of 10 are 10, 20, 30, 40 and the first that is also a multiple of 8 is 40 (4 packs of hot dogs and 5 packs of buns).

solve.work: LCM(10, 8) = 40 hot dogs (4 packs hot dogs, 5 packs buns).

questions.skill: Least common multiple in a problem
questions.stem: Two runners start together at the start line of a loop. Rani runs one lap in 6 minutes and Ty runs one lap in 9 minutes. After how many minutes will they next be together at the start line?
questions.solution: They are together at the start line at times that are multiples of 6 and of 9. The least common multiple of 6 and 9 is 18 minutes. (54 is the product, 3 is the greatest common factor, and 15 is the sum.)

questions.skill: Least common multiple in a problem
questions.stem: Sam waters his plants every 4 days and cleans the fish tank every 10 days. He did both today. In how many days will he next do both on the same day?
questions.solution: The days he waters are multiples of 4 and the days he cleans are multiples of 10. The least common multiple of 4 and 10 is 20 days.

questions.skill: Prime factorization in exponent form
questions.stem: Carlos writes 36 as a product of primes in exponent form. Which is his answer?
questions.solution: $36 = 2 \times 2 \times 3 \times 3 = 2^2 \times 3^2$. The expression $2^2 \times 9$ uses 9 and $6^2$ uses 6, which are not prime, and $2 \times 3^3 = 54$.

solve.work: 36 = 2 x 2 x 3 x 3 = 2^2 x 3^2. 6 and 9 are not prime; 2 x 3^3 = 54.

questions.skill: Prime factorization in exponent form
questions.stem: The prime factorization of 40 is $2^a \times 5$. What is the value of $a$?
questions.solution: $40 = 2 \times 2 \times 2 \times 5 = 2^3 \times 5$, so $a = 3$.

questions.skill: Prime factorization in exponent form
questions.stem: Which shows the prime factorization of 60?
questions.solution: $60 = 2 \times 2 \times 3 \times 5 = 2^2 \times 3 \times 5$. The other products equal 60 too, but they use 10, 4 or 15, which are not prime.

solve.work: 60 = 2^2 x 3 x 5. Others contain 15, 4 or 10, not prime.

questions.skill: Prime factorization in exponent form
questions.stem: How many different prime numbers appear in the prime factorization of 90?
questions.solution: $90 = 2 \times 3 \times 3 \times 5 = 2 \times 3^2 \times 5$. The different primes are 2, 3 and 5, so the answer is 3.

questions.skill: Reading and evaluating exponent form
questions.stem: Evaluate $2^3 \times 3^2$.

questions.skill: Reading and evaluating exponent form
questions.stem: Which number is equal to $2^3 \times 5$?
questions.solution: $2^3 = 2 \times 2 \times 2 = 8$, so $2^3 \times 5 = 8 \times 5 = 40$. (30 treats $2^3$ as $2 \times 3$, 250 is $2 \times 5^3$, and 13 is $8 + 5$.)

questions.skill: Reading and evaluating exponent form
questions.stem: Which comparison of $2^5$ and $5^2$ is true?
questions.solution: $2^5 = 2 \times 2 \times 2 \times 2 \times 2 = 32$ and $5^2 = 5 \times 5 = 25$. So $2^5$ is greater. Swapping the base and the exponent changes the value.

questions.skill: Using prime factorizations to find the GCF or LCM
questions.stem: $24 = 2^3 \times 3$ and $60 = 2^2 \times 3 \times 5$. Use these prime factorizations to find the greatest common factor of 24 and 60.
questions.solution: Take each shared prime to the smaller power: $2^2$ (smaller of $2^3$ and $2^2$) and $3$. The greatest common factor is $2^2 \times 3 = 12$.

solve.work: Shared primes with lowest powers: 2^2 x 3 = 12.

questions.skill: Using prime factorizations to find the GCF or LCM
questions.stem: $12 = 2^2 \times 3$ and $18 = 2 \times 3^2$. Which is the least common multiple of 12 and 18?
questions.solution: For the least common multiple, take each prime to the larger power: $2^2$ and $3^2$. So the LCM is $2^2 \times 3^2 = 4 \times 9 = 36$. (6 is the greatest common factor and 216 is the product.)

questions.skill: Using prime factorizations to find the GCF or LCM
questions.stem: Which is the greatest common factor of $2^3 \times 5$ and $2^2 \times 5^2$?
questions.solution: For the greatest common factor, take each shared prime to the smaller power: $2^2$ (smaller of $2^3$ and $2^2$) and $5$ (smaller of $5^1$ and $5^2$). So the GCF is $2^2 \times 5 = 20$. ($2^3 \times 5^2$ is the least common multiple.)

solve.work: Lowest powers of shared primes: 2^2 x 5 (= 20; numbers are 40 and 100).

questions.skill: Factoring a sum with the distributive property
questions.stem: Use the distributive property to rewrite $32 + 48$ as a product with the greatest common factor. Which is correct?
questions.solution: The greatest common factor of 32 and 48 is 16, so $32 + 48 = 16(2 + 3)$ because $32 = 16 \times 2$ and $48 = 16 \times 3$. The expressions with 8 and 4 are equal to the sum but do not use the greatest common factor, and $16(2 + 4) = 96$.

questions.skill: Factoring a sum with the distributive property
questions.stem: What number makes this true? $42 + 63 = 21(2 + ?)$
questions.solution: $42 = 21 \times 2$ and $63 = 21 \times 3$, so the missing number is 3.

questions.skill: Factoring a sum with the distributive property
questions.stem: The greatest common factor of 54 and 81 is 27, so $54 + 81 = 27(a + b)$. What is the value of $a + b$?

questions.skill: Factoring a sum with the distributive property
questions.stem: Which sum is equal to $9(4 + 7)$?
questions.solution: The distributive property gives $9(4 + 7) = 9 \times 4 + 9 \times 7 = 36 + 63 = 99$. The others equal 43, 29 and 67.

questions.skill: Factoring a sum with the distributive property
questions.stem: Use the distributive property to find the value of $12 \times 7 + 12 \times 3$.
questions.solution: Both products have the factor 12, so $12 \times 7 + 12 \times 3 = 12(7 + 3) = 12 \times 10 = 120$.

questions.skill: Relating factors and multiples
questions.stem: Which number is a factor of 48 but is NOT a multiple of 4?
questions.solution: All four numbers divide 48 evenly. 8, 12 and 16 are multiples of 4 ($8 = 4 \times 2$, $12 = 4 \times 3$, $16 = 4 \times 4$), but 6 is not.

solve.work: All four divide 48. 16, 12, 8 are multiples of 4; 6 is not.

questions.skill: Relating factors and multiples
questions.stem: How many multiples of 6 are between 1 and 50?
questions.solution: The multiples of 6 are 6, 12, 18, 24, 30, 36, 42, 48. The next one, 54, is more than 50. That is 8 multiples.

solve.work: 6, 12, 18, 24, 30, 36, 42, 48 -> 8 (endpoints 1 and 50 are not multiples, so inclusive/exclusive does not matter).

questions.skill: Relating factors and multiples
questions.stem: Which number is a multiple of both 6 and 9 and is less than 30?
questions.solution: 18 is $6 \times 3$ and $9 \times 2$, so it is a multiple of both. 12 is a multiple of 6 only, 27 is a multiple of 9 only, and 15 is neither.

solve.work: Common multiples of 6 and 9 are multiples of 18; under 30 only 18. 12 not multiple of 9; 15, 27 not multiples of 6.

questions.skill: Greatest common factor in a problem
questions.stem: Ms. Cruz has 84 pencils and 126 erasers. She makes identical supply packs that use all of the pencils and all of the erasers. What is the greatest number of packs she can make?
questions.solution: The number of packs must divide both 84 and 126, so it is their greatest common factor. $84 = 2^2 \times 3 \times 7$ and $126 = 2 \times 3^2 \times 7$. The shared factors are $2 \times 3 \times 7 = 42$, so she can make 42 packs.

solve.work: 84 = 2^2 x 3 x 7, 126 = 2 x 3^2 x 7. GCF = 2 x 3 x 7 = 42 packs (2 pencils and 3 erasers each).

questions.skill: Prime factorization in exponent form
questions.stem: Which is the prime factorization of 72 written with exponents?
questions.solution: $72 = 8 \times 9 = 2^3 \times 3^2$. The option $2^3 \times 3$ equals 24, $2^2 \times 3^3$ equals 108, and $2^3 \times 9$ uses 9, which is not prime.

questions.skill: Value of a number written in exponent form
questions.stem: A number's prime factorization is $2^3 \times 3 \times 5^2$. What is the number?
questions.solution: $2^3 = 8$ and $5^2 = 25$, so the number is $8 \times 3 \times 25 = 600$.

questions.skill: Greatest common factor of two numbers
questions.stem: What is the greatest common factor of 84 and 108?
questions.solution: $84 = 2^2 \times 3 \times 7$ and $108 = 2^2 \times 3^3$. The shared primes are $2^2$ and $3$, so the GCF is $2^2 \times 3 = 12$.

questions.skill: Greatest common factor of two numbers
questions.stem: The greatest common factor of two numbers is 9. One of the numbers is 63. Which could be the other number?
questions.solution: $63 = 9 \times 7$ and $45 = 9 \times 5$, and 7 and 5 share no factor other than 1, so the GCF of 63 and 45 is 9. The greatest common factors of 63 with 42, 21 and 35 are 21, 21 and 7.

questions.skill: Greatest common factor of two numbers
questions.stem: The greatest common factor of a number and 36 is 12. The number is greater than 20 and less than 40. What is the number?
questions.solution: The number must be a multiple of 12, and the multiples of 12 between 20 and 40 are 24 and 36. The GCF of 36 and 36 is 36, not 12, but the GCF of 24 and 36 is 12. So the number is 24.

solve.work: The number is a multiple of 12 between 20 and 40: 24 or 36. GCF(24, 36) = 12; GCF(36, 36) = 36. Answer 24.

questions.skill: Greatest common factor in a problem
questions.stem: A bakery has 48 muffins and 72 cookies to pack into identical boxes with nothing left over. Every box has the same number of muffins and the same number of cookies. The bakery makes as many boxes as possible. How many muffins and cookies are in each box altogether?
questions.solution: The most boxes is the greatest common factor of 48 and 72, which is 24. Each box has $48 \div 24 = 2$ muffins and $72 \div 24 = 3$ cookies, which is $2 + 3 = 5$ items. (24 is the number of boxes.)

questions.skill: Greatest common factor in a problem
questions.stem: A sheet of paper is 84 centimeters long and 60 centimeters wide. It is cut into squares that are all the same size, with no paper left over. The squares are as large as possible. How many squares are there?
questions.solution: The side of the largest square is the greatest common factor of 84 and 60, which is 12 centimeters. Along the length there are $84 \div 12 = 7$ squares, and along the width $60 \div 12 = 5$. In all there are $7 \times 5 = 35$ squares.

questions.skill: Greatest common factor in a problem
questions.stem: Mara has 56 candies and 42 stickers. She makes as many identical gift bags as she can, using every candy and every sticker, with the same number of each in every bag. How many candies are in each bag?
questions.solution: The most bags is the greatest common factor of 56 and 42, which is 14. Each bag then has $56 \div 14 = 4$ candies (and $42 \div 14 = 3$ stickers). (14 is the number of bags.)

questions.skill: Least common multiple of two numbers
questions.stem: Find the least common multiple of 11 and 12.
questions.solution: 11 and 12 have no common factor other than 1, so their least common multiple is their product: $11 \times 12 = 132$.

questions.skill: Least common multiple of two numbers
questions.stem: Which is the least common multiple of 10 and 12?
questions.solution: $10 = 2 \times 5$ and $12 = 2^2 \times 3$. Take each prime to the larger power: $2^2 \times 3 \times 5 = 60$. (120 is the product, 22 is the sum, and 2 is the greatest common factor.)

questions.skill: Least common multiple of two numbers
questions.stem: The least common multiple of 6 and another whole number is 30. The other number is greater than 1 and less than 10. What is the other number?
questions.solution: Check the numbers from 2 to 9: the least common multiples with 6 are 6, 6, 12, 30, 6, 42, 24, 18. Only 5 gives 30.

solve.work: The other number must divide 30 and contain the factor 5: 5, 10, 15, 30. Between 1 and 10 only 5. LCM(6, 5) = 30.

questions.skill: Least common multiple in a problem
questions.stem: A red light flashes every 4 seconds, a blue light every 6 seconds and a green light every 10 seconds. All three flash together now. In how many seconds will all three next flash together?
questions.solution: The answer is the least common multiple of 4, 6 and 10. $4 = 2^2$, $6 = 2 \times 3$ and $10 = 2 \times 5$, so the LCM is $2^2 \times 3 \times 5 = 60$. (30 is not a multiple of 4, 120 is a common multiple but not the least, and 240 is the product.)

questions.skill: Least common multiple in a problem
questions.stem: One row of a wall is built from bricks that are 15 centimeters long, and another row from blocks that are 20 centimeters long. Both rows start at the same left edge. What is the shortest length of wall, in centimeters, at which both rows end together?
questions.solution: The length must be a multiple of 15 and of 20. The least common multiple of 15 and 20 is 60 centimeters (4 bricks and 3 blocks). (300 is the product, 5 is the greatest common factor, and 35 is the sum.)

questions.skill: Least common multiple in a problem
questions.stem: Notebooks come in packs of 6 and pens come in packs of 8. Ms. Park wants exactly the same number of notebooks and pens, and she buys as few as possible. How many packs does she buy altogether?
questions.solution: The least number of each is the least common multiple of 6 and 8, which is 24. That is $24 \div 6 = 4$ packs of notebooks and $24 \div 8 = 3$ packs of pens, so $4 + 3 = 7$ packs.

solve.work: LCM(6, 8) = 24 of each: 24/6 = 4 notebook packs, 24/8 = 3 pen packs; 7 packs.

questions.skill: Least common multiple in a problem
questions.stem: Two cyclists start together at the same point on a circular track. One cyclist takes 8 minutes for each lap and the other takes 12 minutes. How many laps has the faster cyclist ridden when they next meet at the starting point?
questions.solution: They meet again after the least common multiple of 8 and 12 minutes, which is 24 minutes. The faster cyclist, at 8 minutes a lap, has ridden $24 \div 8 = 3$ laps (and the other has ridden 2).

solve.work: LCM(8, 12) = 24 minutes. Faster (8 min/lap) has ridden 24/8 = 3 laps.

questions.skill: Prime factorization in exponent form
questions.stem: Which is the prime factorization of 180 written with exponents?
questions.solution: $180 = 2 \times 90 = 2 \times 2 \times 45 = 2 \times 2 \times 3 \times 3 \times 5 = 2^2 \times 3^2 \times 5$. The other expressions equal 300, 450 and 120.

questions.skill: Prime factorization in exponent form
questions.stem: The prime factorization of 200 is $2^a \times 5^b$. What is the value of $a + b$?
questions.solution: $200 = 2 \times 100 = 2 \times 2 \times 50 = 2 \times 2 \times 2 \times 25 = 2^3 \times 5^2$. So $a = 3$, $b = 2$ and $a + b = 5$.

questions.skill: Prime factorization in exponent form
questions.stem: The prime factorization of 144 is written in exponent form. If it were written as a product of primes with no exponents, how many prime numbers would be multiplied? Count a repeated prime each time it appears.
questions.solution: $144 = 12 \times 12 = (2 \times 2 \times 3) \times (2 \times 2 \times 3) = 2^4 \times 3^2$. Without exponents that is $2 \times 2 \times 2 \times 2 \times 3 \times 3$, which has $4 + 2 = 6$ primes.

questions.skill: Reading and evaluating exponent form
questions.stem: One number is $2^4 \times 7$ and another number is $2^2 \times 7$. How many times as large as the second number is the first number?
questions.solution: The first number is $16 \times 7 = 112$ and the second is $4 \times 7 = 28$. Then $112 \div 28 = 4$. (The factor 7 is in both, and $2^4 \div 2^2 = 2^2 = 4$.)

questions.skill: Reading and evaluating exponent form
questions.stem: Which of these numbers is the greatest?

solve.issues: Minor: comparing powers tests exponents more than factors and multiples; only loosely aligned.

questions.skill: Using prime factorizations to find the GCF or LCM
questions.stem: $2^3 \times 3 \times 5$ and $2^2 \times 3^2 \times 7$ are the prime factorizations of two numbers. What is the greatest common factor of the two numbers?
questions.solution: Take each prime that appears in both to its smaller power: $2^2$ and $3$ (the 5 and the 7 are in only one number). The GCF is $2^2 \times 3 = 12$.

solve.work: Shared primes, lowest powers: 2^2 x 3 = 12. (120 and 252.)

questions.skill: Using prime factorizations to find the GCF or LCM
questions.stem: The prime factorizations of two numbers are $2^3 \times 3^2$ and $2^2 \times 3 \times 5$. Which is the least common multiple of the two numbers?
questions.solution: For the least common multiple, use every prime that appears, each to its larger power: $2^3$, $3^2$ and $5$. So the LCM is $2^3 \times 3^2 \times 5 = 360$. ($2^2 \times 3$ is the greatest common factor and $2^5 \times 3^3 \times 5$ is the product.)

questions.skill: Using prime factorizations to find the GCF or LCM
questions.stem: $60 = 2^2 \times 3 \times 5$ and $84 = 2^2 \times 3 \times 7$. Use these prime factorizations to find the least common multiple of 60 and 84.
questions.solution: Use every prime that appears, each to its larger power: $2^2$, $3$, $5$ and $7$. The LCM is $2^2 \times 3 \times 5 \times 7 = 4 \times 105 = 420$.

questions.skill: Using prime factorizations to find the GCF or LCM
questions.stem: Maria says that the greatest common factor of $2^2 \times 5^2$ and $2^3 \times 5$ is $2^3 \times 5^2$. Which statement is correct?
choices: She is correct; the GCF is $2^3 \times 5^2$
She found the least common multiple; the GCF is $2^3 \times 5$
She found the least common multiple; the GCF is $2 \times 5$
She found the least common multiple; the GCF is $2^2 \times 5$
questions.answer: She found the least common multiple; the GCF is $2^2 \times 5$
questions.solution: The greatest common factor uses the smaller power of each shared prime: $2^2$ and $5^1$, so the GCF is $2^2 \times 5 = 20$. Maria used the larger powers, which gives the least common multiple, $2^3 \times 5^2 = 200$.

solve.answer: She found the least common multiple; the GCF is $2^2 \times 5$
solve.work: 2^3 x 5^2 takes highest powers, the LCM (200). GCF takes lowest: 2^2 x 5 = 20.

questions.skill: Factoring a sum with the distributive property
questions.stem: What is the greatest common factor that can be pulled out of $72 + 96$?
questions.solution: The greatest common factor of 72 and 96 is 24, because $72 = 24 \times 3$ and $96 = 24 \times 4$. So $72 + 96 = 24(3 + 4)$.

questions.skill: Factoring a sum with the distributive property
questions.stem: Which sum has no common factor greater than 1 that can be pulled out?
questions.solution: 15 and 28 share only the factor 1. The other pairs share 7, 9 and 8, so $14 + 21 = 7(2 + 3)$, $18 + 27 = 9(2 + 3)$ and $16 + 40 = 8(2 + 5)$.

questions.skill: Factoring a sum with the distributive property
questions.stem: Which expression has the same value as $17 \times 6 + 17 \times 4$?
questions.solution: Both products have the factor 17, so $17 \times 6 + 17 \times 4 = 17(6 + 4) = 17 \times 10$. ($17 \times 24$ multiplies 6 and 4, and the other two change the 17 or subtract.)

questions.skill: Factoring a sum with the distributive property
questions.stem: Which equation is true?
questions.solution: $45 = 15 \times 3$ and $60 = 15 \times 4$, so $45 + 60 = 15(3 + 4) = 105$. The others work out to 135, 95 and 49.

questions.skill: Relating factors and multiples
questions.stem: How many of the whole numbers from 2 to 9 are factors of 72?
questions.solution: 72 divides evenly by 2, 3, 4, 6, 8 and 9 ($72 \div 2 = 36$, $\div 3 = 24$, $\div 4 = 18$, $\div 6 = 12$, $\div 8 = 9$, $\div 9 = 8$). It does not divide evenly by 5 or 7. So 6 of the numbers are factors.

solve.work: 72 = 2^3 x 3^2. From 2-9: 2, 3, 4, 6, 8, 9 divide 72; 5, 7 do not. 6 numbers.

questions.skill: Relating factors and multiples
questions.stem: The number 14 is a factor of a whole number $n$. Which of these must also be a factor of $n$?
questions.solution: Since $14 = 7 \times 2$, any multiple of 14 is also a multiple of 7. If $n = 14$, then 7 is a factor of $n$ but 28, 4 and 21 are not, so only 7 must be a factor.

solve.work: 14 | n means 7 | n (7 divides 14). n = 14 shows 4, 21, 28 need not be factors.

questions.skill: Relating factors and multiples
questions.stem: A whole number is a multiple of 12 and is also a factor of 60. It is greater than 12. What is the number?
questions.solution: The factors of 60 are 1, 2, 3, 4, 5, 6, 10, 12, 15, 20, 30 and 60. Of these, the multiples of 12 are 12 and 60, so the number greater than 12 is 60.

solve.work: Multiples of 12 above 12: 24, 36, 48, 60. Of these only 60 divides 60.

questions.skill: Relating factors and multiples
questions.stem: Which number has exactly three factors?
questions.solution: The factors of 9 are 1, 3 and 9 (three). The factors of 8 are 1, 2, 4, 8 (four), of 10 are 1, 2, 5, 10 (four) and of 12 are 1, 2, 3, 4, 6, 12 (six).

questions.skill: Adding fractions with unlike denominators
questions.stem: What is $\frac{2}{3} + \frac{1}{6}$?
questions.solution: Write $\frac{2}{3}$ as $\frac{4}{6}$. Then $\frac{4}{6} + \frac{1}{6} = \frac{5}{6}$.

questions.skill: Multiplying fractions
questions.stem: What is $\frac{3}{4} \times \frac{2}{5}$?
questions.solution: Multiply the numerators and the denominators: $\frac{3 \times 2}{4 \times 5} = \frac{6}{20} = \frac{3}{10}$.

questions.skill: Checking reasonableness by estimating
questions.stem: Rounding each mixed number to the nearest whole number, which is the best estimate of $4\frac{7}{8} + 2\frac{1}{9}$?
questions.solution: $4\frac{7}{8}$ is close to 5 and $2\frac{1}{9}$ is close to 2, so the sum is about $5 + 2 = 7$. Dropping the fractions gives 6, which is too low, and 8 and 12 are too high.

solve.work: 4 7/8 rounds to 5; 2 1/9 rounds to 2. 5 + 2 = 7 (exact sum about 6.99).

questions.skill: Adding fractions and mixed numbers
questions.stem: What is $\frac{1}{4} + \frac{3}{8}$?
questions.solution: Rewrite $\frac{1}{4}$ as $\frac{2}{8}$. Then $\frac{2}{8} + \frac{3}{8} = \frac{5}{8}$.

questions.skill: Adding fractions and mixed numbers
questions.stem: What is the sum of $\frac{1}{2}$ and $\frac{1}{3}$?
questions.solution: Use sixths: $\frac{1}{2} = \frac{3}{6}$ and $\frac{1}{3} = \frac{2}{6}$. Then $\frac{3}{6} + \frac{2}{6} = \frac{5}{6}$. Adding the tops and the bottoms (to get $\frac{2}{5}$) is a common mistake.

questions.skill: Adding fractions and mixed numbers
questions.stem: What is $1\frac{1}{2} + 2\frac{1}{4}$?
questions.solution: Add the whole numbers: 1 + 2 = 3. Add the fractions: $\frac{1}{2} + \frac{1}{4} = \frac{2}{4} + \frac{1}{4} = \frac{3}{4}$. The sum is $3\frac{3}{4}$.

questions.skill: Adding fractions and mixed numbers
questions.stem: Add $\frac{3}{10} + \frac{1}{5}$. Which is the sum?
questions.solution: Write $\frac{1}{5}$ as $\frac{2}{10}$. Then $\frac{3}{10} + \frac{2}{10} = \frac{5}{10}$, which is $\frac{1}{2}$.

questions.skill: Subtracting fractions and mixed numbers
questions.stem: What is $\frac{7}{8} - \frac{1}{4}$?
questions.solution: Write $\frac{1}{4}$ as $\frac{2}{8}$. Then $\frac{7}{8} - \frac{2}{8} = \frac{5}{8}$.

questions.skill: Subtracting fractions and mixed numbers
questions.stem: Subtract: $\frac{2}{3} - \frac{1}{6}$. Which is the difference?
questions.solution: Write $\frac{2}{3}$ as $\frac{4}{6}$. Then $\frac{4}{6} - \frac{1}{6} = \frac{3}{6}$, which is $\frac{1}{2}$.

questions.skill: Subtracting fractions and mixed numbers
questions.stem: Subtract $1\frac{1}{4}$ from $3\frac{3}{4}$. What is the difference?
questions.solution: Subtract the whole numbers: 3 - 1 = 2. Subtract the fractions: $\frac{3}{4} - \frac{1}{4} = \frac{2}{4} = \frac{1}{2}$. The difference is $2\frac{1}{2}$.

questions.skill: Multiplying fractions
questions.stem: Find the product of $\frac{1}{2}$ and $\frac{3}{5}$.
questions.solution: Multiply the tops: 1 x 3 = 3. Multiply the bottoms: 2 x 5 = 10. The product is $\frac{3}{10}$.

questions.skill: Multiplying fractions
questions.stem: Find $\frac{2}{3}$ of 12.
questions.solution: One third of 12 is 4, so $\frac{2}{3}$ of 12 is 4 x 2 = 8.

questions.skill: Multiplying fractions
questions.stem: What is $\frac{3}{4} \times \frac{8}{9}$?
questions.solution: Multiply the tops (3 x 8 = 24) and the bottoms (4 x 9 = 36): $\frac{24}{36}$. Divide both by 12 to get $\frac{2}{3}$.

questions.skill: Multiplying mixed numbers
questions.stem: Multiply: $1\frac{1}{2} \times 4$.
questions.solution: $1\frac{1}{2}$ is $\frac{3}{2}$. Then $\frac{3}{2} \times 4 = \frac{12}{2} = 6$. Or: 4 groups of 1 is 4, and 4 halves is 2, so 6.

questions.skill: Dividing a whole number by a fraction
questions.stem: Mr. Lee has 4 pounds of rice and puts $\frac{1}{2}$ pound in each bag. How many bags can he fill?
questions.solution: Each pound fills 2 bags, so 4 pounds fill 4 x 2 = 8 bags. In symbols, $4 \div \frac{1}{2} = 8$.

questions.skill: Dividing a whole number by a fraction
questions.stem: Divide: $6 \div \frac{1}{3}$.
questions.solution: There are 3 thirds in each whole, so 6 wholes hold 6 x 3 = 18 thirds. So $6 \div \frac{1}{3} = 18$.

questions.skill: Dividing a whole number by a fraction
questions.stem: A tank has 5 liters of juice. How many $\frac{1}{3}$-liter cups can be filled from it?
questions.solution: Each liter fills 3 cups, so 5 liters fill 5 x 3 = 15 cups. That is $5 \div \frac{1}{3} = 15$.

questions.skill: Dividing a fraction by a whole number
questions.stem: What is $\frac{6}{7} \div 3$?
questions.solution: Share 6 sevenths into 3 equal groups: 2 sevenths in each group. So $\frac{6}{7} \div 3 = \frac{2}{7}$.

questions.skill: Dividing a fraction by a whole number
questions.stem: Divide $\frac{1}{2}$ by 4. Which is the quotient?
questions.solution: Cut one half into 4 equal parts. Each part is $\frac{1}{8}$ of the whole, so $\frac{1}{2} \div 4 = \frac{1}{8}$. Multiplying by 4 gives 2, which is a mistake.

questions.skill: Dividing a fraction by a fraction
questions.stem: Find the quotient: $\frac{2}{3} \div \frac{1}{6}$.
questions.solution: $\frac{2}{3} = \frac{4}{6}$. There are 4 sixths in 4 sixths, so the answer is 4: $\frac{2}{3} \div \frac{1}{6} = 4$.

questions.skill: Dividing a fraction by a fraction
questions.stem: Which is the quotient $\frac{1}{2} \div \frac{1}{8}$?
questions.solution: $\frac{1}{2} = \frac{4}{8}$, and there are 4 eighths in 4 eighths. So $\frac{1}{2} \div \frac{1}{8} = 4$.

questions.skill: Interpreting a quotient
questions.stem: Dev has 2 pounds of nuts and puts $\frac{1}{4}$ pound in each bag. Which expression shows how many bags he can fill?
questions.solution: The number of bags is how many $\frac{1}{4}$s fit in 2, which is $2 \div \frac{1}{4}$. (It equals 8 bags.)

solve.work: How many 1/4-pound groups are in 2 pounds: 2 / (1/4) (= 8).

questions.skill: Interpreting a quotient
questions.stem: Leo has $\frac{3}{4}$ of a pie and shares it equally among 3 people. Which expression gives each person's share?
questions.solution: Sharing equally among 3 people means dividing by 3, so each share is $\frac{3}{4} \div 3$ (which is $\frac{1}{4}$ of the pie).

questions.skill: Interpreting a quotient
questions.stem: Think about $6 \div \frac{1}{2}$. Which statement is true?
choices: The answer is less than 6, because halves are smaller than wholes
The answer is 3, because half of 6 is 3
The answer is greater than 6, because each whole holds 2 halves
The answer is 6, because the top number of $\frac{1}{2}$ is 1
questions.answer: The answer is greater than 6, because each whole holds 2 halves
questions.solution: Each whole holds 2 halves, so 6 wholes hold 12 halves. $6 \div \frac{1}{2} = 12$, which is greater than 6.

solve.answer: The answer is greater than 6, because each whole holds 2 halves
solve.work: 6 / (1/2) = 12, which is greater than 6 because each whole contains 2 halves. The other statements give 6, 3, or 'less than 6', all false.

questions.skill: One-step fraction word problem
questions.stem: Sara walked $\frac{3}{4}$ mile in the morning and $\frac{1}{2}$ mile in the afternoon. How many miles did she walk in all?
questions.solution: $\frac{3}{4} + \frac{2}{4} = \frac{5}{4}$, which is $1\frac{1}{4}$ miles.

questions.skill: One-step fraction word problem
questions.stem: A ribbon is $\frac{5}{6}$ meter long. Tom cuts off $\frac{1}{3}$ meter. How many meters of ribbon are left?

questions.skill: One-step fraction word problem
questions.stem: A pan holds $\frac{3}{4}$ liter of water when it is full. Nia fills $\frac{1}{3}$ of the pan. How many liters of water are in the pan?
questions.solution: "$\frac{1}{3}$ of" the pan means multiply: $\frac{3}{4} \times \frac{1}{3} = \frac{3}{12} = \frac{1}{4}$.

questions.skill: One-step fraction word problem
questions.stem: One serving of soup is $\frac{3}{4}$ cup. How many cups of soup are in 4 servings?
questions.solution: 4 servings of $\frac{3}{4}$ cup: $4 \times \frac{3}{4} = \frac{12}{4} = 3$ cups.

questions.skill: Checking reasonableness by estimating
questions.stem: Which number is closest to the value of $\frac{7}{8} + \frac{11}{12}$?
questions.solution: $\frac{7}{8}$ is close to 1 and $\frac{11}{12}$ is close to 1, so the sum is close to 1 + 1 = 2.

solve.work: Each fraction is close to 1, so the sum is close to 2. Exactly: 21/24 + 22/24 = 43/24 = about 1.79, nearest option 2.

questions.skill: Checking reasonableness by estimating
questions.stem: Which is the best estimate of $5\frac{1}{8} - 2\frac{7}{8}$?
questions.solution: $5\frac{1}{8}$ is about 5 and $2\frac{7}{8}$ is about 3. Then 5 - 3 = 2.

solve.work: 5 1/8 is about 5, 2 7/8 is about 3; 5 - 3 = 2. Exact: 2 1/4, nearest option 2.

questions.skill: Checking reasonableness by estimating
questions.stem: Without multiplying, which product is greater than 6?
questions.solution: Multiplying 6 by a number less than 1 gives less than 6. Only $1\frac{1}{4}$ is greater than 1, so $6 \times 1\frac{1}{4}$ is greater than 6.

solve.work: Multiplying 6 by a number greater than 1 gives more than 6; only 1 1/4 is greater than 1 (5/8, 1/2, 3/4 are less than 1).

questions.skill: Finding a missing number in a fraction equation
questions.stem: What is the value of n in $n + \frac{1}{6} = \frac{5}{6}$?
questions.solution: Take $\frac{1}{6}$ away from $\frac{5}{6}$: $n = \frac{5}{6} - \frac{1}{6} = \frac{4}{6} = \frac{2}{3}$.

questions.skill: Finding a missing number in a fraction equation
questions.stem: Which fraction makes this true: $\frac{1}{2} + ? = \frac{7}{8}$?
questions.solution: $\frac{1}{2} = \frac{4}{8}$. The missing part is $\frac{7}{8} - \frac{4}{8} = \frac{3}{8}$.

questions.skill: Subtracting mixed numbers
questions.stem: What is $5\frac{1}{3} - 2\frac{3}{4}$? Give the answer as a mixed number.

questions.skill: Dividing a fraction by a fraction (how many fit)
questions.stem: How many $\frac{1}{8}$-cup scoops fit exactly into $\frac{3}{4}$ cup of flour?
questions.solution: $\frac{3}{4} = \frac{6}{8}$, which is 6 eighths. So 6 scoops of $\frac{1}{8}$ cup fill $\frac{3}{4}$ cup. In symbols, $\frac{3}{4} \div \frac{1}{8} = \frac{3}{4} \times 8 = 6$.

questions.skill: Interpreting a quotient
questions.stem: Which question can be answered by finding $4 \div \frac{1}{3}$?
choices: What is one third of 4 cups of juice?
How much juice does each of 3 people get if they share 4 cups equally?
How many 4-cup jugs can be filled from one third of a cup of juice?
How many one-third-cup servings are in 4 cups of juice?
questions.answer: How many one-third-cup servings are in 4 cups of juice?
questions.solution: $4 \div \frac{1}{3}$ asks how many groups of $\frac{1}{3}$ fit into 4, so the answer is 12 servings. One third of 4 is multiplication, the jug question is $\frac{1}{3} \div 4$, and sharing 4 cups among 3 people is $4 \div 3$.

solve.answer: How many one-third-cup servings are in 4 cups of juice?
solve.work: 4 / (1/3) asks how many groups of 1/3 are in 4: servings of one-third cup in 4 cups (= 12). One third of 4 is 4 x 1/3; sharing among 3 is 4 / 3; the jug option is (1/3) / 4.

questions.skill: Adding fractions and mixed numbers
questions.stem: Find the sum: $2\frac{2}{3} + 1\frac{3}{4}$.
questions.solution: Whole numbers: 2 + 1 = 3. Fractions: $\frac{2}{3} = \frac{8}{12}$ and $\frac{3}{4} = \frac{9}{12}$, so $\frac{8}{12} + \frac{9}{12} = \frac{17}{12} = 1\frac{5}{12}$. The total is 3 + $1\frac{5}{12}$ = $4\frac{5}{12}$.

questions.skill: Subtracting fractions and mixed numbers
questions.stem: Which is the value of $3 - 1\frac{3}{5}$?
questions.solution: Regroup 3 as $2\frac{5}{5}$. Then $2\frac{5}{5} - 1\frac{3}{5} = 1\frac{2}{5}$.

questions.skill: Multiplying fractions
questions.stem: What is $\frac{5}{6} \times \frac{9}{10}$?
questions.solution: Multiply the tops (5 x 9 = 45) and the bottoms (6 x 10 = 60): $\frac{45}{60}$. Divide the top and bottom by 15 to get $\frac{3}{4}$.

questions.skill: Multiplying fractions
questions.stem: What is $\frac{5}{8}$ of 40?
questions.solution: One eighth of 40 is 5, so $\frac{5}{8}$ of 40 is 5 x 5 = 25.

questions.skill: Multiplying fractions
questions.stem: What is $\frac{5}{12} \times \frac{9}{10}$?
questions.solution: Cancel 5 with 10 (leaving 1 and 2) and 9 with 12 (leaving 3 and 4). The product is $\frac{3}{8}$. Check: $\frac{5}{12} \times \frac{9}{10} = \frac{45}{120} = \frac{3}{8}$.

questions.skill: Multiplying mixed numbers
questions.stem: Find the product: $1\frac{1}{3} \times 2\frac{1}{4}$.
questions.solution: Change to improper fractions: $\frac{4}{3} \times \frac{9}{4}$. The 4s cancel and 9 divided by 3 is 3, so the product is 3.

questions.skill: Multiplying mixed numbers
questions.stem: Evaluate $3\frac{1}{2} \times \frac{4}{7}$.

questions.skill: Dividing a whole number by a fraction
questions.stem: A baker has 6 cups of flour. Each batch of bread uses $\frac{3}{4}$ cup. How many batches can the baker make?
questions.solution: $6 \div \frac{3}{4} = 6 \times \frac{4}{3} = \frac{24}{3} = 8$. Check: 8 batches of $\frac{3}{4}$ cup is 6 cups.

questions.skill: Dividing a whole number by a fraction
questions.stem: What is $8 \div \frac{2}{3}$?
questions.solution: Multiply by the flip of $\frac{2}{3}$: $8 \times \frac{3}{2} = \frac{24}{2} = 12$.

questions.skill: Dividing a fraction by a whole number
questions.stem: Four friends share $\frac{2}{3}$ of a pizza equally. What fraction of the whole pizza does each friend get?

questions.skill: Dividing a fraction by a whole number
questions.stem: Find $\frac{9}{10} \div 3$.
questions.solution: Dividing by 3 is the same as multiplying by $\frac{1}{3}$: $\frac{9}{10} \times \frac{1}{3} = \frac{9}{30} = \frac{3}{10}$.

questions.skill: Dividing a fraction by a fraction
questions.stem: Find the value of $\frac{5}{6} \div \frac{1}{3}$.
questions.solution: Multiply by the flip: $\frac{5}{6} \times \frac{3}{1} = \frac{15}{6} = \frac{5}{2} = 2\frac{1}{2}$.

questions.skill: Dividing a fraction by a fraction
questions.stem: What is $\frac{3}{4} \div \frac{9}{10}$?
questions.solution: Multiply by the flip: $\frac{3}{4} \times \frac{10}{9} = \frac{30}{36} = \frac{5}{6}$.

questions.skill: Dividing a fraction by a fraction
questions.stem: What is $\frac{7}{8} \div \frac{3}{4}$?
questions.solution: Multiply by the flip: $\frac{7}{8} \times \frac{4}{3} = \frac{28}{24} = \frac{7}{6} = 1\frac{1}{6}$.

choices: $\frac{3}{4}$ cup of juice is shared equally by 8 people. How much does each person get?
What is $\frac{1}{8}$ of $\frac{3}{4}$ cup of juice?

How much is left when $\frac{1}{8}$ cup is taken from $\frac{3}{4}$ cup of juice?
questions.answer: A ribbon $\frac{3}{4}$ meter long is cut into pieces $\frac{1}{8}$ meter long. How many pieces are there?
questions.solution: Cutting a length into equal pieces and asking how many pieces is division of the length by the piece size: $\frac{3}{4} \div \frac{1}{8} = 6$.

solve.answer: A ribbon $\frac{3}{4}$ meter long is cut into pieces $\frac{1}{8}$ meter long. How many pieces are there?
solve.work: 3/4 / (1/8) asks how many 1/8s are in 3/4: the ribbon cut into 1/8-meter pieces. Sharing by 8 is 3/4 / 8; 1/8 of 3/4 is multiplication; taking 1/8 away is subtraction.

questions.skill: Interpreting a quotient
questions.stem: Joel has $\frac{7}{8}$ gallon of paint. Each fence panel needs $\frac{1}{4}$ gallon. He finds $\frac{7}{8} \div \frac{1}{4} = 3\frac{1}{2}$. What does the $\frac{1}{2}$ in $3\frac{1}{2}$ tell him?
choices: He has $\frac{1}{2}$ gallon of paint left over
He has enough paint for 3 whole panels and half of another
Each panel needs $\frac{1}{2}$ gallon of paint
He will use up half of his paint
questions.answer: He has enough paint for 3 whole panels and half of another
questions.solution: The quotient counts panels: 3 whole panels and half of another panel. (3 panels use $\frac{3}{4}$ gallon, leaving $\frac{1}{8}$ gallon, which is half of a panel.)

solve.answer: He has enough paint for 3 whole panels and half of another
solve.work: 7/8 / (1/4) = 7/8 x 4 = 7/2 = 3 1/2 panels. The 1/2 is half a panel's worth: 3 panels use 3/4 gal, leaving 1/8 gal = half of 1/4. Not 1/2 gallon left over.

questions.skill: Interpreting a quotient
questions.stem: A ribbon is $\frac{5}{6}$ meter long. It is cut into pieces that are each $\frac{1}{4}$ meter long. How many full pieces can be cut?
questions.solution: $\frac{5}{6} \div \frac{1}{4} = \frac{5}{6} \times 4 = \frac{20}{6} = 3\frac{1}{3}$. Only whole pieces count, so there are 3 full pieces. (3 pieces use $\frac{3}{4}$ meter; 4 pieces would need 1 meter.)

questions.stem: Dana has $5\frac{1}{4}$ meters of ribbon. She uses $1\frac{1}{2}$ meters for a gift and cuts the rest into pieces $\frac{3}{4}$ meter long. How many pieces does she cut?
questions.solution: Ribbon left: $5\frac{1}{4} - 1\frac{1}{2} = 3\frac{3}{4}$ meters. Pieces: $3\frac{3}{4} \div \frac{3}{4} = \frac{15}{4} \div \frac{3}{4} = 5$.

questions.skill: Checking reasonableness by estimating
questions.stem: Which is the best estimate of $3\frac{7}{8} \times 4\frac{1}{10}$?
questions.solution: $3\frac{7}{8}$ is about 4 and $4\frac{1}{10}$ is about 4. Then 4 x 4 = 16.

questions.skill: Checking reasonableness by estimating
questions.stem: Without calculating, which statement is true?
questions.solution: Multiplying by a number less than 1 makes 6 smaller, so $6 \times \frac{3}{4}$ is less than 6. Dividing by $\frac{3}{4}$ makes it bigger (8); multiplying by $1\frac{1}{4}$ makes it bigger; dividing by $1\frac{1}{4}$ makes it smaller.

solve.work: 6 / 1 1/4 < 6 (divisor > 1), so A false. 6 / (3/4) > 6 (divisor < 1), B false. 6 x 1 1/4 > 6, C false. 6 x 3/4 < 6 (factor < 1), D true.

questions.skill: Finding a missing number in a fraction equation
questions.stem: What is the value of n in $n \times \frac{5}{6} = \frac{5}{9}$?
questions.solution: Undo the multiplication by dividing: $n = \frac{5}{9} \div \frac{5}{6} = \frac{5}{9} \times \frac{6}{5} = \frac{30}{45} = \frac{2}{3}$. Check: $\frac{2}{3} \times \frac{5}{6} = \frac{10}{18} = \frac{5}{9}$.

questions.skill: Multiplying mixed numbers in context
questions.stem: A recipe needs $2\frac{1}{2}$ cups of flour. Maya makes $1\frac{3}{5}$ times the recipe. How many cups of flour does she need?
questions.solution: Write the mixed numbers as fractions: $2\frac{1}{2} = \frac{5}{2}$ and $1\frac{3}{5} = \frac{8}{5}$. Then $\frac{5}{2} \times \frac{8}{5} = \frac{40}{10} = 4$ cups.

questions.skill: Interpreting a quotient greater than 1
questions.stem: A baker has $\frac{5}{6}$ kilogram of dough. Each loaf uses $\frac{2}{3}$ kilogram. How many loaves can the baker make, counting part of a loaf? Give the answer as a mixed number.
questions.solution: Divide: $\frac{5}{6} \div \frac{2}{3} = \frac{5}{6} \times \frac{3}{2} = \frac{15}{12} = \frac{5}{4} = 1\frac{1}{4}$ loaves.

questions.solution: $5\frac{1}{3} = \frac{16}{3}$ and $2\frac{5}{8} = \frac{21}{8}$. Then $\frac{16}{3} \times \frac{21}{8} = 2 \times 7 = 14$ after cancelling 8 into 16 and 3 into 21.

questions.stem: Divide $\frac{4}{9}$ by $\frac{10}{3}$. What is the quotient?
questions.solution: Multiply by the flip: $\frac{4}{9} \times \frac{3}{10}$. Cancel 4 with 10 (leaving 2 and 5) and 3 with 9 (leaving 1 and 3). The product is $\frac{2}{15}$.

questions.skill: Interpreting a quotient
questions.stem: Ravi has 4 meters of ribbon and cuts pieces $\frac{3}{4}$ meter long. He finds $4 \div \frac{3}{4} = 5\frac{1}{3}$. What does the $\frac{1}{3}$ tell him?
choices: There are 5 full pieces, and the leftover ribbon is $\frac{1}{3}$ meter long
There are 5 full pieces, and the leftover ribbon is $\frac{1}{3}$ of another piece
There are 5 full pieces, and $\frac{1}{3}$ of the ribbon is not used
questions.answer: There are 5 full pieces, and the leftover ribbon is $\frac{1}{3}$ of another piece
questions.solution: 5 pieces use $\frac{15}{4}$ meters, leaving $\frac{1}{4}$ meter. That is one third of a $\frac{3}{4}$-meter piece, so the $\frac{1}{3}$ counts a part of a piece, not meters.

solve.answer: There are 5 full pieces, and the leftover ribbon is $\frac{1}{3}$ of another piece
solve.work: 4 / (3/4) = 16/3 = 5 1/3. 5 pieces use 15/4 m, leaving 1/4 m, which is 1/3 of a 3/4-m piece. Not 1/3 meter, not 1/3 of the ribbon (1/4 of 4 m is 1/16).

questions.skill: Interpreting a quotient
questions.stem: Which of these is NOT a situation that $\frac{2}{3} \div \frac{1}{6}$ describes?
choices: How many $\frac{1}{6}$-meter pieces can be cut from a rope $\frac{2}{3}$ meter long?
A $\frac{2}{3}$-liter bottle is shared equally by 6 people. How much does each person get?
$\frac{2}{3}$ of a pizza is cut into slices that are each $\frac{1}{6}$ of the whole pizza. How many slices?
How many $\frac{1}{6}$-cup scoops fit in $\frac{2}{3}$ cup of rice?
questions.answer: A $\frac{2}{3}$-liter bottle is shared equally by 6 people. How much does each person get?
questions.solution: The other three ask how many $\frac{1}{6}$s fit in $\frac{2}{3}$, which is $\frac{2}{3} \div \frac{1}{6} = 4$. Sharing $\frac{2}{3}$ among 6 people is $\frac{2}{3} \div 6 = \frac{1}{9}$.

solve.answer: A $\frac{2}{3}$-liter bottle is shared equally by 6 people. How much does each person get?
solve.work: Rope pieces, pizza slices of 1/6 each, and 1/6-cup scoops all ask how many 1/6s are in 2/3 (= 4). Sharing 2/3 liter among 6 people is 2/3 / 6 = 1/9, not 2/3 / (1/6).

questions.stem: A recipe for 12 muffins uses $2\frac{1}{4}$ cups of flour. Rosa has $6\frac{3}{4}$ cups of flour. How many muffins can she make if she uses all of her flour for this recipe?
questions.solution: $6\frac{3}{4} \div 2\frac{1}{4} = \frac{27}{4} \div \frac{9}{4} = 3$, so she can make the recipe 3 times. 3 x 12 = 36 muffins.

questions.skill: Multi-step fraction word problem
questions.stem: A garden is $4\frac{1}{2}$ meters long and $2\frac{2}{3}$ meters wide. Tom plants one packet of seeds for every $\frac{3}{4}$ square meter. How many packets does he need?
questions.solution: Area: $4\frac{1}{2} \times 2\frac{2}{3} = \frac{9}{2} \times \frac{8}{3} = 12$ square meters. Packets: $12 \div \frac{3}{4} = 12 \times \frac{4}{3} = 16$.

questions.skill: Multi-step fraction word problem
questions.stem: Priya has 10 yards of ribbon. She uses $2\frac{1}{3}$ yards for each of 3 gifts. How many yards of ribbon are left?
questions.solution: Used: $3 \times 2\frac{1}{3} = 3 \times \frac{7}{3} = 7$ yards. Left: 10 - 7 = 3 yards.

solve.work: 3 x 2 1/3 = 3 x 7/3 = 7 yards used; 10 - 7 = 3 yards left.

questions.skill: Multi-step fraction word problem
questions.stem: A bag of trail mix has $3\frac{1}{2}$ cups of nuts and $2\frac{1}{4}$ cups of raisins. Jo eats $\frac{1}{3}$ of the mix. How many cups of the mix does Jo eat?
questions.solution: Total mix: $3\frac{1}{2} + 2\frac{1}{4} = 5\frac{3}{4} = \frac{23}{4}$ cups. Jo eats $\frac{1}{3} \times \frac{23}{4} = \frac{23}{12} = 1\frac{11}{12}$ cups.

questions.solution: $8\frac{1}{9}$ is about 8 and $1\frac{9}{10}$ is about 2. Then $8 \div 2 = 4$.

questions.skill: Checking reasonableness by estimating

questions.solution: $4\frac{9}{10}$ is about 5 and $6\frac{1}{8}$ is about 6, so the product is near 30. (The exact value is $\frac{49}{10} \times \frac{49}{8} = \frac{2401}{80} = 30\frac{1}{80}$.)

questions.stem: Maria says that $0.4 \times 0.3 = 1.2$. Which explanation shows her mistake?
choices: The product should be 0.012, because the factors have three decimal places in all
Both numbers are less than 1, so the product must be less than 1; it is 0.12
questions.answer: Both numbers are less than 1, so the product must be less than 1; it is 0.12
questions.solution: 0.4 and 0.3 are both less than 1, so their product is less than 1. $4 \times 3 = 12$ and there are two decimal places in all (one in each factor), so $0.4 \times 0.3 = 0.12$.

solve.answer: Both numbers are less than 1, so the product must be less than 1; it is 0.12
solve.work: 0.4 x 0.3 = 0.12 (4 x 3 = 12, two decimal places). Both factors < 1 so product < 1. Option B wrongly counts three decimal places; C gives 12; D changes the operation.

questions.solution: $8 \times 3.49 = 27.92$ dollars. Check: 8 x 3.50 is 28.

questions.stem: A pack of 6 batteries costs 7.50 dollars. If every battery costs the same, how many dollars does one battery cost?
questions.solution: $7.50 \div 6 = 1.25$ dollars.

questions.skill: One-step decimal word problem
questions.stem: A rectangle is 4.5 centimeters long and 2.6 centimeters wide. What is its area in square centimeters?
questions.solution: Area is length times width: $4.5 \times 2.6 = 11.7$. (14.2 is the perimeter.)

questions.skill: One-step decimal word problem
questions.stem: Zed walks 1.25 kilometers each day. How many kilometers does he walk in 12 days?
questions.solution: $12 \times 1.25 = 15$ kilometers. Four days make 5 kilometers, and 12 days is 3 times that.

questions.skill: Multi-step decimal word problem
questions.stem: A shirt costs 18.75 dollars and a hat costs 9.40 dollars. Dee pays with two 20 dollar bills. How many dollars of change does Dee get?
questions.solution: Cost: $18.75 + 9.40 = 28.15$ dollars. Paid: 40 dollars. Change: $40 - 28.15 = 11.85$ dollars.

questions.skill: Multi-step decimal word problem
questions.stem: Pia buys 3 books that cost 6.85 dollars each and 2 pens that cost 1.20 dollars each. How many dollars does she spend in all?

questions.skill: Multi-step decimal word problem
questions.stem: Kai ran 3.6 kilometers on Monday. On Tuesday he ran 1.45 kilometers less than on Monday. How many kilometers did he run on both days together?
questions.solution: Tuesday: $3.6 - 1.45 = 2.15$ kilometers. Both days: $3.6 + 2.15 = 5.75$ kilometers.

questions.skill: Reasoning about decimal operations
questions.stem: Without calculating, which statement is true?
questions.solution: Dividing by a number less than 1 gives more than 6.4 ($6.4 \div 0.8 = 8$). Multiplying by 0.8 gives less than 6.4, and dividing by 1.6 gives less than 6.4.

solve.work: Dividing by 0.8 (< 1) gives more than 6.4 (it is 8): A true, B false. 6.4 / 1.6 = 4 < 6.4: C false. 6.4 x 0.8 = 5.12 < 6.4: D false.

questions.skill: Reasoning about decimal operations
questions.stem: Sam found $4.8 \times 3.25 = 1.56$. Which statement about his answer is true?
choices: It is correct, because multiplying by a decimal always gives a smaller number
It is too small, because $4.8 \times 3$ is already more than 14
It is too big, because the product must be less than 4.8
It is too big, because 3.25 is greater than 3
questions.answer: It is too small, because $4.8 \times 3$ is already more than 14
questions.solution: $4.8 \times 3 = 14.4$, and 3.25 is more than 3, so the product is more than 14.4. The answer 1.56 has the decimal point in the wrong place; the product is 15.6.

solve.answer: It is too small, because $4.8 \times 3$ is already more than 14
solve.work: 4.8 x 3.25 = 15.6, so 1.56 is too small. 4.8 x 3 = 14.4 > 14, which shows this. A, B and C are false.

questions.skill: Finding a missing number in a decimal equation
questions.stem: What is the value of n in $n \times 0.04 = 0.36$?
questions.solution: Undo the multiplication by dividing: $n = 0.36 \div 0.04 = 36 \div 4 = 9$. Check: 9 x 0.04 = 0.36.

questions.skill: Finding a missing number in a decimal equation
questions.stem: What is the value of n in $17.5 - n = 9.875$?
questions.solution: The missing amount is what is left after taking 9.875 from 17.5: $n = 17.500 - 9.875 = 7.625$.

questions.skill: Adding decimals to thousandths
questions.stem: Three boards are 1.275 meters, 0.8 meter and 2.065 meters long. Laid end to end, how many meters long are they together?
questions.solution: Line up the decimal points: $1.275 + 0.800 + 2.065 = 4.140$, which is 4.14 meters.

questions.skill: Dividing by a decimal in a word problem
questions.stem: A runner jogs 5.75 kilometers each day. How many days will it take the runner to jog a total of 46 kilometers?
questions.solution: Divide the total by the distance each day: $46 \div 5.75$. Multiply both numbers by 100 to get $4600 \div 575 = 8$. Check: $5.75 \times 8 = 46$. It takes 8 days.

questions.skill: Multiplying decimals and placing the decimal point
questions.stem: Which is the product $0.48 \times 6.5$?
questions.solution: Multiply as whole numbers: $48 \times 65 = 3120$. The factors have 2 + 1 = 3 decimal places, so the product is 3.120 = 3.12. Estimate to check: about $0.5 \times 6.5 \approx 3$.

questions.skill: Adding decimals
questions.solution: Line up the decimal points with three decimal places: $0.875 + 12.400 + 3.090 = 16.365$.

questions.skill: Adding decimals
Subtracting decimals
Subtracting decimals
questions.stem: Find the difference: $100.1 - 0.999$.

questions.skill: Subtracting decimals
Multiplying decimals
questions.stem: What is $0.35 \times 0.28$?
questions.solution: 35 x 28 = 980. There are 2 + 2 = 4 decimal places in all, so the product is 0.0980, which is 0.098.

questions.skill: Multiplying decimals
questions.stem: Find the product: $6.25 \times 0.16$.
questions.solution: 625 x 16 = 10000. There are 2 + 2 = 4 decimal places in all, so the product is 1.0000, which is 1.

questions.skill: Multiplying decimals
questions.stem: What is $12.4 \times 0.75$?
questions.solution: 124 x 75 = 9300. There are 1 + 2 = 3 decimal places in all, so the product is 9.300, which is 9.3.

questions.skill: Multiplying decimals
questions.stem: Multiply $3.07$ by $4.5$. Which is the product?
questions.solution: 307 x 45 = 13815. There are 2 + 1 = 3 decimal places in all, so the product is 13.815. Check: 3 x 4.5 = 13.5.

questions.skill: Dividing decimals
questions.stem: What is $2.4 \div 0.16$?
questions.solution: Multiply both numbers by 100: $240 \div 16 = 15$. Check: 0.16 x 15 = 2.4.

questions.skill: Dividing decimals
questions.solution: Multiply both numbers by 100: $3150 \div 45 = 70$. Check: 0.45 x 70 = 31.5.

questions.skill: Dividing decimals
questions.stem: What is $5.1 \div 0.12$?
questions.solution: Multiply both numbers by 100: $510 \div 12 = 42.5$. Check: 0.12 x 42.5 = 5.1.

questions.skill: Dividing decimals
questions.stem: Find $9 \div 0.24$.
questions.solution: Multiply both numbers by 100: $900 \div 24 = 37.5$. Check: 0.24 x 37.5 = 9.

questions.skill: Placing the decimal point from a known product or quotient
questions.stem: Since $64 \times 125 = 8000$, what is $0.64 \times 1.25$?
questions.solution: The factors have 2 + 2 = 4 decimal places in all, so 8000 becomes 0.8000, which is 0.8. Check: 0.64 is about 0.6 and 1.25 is a little more than 1, so the product is a little less than 1.

questions.skill: Estimating with decimals
questions.stem: Which is the best estimate of $0.49 \times 81.6$?
questions.solution: 0.49 is about 0.5 and 81.6 is about 80. Half of 80 is 40.

questions.skill: Estimating with decimals
questions.stem: Dana rounds 4.96, 3.08 and 2.1 to the nearest whole number and multiplies the three results to estimate their product. What estimate does she get?
questions.solution: 4.96 rounds to 5, 3.08 rounds to 3 and 2.1 rounds to 2. Then $5 \times 3 \times 2 = 30$.

questions.skill: Estimating with decimals
questions.stem: Which expression gives the best estimate of $24.9 \times 0.31$?
questions.solution: 24.9 is about 25 and 0.31 is about 0.3, so the estimate is $25 \times 0.3 = 7.5$. (The exact product is 7.719.) The other expressions are 10 times too big or 10 times too small.

solve.work: 24.9 is about 25 and 0.31 is about 0.3, so 25 x 0.3 (= 7.5; exact 7.719).

questions.skill: One-step decimal word problem
questions.stem: A 3.6-kilogram sack of rice is divided into bags of 0.45 kilogram each. How many bags are filled?
questions.solution: Multiply both numbers by 100: $360 \div 45 = 8$ bags.

questions.skill: One-step decimal word problem
questions.stem: A copper wire weighs 0.35 kilogram per meter. How many kilograms does a 2.64-meter piece of the wire weigh?
questions.solution: $2.64 \times 0.35$: 264 x 35 = 9240, and there are 2 + 2 = 4 decimal places, so the answer is 0.9240, which is 0.924 kilogram.

questions.skill: Multi-step decimal word problem
questions.stem: A taxi charges 3.50 dollars to start plus 2.15 dollars for each mile. How many dollars does a 6-mile ride cost?
questions.solution: Miles: $6 \times 2.15 = 12.90$. Add the starting charge: $12.90 + 3.50 = 16.40$, which is 16.4 dollars.

questions.skill: Multi-step decimal word problem
questions.stem: Lena buys 2.5 kilograms of apples at 1.80 dollars per kilogram and 0.75 kilogram of cheese at 12.40 dollars per kilogram. How many dollars does she spend in all?
questions.solution: Apples: $2.5 \times 1.80 = 4.50$. Cheese: $0.75 \times 12.40 = 9.30$. Total: $4.50 + 9.30 = 13.80$, which is 13.8 dollars.

questions.skill: Multi-step decimal word problem
questions.stem: Jordan has 40 dollars. A game costs 24.95 dollars and a case costs 6.80 dollars. How many dollars does Jordan have left after buying both?

questions.skill: Multi-step decimal word problem
questions.stem: A rectangular room is 5.6 meters long and 4.25 meters wide. Carpet costs 8 dollars per square meter. How many dollars does it cost to carpet the whole floor?
questions.solution: Area: $5.6 \times 4.25 = 23.8$ square meters. Cost: $23.8 \times 8 = 190.4$ dollars.

questions.skill: Multi-step decimal word problem
questions.stem: A tank holds 45.6 liters. It already has 9.6 liters in it. A hose adds 2.4 liters each minute. How many minutes does it take to fill the tank?
questions.solution: Space left: $45.6 - 9.6 = 36$ liters. Time: $36 \div 2.4 = 360 \div 24 = 15$ minutes.

questions.skill: Multi-step decimal word problem
questions.stem: A train ticket costs 12.75 dollars. A group of 6 gets 1.50 dollars off each ticket. How many dollars does the group pay in all?
questions.solution: Price after the discount: $12.75 - 1.50 = 11.25$ dollars. For 6 tickets: $6 \times 11.25 = 67.50$, which is 67.5 dollars.

questions.skill: Multi-step decimal word problem
questions.stem: Eva runs 4.35 kilometers on each of 3 mornings and 2.8 kilometers on each of 2 evenings. She wants to run 25 kilometers this week. How many more kilometers does she need to run?
questions.solution: Mornings: $3 \times 4.35 = 13.05$. Evenings: $2 \times 2.8 = 5.6$. So far: $13.05 + 5.60 = 18.65$. Still to run: $25 - 18.65 = 6.35$ kilometers.

questions.skill: Reasoning about decimal operations
questions.stem: Dev says $5.2 \div 0.4 = 1.3$, because $52 \div 4 = 13$. Which statement is true?
choices: He should not move the decimal point in the quotient; $5.2 \div 0.4 = 13$
He is right, because dividing by a number less than 1 gives a smaller answer
He should have moved it two places; $5.2 \div 0.4 = 0.13$
He is right, because the decimal point moves one place left when dividing by tenths
questions.answer: He should not move the decimal point in the quotient; $5.2 \div 0.4 = 13$
questions.solution: Multiplying both numbers by 10 gives $52 \div 4 = 13$, and the quotient does not change when both numbers are multiplied by the same amount. So $5.2 \div 0.4 = 13$. Check: 0.4 x 13 = 5.2.

solve.answer: He should not move the decimal point in the quotient; $5.2 \div 0.4 = 13$
solve.work: 5.2 / 0.4 = 52 / 4 = 13 (multiply both by 10; quotient unchanged). 1.3 is wrong (dividing by < 1 gives more than 5.2); 0.13 wrong. So 13.

questions.skill: Reasoning about decimal operations
questions.stem: Without finding exact values, which expression has the greatest value?
questions.solution: Dividing 4.6 by 0.9, which is less than 1, gives more than 4.6 (about 5.1). The others are 4.14, 3.7 and 4.69, which are all less than 5.

questions.skill: Finding a missing number in a decimal equation
questions.stem: What is the value of n in $n \times 0.35 = 2.8$?
questions.solution: Undo the multiplication by dividing: $n = 2.8 \div 0.35 = 280 \div 35 = 8$. Check: 8 x 0.35 = 2.8.

questions.skill: Finding a missing number in a decimal equation
questions.stem: A number is multiplied by 0.25, and then 1.5 is added. The result is 4.75. What is the number?
questions.solution: Work backward. Undo the addition: $4.75 - 1.5 = 3.25$. Undo the multiplication: $3.25 \div 0.25 = 13$. Check: 13 x 0.25 = 3.25, and 3.25 + 1.5 = 4.75.

questions.skill: Adding integers
questions.stem: What is $-7 + 12$?
questions.solution: Seven of the 12 positive units cancel the 7 negative units (zero pairs). That leaves $12 - 7 = 5$ positive units.

questions.skill: Subtracting integers
questions.stem: What is $5 - 9$?
questions.solution: $5 - 9 = 5 + (-9)$. Nine negative units cancel 5 positive units and leave 4 negative units, so the answer is $-4$.

questions.skill: Zero pairs
questions.stem: A collection has 5 positive chips and 8 negative chips. Each positive chip and negative chip together make a zero pair. What is the value of the whole collection?
questions.solution: Five zero pairs cancel, using all 5 positive chips and 5 of the negative chips. That leaves 3 negative chips, so the value is $-3$.

solve.work: 5 zero pairs cancel; 3 negative chips remain: 5 + (-8) = -3.

questions.skill: Zero pairs and chip models
questions.stem: Maya has 9 positive chips and 4 negative chips on a mat. She removes every zero pair. What is left on the mat?
questions.solution: Each of the 4 negative chips pairs with a positive chip, and every pair is worth 0. That removes 4 positive chips and leaves $9 - 4 = 5$ positive chips.

solve.work: 9 positive and 4 negative make 4 zero pairs; removing them leaves 9 - 4 = 5 positive chips.

questions.skill: Zero pairs and chip models
questions.stem: A zero pair is one positive chip together with one negative chip. How many zero pairs can be made from 7 positive chips and 10 negative chips?
questions.solution: Each zero pair needs one chip of each kind. There are only 7 positive chips, so at most 7 pairs can be made. Three negative chips are left over.

solve.work: Each zero pair uses one positive and one negative; only 7 positives exist, so min(7, 10) = 7 pairs.

questions.skill: Zero pairs and chip models
questions.stem: Which collection of chips has a total value of 0?
questions.solution: The chips must pair off completely. Only 6 positive chips and 6 negative chips make 6 zero pairs with nothing left over. The other collections leave 1 negative chip, 6 negative chips or 6 positive chips.

questions.skill: Adding integers
questions.stem: Find the sum: $-4 + (-9)$.
questions.solution: Both numbers are negative, so add 4 and 9 and keep the negative sign: $-4 + (-9) = -13$.

solve.work: Same signs: add absolute values 4+9=13, keep the negative sign: -13.

questions.skill: Adding integers
questions.solution: The negative number is farther from 0, so the sum is negative. Subtract the sizes: $10 - 4 = 6$, so $-10 + 4 = -6$.

solve.work: Different signs: 10-4=6, sign of -10 (larger absolute value): -6.

questions.skill: Adding integers
questions.stem: What is the sum of $-7$ and $-7$?
questions.solution: Two negative numbers add to a negative number: $7 + 7 = 14$, so the sum is $-14$.

questions.skill: Adding integers
questions.stem: Calculate $9 + (-12)$.
questions.solution: Start at 9 and move 12 units to the left. You pass 0 after 9 units and end 3 units below it, at $-3$.
