solve.work: Area = 15 x 6 = 90. Height to the 9 cm side = 90 / 9 = 10. Consistent: 10 <= 15 and 6 <= 9.

questions.skill: Choosing the right measurements and checking an answer
questions.stem: Which is the best estimate for the area of a triangle with a base of 19.8 meters and a height of 10.2 meters, in square meters?
questions.solution: Round to 20 and 10. Half of $20 \times 10$ is 100. The exact area is $\frac{1}{2} \times 19.8 \times 10.2 = 100.98$, so 100 is the best estimate. A value of 200 forgets to take half.

solve.work: Round to base 20, height 10: 1/2 x 20 x 10 = 100. (Exact: 100.98.)

questions.skill: Solving area problems in context
questions.stem: Anita wants a rectangular wall panel with the same area as 30 parallelogram-shaped stickers. Each sticker has a base of 6 centimeters and a height of 4 centimeters. The panel is 20 centimeters tall. How long is the panel, in centimeters?
questions.solution: One sticker has an area of $6 \times 4 = 24$ square centimeters, so 30 stickers have an area of 720 square centimeters. The panel has area length times 20, so the length is $720 \div 20 = 36$ centimeters.

solve.work: Each sticker 6 x 4 = 24 sq cm; 30 stickers = 720 sq cm. Length = 720 / 20 = 36 cm.

questions.skill: Telling which quadrant a point is in from the signs of its coordinates
questions.stem: Which point is in the part of the coordinate plane where both the x-coordinate and the y-coordinate are negative?
questions.solution: Both coordinates must be negative. Only $(-4, -2)$ has a negative x-coordinate and a negative y-coordinate.

solve.work: Both coordinates negative is Quadrant III: (-4, -2).

questions.skill: Reflecting a point across the x-axis
questions.stem: The point $(3, 5)$ is reflected across the x-axis. What are the coordinates of the new point?
questions.solution: A reflection across the x-axis keeps the x-coordinate and changes the sign of the y-coordinate, so $(3, 5)$ becomes $(3, -5)$.

solve.work: Reflection across the x-axis keeps x and negates y: (3, 5) -> (3, -5).

questions.skill: Distance between two points with the same x-coordinate
questions.stem: Point $A$ is at $(4, 1)$ and point $B$ is at $(4, 8)$. How many units apart are the two points?
questions.solution: The points have the same x-coordinate, so they are on one vertical line. The distance is the difference of the y-coordinates: $8 - 1 = 7$ units.

questions.skill: Naming the quadrant or axis of a point
questions.stem: In which quadrant is the point $(4, -6)$? Quadrant I is where both coordinates are positive, and the quadrants are numbered I, II, III, IV going counterclockwise from there.
questions.solution: The x-coordinate 4 is positive and the y-coordinate $-6$ is negative. Positive x with negative y is Quadrant IV.

solve.work: x = 4 > 0, y = -6 < 0: right and below, Quadrant IV.

questions.skill: Naming the quadrant or axis of a point
questions.stem: Which of these ordered pairs names a point in Quadrant II? Quadrant I is where both coordinates are positive, and the quadrants are numbered I, II, III, IV going counterclockwise from there.
questions.solution: Quadrant II has a negative x-coordinate and a positive y-coordinate. Only $(-5, 2)$ has that pattern.

solve.work: Quadrant II needs x < 0 and y > 0: only (-5, 2).

questions.skill: Naming the quadrant or axis of a point
questions.stem: Where does the point $(0, -4)$ lie?
questions.solution: A point with an x-coordinate of 0 is on the y-axis. Points on an axis are not inside any quadrant.

solve.work: x = 0, so the point is on the y-axis (4 below the origin), not in any quadrant.

questions.skill: Reading ordered pairs and plotting by moves
questions.stem: To plot the point $(5, -3)$ starting at the origin, how should you move?
questions.solution: The first number tells the horizontal move and the second tells the vertical move. A positive 5 means right and a negative 3 means down.

questions.skill: Reading ordered pairs and plotting by moves
questions.stem: Starting at the origin, Lee moves 4 units to the left and 6 units up. What is the x-coordinate of the point where Lee stops?
questions.solution: Moving 4 units left from 0 gives an x-coordinate of $-4$. (Moving up changes only the y-coordinate, which is 6.)

questions.skill: Reading ordered pairs and plotting by moves
questions.stem: Which ordered pair names the point 2 units left of the y-axis and 7 units below the x-axis?
questions.solution: Left of the y-axis means a negative x-coordinate, $-2$. Below the x-axis means a negative y-coordinate, $-7$. The x-coordinate is written first.

questions.skill: Reflecting a point across the x-axis or the y-axis
questions.stem: The point $(2, 6)$ is reflected across the y-axis. What is the x-coordinate of the new point?
questions.solution: A reflection across the y-axis changes the sign of the x-coordinate and keeps the y-coordinate. The new point is $(-2, 6)$, so the x-coordinate is $-2$.

solve.work: Across the y-axis x changes sign: (-2, 6). x = -2.

questions.skill: Reflecting a point across the x-axis or the y-axis
questions.stem: The point $(-4, 3)$ is reflected across the y-axis. What are the coordinates of the new point?
questions.solution: Reflecting across the y-axis changes the sign of the x-coordinate only. $-4$ becomes 4 and the y-coordinate 3 stays.

questions.skill: Reflecting a point across the x-axis or the y-axis
questions.stem: A point is reflected across the x-axis. What happens to its coordinates?
choices: The x-coordinate stays the same and the y-coordinate changes sign.
The y-coordinate stays the same and the x-coordinate changes sign.
questions.answer: The x-coordinate stays the same and the y-coordinate changes sign.
questions.solution: The x-axis is a horizontal line. A point and its reflection are the same distance from it on opposite sides, so the x-coordinate stays and the y-coordinate becomes its opposite.

solve.answer: The x-coordinate stays the same and the y-coordinate changes sign.
solve.work: Reflection across the x-axis keeps x and negates y.

questions.skill: Reflections across both axes and what they preserve
questions.stem: A point in Quadrant I is reflected across the x-axis. In which quadrant is the new point? Quadrant I is where both coordinates are positive, and the quadrants are numbered I, II, III, IV going counterclockwise from there.
questions.solution: A point in Quadrant I has positive x and positive y. Across the x-axis the y-coordinate becomes negative, so the new point has positive x and negative y, which is Quadrant IV.

questions.skill: Reflections across both axes and what they preserve
questions.stem: The point $(3, 2)$ is reflected across the x-axis, and the new point is then reflected across the y-axis. What is the x-coordinate of the final point?
questions.solution: Across the x-axis: $(3, 2)$ becomes $(3, -2)$. Across the y-axis: $(3, -2)$ becomes $(-3, -2)$. The final x-coordinate is $-3$.

questions.skill: Reflections across both axes and what they preserve
questions.stem: Which move takes the point $(2, 5)$ to the point $(-2, 5)$?
choices: Moving it 2 units to the left
questions.solution: Only the x-coordinate changes, and it changes sign. That is a reflection across the y-axis. Moving 2 units left would give $(0, 5)$.

solve.work: Only x changes sign: reflection across the y-axis. (x-axis gives (2,-5); both gives (-2,-5); 2 left gives (0,5).)

questions.skill: Distance between points that share a coordinate
questions.stem: Maya walks along a grid line from $(1, 5)$ to $(8, 5)$. Each unit of the grid is one block. How many blocks does she walk?
questions.solution: The y-coordinates are both 5, so she walks along a horizontal line. The distance is $8 - 1 = 7$ blocks.

questions.skill: Distance between points that share a coordinate
questions.stem: On a map grid, a library is at $(6, 2)$ and a park is at $(6, 10)$. How many units apart are they?
questions.solution: The x-coordinates match, so the points are on a vertical line. The distance is $10 - 2 = 8$ units.

questions.skill: Distance between points that share a coordinate
questions.stem: A drone flies straight along a grid line from $(-3, 4)$ to $(-3, 9)$. How many units does it fly?
questions.solution: Both points have an x-coordinate of $-3$, so the path is vertical. The distance is $9 - 4 = 5$ units.

questions.skill: Distance from a point to an axis
questions.stem: How many units is the point $(5, 8)$ from the y-axis?
questions.solution: The distance from the y-axis is the size of the x-coordinate. Here that is 5 units.

questions.skill: Distance from a point to an axis
questions.stem: How many units is the point $(-6, 2)$ from the x-axis?
questions.solution: The distance from the x-axis is the size of the y-coordinate, which is 2 units. (The 6 is the distance from the y-axis.)

questions.skill: Distance from a point to an axis
questions.stem: How many units is the point $(0, -7)$ from the origin?
questions.solution: The point is on the y-axis, 7 units below the origin. The distance is 7 units.

solve.work: On the y-axis, 7 below the origin: 7.

questions.skill: Perimeter of a polygon on the coordinate plane
questions.stem: A square has vertices at $(0, 0)$, $(5, 0)$, $(5, 5)$ and $(0, 5)$. What is its perimeter in units?
questions.solution: Each side is 5 units long. The perimeter is $4 \times 5 = 20$ units.

questions.skill: Perimeter of a polygon on the coordinate plane
questions.stem: A rectangle has vertices at $(0, 0)$, $(6, 0)$, $(6, 2)$ and $(0, 2)$. What is its perimeter in units?
questions.solution: The sides are 6 units and 2 units long. The perimeter is $2 \times (6 + 2) = 16$ units. (The area is 12, which is not the perimeter.)

questions.skill: Perimeter of a polygon on the coordinate plane
questions.stem: A square has vertices at $(-2, -2)$, $(1, -2)$, $(1, 1)$ and $(-2, 1)$. What is its perimeter in units?
questions.solution: The bottom side runs from $x = -2$ to $x = 1$, which is 3 units. All four sides are 3 units, so the perimeter is $4 \times 3 = 12$ units.

questions.skill: Area of a rectangle or square on the coordinate plane
questions.stem: A rectangle has vertices at $(0, 0)$, $(5, 0)$, $(5, 3)$ and $(0, 3)$. What is its area in square units?
questions.solution: The width is 5 units and the height is 3 units. The area is $5 \times 3 = 15$ square units.

questions.skill: Area of a rectangle or square on the coordinate plane
questions.stem: A square has vertices at $(0, 0)$, $(-5, 0)$, $(-5, 5)$ and $(0, 5)$. What is its area in square units?
questions.solution: Each side is 5 units long, so the area is $5 \times 5 = 25$ square units. (20 would be the perimeter.)

questions.skill: Area of a rectangle or square on the coordinate plane
questions.stem: One side of a rectangle goes from $(-2, 1)$ to $(3, 1)$. The rectangle extends 2 units upward from that side. What is its area in square units?
questions.solution: The side is $3 - (-2) = 5$ units long and the rectangle is 2 units tall. The area is $5 \times 2 = 10$ square units.

questions.skill: Area of a triangle, parallelogram or trapezoid from its vertices
questions.stem: A triangle has vertices at $(0, 0)$, $(6, 0)$ and $(0, 4)$. What is its area in square units?
questions.solution: The base along the x-axis is 6 units and the height along the y-axis is 4 units. Area $= \frac{1}{2} \times 6 \times 4 = 12$ square units.

questions.skill: Area of a triangle, parallelogram or trapezoid from its vertices
questions.stem: Three corners of a triangular garden on a map grid are $(1, 1)$, $(7, 1)$ and $(4, 6)$. Each grid unit is 1 meter. What is the area of the garden in square meters?
questions.solution: The base from $(1, 1)$ to $(7, 1)$ is 6 units. The top point is 5 units above the base, since $6 - 1 = 5$. Area $= \frac{1}{2} \times 6 \times 5 = 15$ square units.

solve.work: Base from (1,1) to (7,1) = 6; height 6 - 1 = 5; area 1/2 x 6 x 5 = 15.

questions.skill: Area of a triangle, parallelogram or trapezoid from its vertices
questions.stem: A triangle has vertices at $(2, -1)$, $(2, 5)$ and $(5, 5)$. What is its area in square units?
questions.solution: One side is vertical, from $y = -1$ to $y = 5$, which is 6 units. Another is horizontal, from $x = 2$ to $x = 5$, which is 3 units. They meet at a right angle at $(2, 5)$, so the area is $\frac{1}{2} \times 6 \times 3 = 9$ square units.

solve.work: Right angle at (2,5): vertical leg 5 - (-1) = 6, horizontal leg 5 - 2 = 3. Area 9.

questions.skill: Finding a missing vertex or a point from conditions
questions.stem: Three corners of a square are $(0, 0)$, $(4, 0)$ and $(4, 4)$. What is the fourth corner?
questions.solution: The corner opposite $(4, 0)$ is above $(0, 0)$ and level with $(4, 4)$. It has x-coordinate 0 and y-coordinate 4, so it is $(0, 4)$.

solve.work: Right angle at (4,0); fourth corner completes the square: (0, 4).

questions.skill: Finding a missing vertex or a point from conditions
questions.stem: Point $A$ is at $(2, 3)$. Point $B$ is 5 units to the right of $A$ on the same horizontal line. What is the x-coordinate of $B$?
questions.solution: Moving 5 units right adds 5 to the x-coordinate: $2 + 5 = 7$.

questions.skill: Finding a missing vertex or a point from conditions
questions.stem: Point $P$ is at $(-3, 5)$. Point $Q$ is directly below $P$, 8 units away. What is the y-coordinate of $Q$?
questions.solution: Moving 8 units down subtracts 8 from the y-coordinate: $5 - 8 = -3$. So $Q$ is at $(-3, -3)$.

questions.skill: Distance between points on opposite sides of an axis
questions.stem: Point $A$ is at $(-7, 2)$ and point $B$ is at $(3, 2)$. How many units apart are the two points?
questions.solution: The points have the same y-coordinate, and they are on opposite sides of the y-axis. Add their distances from the axis: $7 + 3 = 10$ units. (Subtracting $7 - 3 = 4$ would be right only if both were on the same side.)

questions.skill: Distance between a point and its reflection
questions.stem: The point $(-3, 4)$ is reflected across the x-axis. How many units apart are the original point and its reflection?
questions.solution: The reflection is $(-3, -4)$. The two points are 4 units above and 4 units below the x-axis, so they are $4 + 4 = 8$ units apart.

solve.work: Reflection of (-3, 4) across the x-axis is (-3, -4). Distance = |4 - (-4)| = 8.

questions.skill: Perimeter of a rectangle on the coordinate plane
questions.stem: A rectangle has vertices at $(1, 2)$, $(7, 2)$, $(7, -3)$ and $(1, -3)$. What is the perimeter of the rectangle in units?
questions.solution: The width is $7 - 1 = 6$ units. The height is $2 - (-3) = 5$ units. The perimeter is $2 \times (6 + 5) = 22$ units.

solve.work: Width from x = 1 to 7 is 6; height from y = -3 to 2 is 5. Perimeter = 2(6 + 5) = 22.

questions.skill: Naming the quadrant or axis of a point
questions.stem: Here are five points: $(2, 3)$, $(-1, 4)$, $(5, -2)$, $(6, 6)$ and $(-3, -3)$. How many of them are in Quadrant I?
questions.solution: Quadrant I needs both coordinates positive. Only $(2, 3)$ and $(6, 6)$ qualify, so the answer is 2.

questions.skill: Naming the quadrant or axis of a point
questions.stem: The point $P$ is at $(-8, 5)$. Which statement is true?
choices: P is to the right of the y-axis and above the x-axis.
P is to the left of the y-axis and below the x-axis.
P is to the right of the y-axis and below the x-axis.
P is to the left of the y-axis and above the x-axis.
questions.answer: P is to the left of the y-axis and above the x-axis.
questions.solution: A negative x-coordinate puts a point to the left of the y-axis. A positive y-coordinate puts it above the x-axis.

solve.answer: P is to the left of the y-axis and above the x-axis.
solve.work: x = -8 < 0: left of y-axis; y = 5 > 0: above x-axis.

questions.skill: Naming the quadrant or axis of a point
questions.stem: Exactly one of these points is not in the upper left part of the plane (Quadrant II). Which one is it?
questions.solution: Quadrant II points have a negative x-coordinate and a positive y-coordinate. $(3, 7)$ has a positive x-coordinate, so it is in Quadrant I.

solve.work: (-1,10), (-2,6), (-9,1) all have x<0, y>0 (Quadrant II). (3, 7) has x>0, so it is in Quadrant I.

questions.skill: Reading ordered pairs and plotting by moves
questions.stem: A game piece is on the point $(-2, 3)$. It moves 5 units right and 6 units down. What is the y-coordinate of the point where it stops?
questions.solution: Moving down 6 units lowers the y-coordinate: $3 - 6 = -3$. (The 5 units right changes only the x-coordinate, from $-2$ to 3.)

questions.skill: Reading ordered pairs and plotting by moves
questions.stem: Jo starts at the point $(3, -4)$ and moves 7 units left and 2 units up. Where does Jo stop?
questions.solution: Moving 7 left: $3 - 7 = -4$. Moving 2 up: $-4 + 2 = -2$. Jo stops at $(-4, -2)$.

questions.skill: Reading ordered pairs and plotting by moves
questions.stem: Starting at the origin, a robot moves 6 units right, then 9 units down, then 6 units left. How many units is the robot from the origin when it stops?
questions.solution: After 6 right and 6 left the robot is back on the y-axis at x = 0. It is 9 units down, at $(0, -9)$, which is 9 units from the origin.

solve.work: (0,0) -> (6,0) -> (6,-9) -> (0,-9). Distance from origin along the y-axis: 9.

questions.skill: Reflecting a point across the x-axis or the y-axis
questions.stem: The point $(-6, -2)$ is reflected across the x-axis. What are the coordinates of the new point?
questions.solution: Across the x-axis only the y-coordinate changes sign: $-2$ becomes 2. The x-coordinate $-6$ stays.

questions.skill: Reflecting a point across the x-axis or the y-axis
questions.stem: A point is reflected across the x-axis and lands at $(3, 8)$. What was the y-coordinate of the original point?
questions.solution: Reflecting across the x-axis changes the sign of the y-coordinate, so the original y-coordinate was the opposite of 8, which is $-8$. The original point was $(3, -8)$.

questions.skill: Reflecting a point across the x-axis or the y-axis
questions.stem: The point $A$ is reflected across the y-axis to give the point $B$ at $(-7, -1)$. What are the coordinates of $A$?
questions.solution: A reflection across the y-axis changes the sign of the x-coordinate, so undoing it changes the sign again. $A$ is $(7, -1)$.

solve.work: Reflect B back across the y-axis: (7, -1).

questions.skill: Reflections across both axes and what they preserve
questions.stem: The point $(-5, 3)$ is reflected across the x-axis, and the new point is then reflected across the y-axis. What are the coordinates of the final point?
questions.solution: Across the x-axis: $(-5, 3)$ becomes $(-5, -3)$. Across the y-axis: $(-5, -3)$ becomes $(5, -3)$.

questions.skill: Reflections across both axes and what they preserve
questions.stem: A triangle has vertices at $(1, 2)$, $(4, 2)$ and $(4, 6)$. It is reflected across the x-axis. What is the area of the reflected triangle in square units?
questions.solution: A reflection does not change the size or shape of a figure. The original triangle has a horizontal side from 1 to 4 (length 3) and a vertical side from 2 to 6 (length 4), so its area is $\frac{1}{2} \times 3 \times 4 = 6$. The reflected triangle also has area 6.

solve.work: Right triangle: legs 4 - 1 = 3 and 6 - 2 = 4. Area 1/2 x 3 x 4 = 6; a reflection keeps the area.

questions.skill: Reflections across both axes and what they preserve
questions.stem: The point $(-4, 7)$ is reflected across the y-axis, and the new point is then reflected across the x-axis. What is the sum of the two coordinates of the final point?
questions.solution: Across the y-axis: $(-4, 7)$ becomes $(4, 7)$. Across the x-axis: $(4, 7)$ becomes $(4, -7)$. The sum is $4 + (-7) = -3$.

questions.skill: Distance between points that share a coordinate
questions.stem: Point $P$ is at $(-5, 3)$ and point $Q$ is at $(-5, -4)$. How many units apart are they?
questions.solution: The points are on opposite sides of the x-axis. The distance from $P$ to the axis is 3 and from $Q$ to the axis is 4, so the distance is $3 + 4 = 7$ units.

questions.skill: Distance between points that share a coordinate
questions.stem: A hiker walks along a horizontal line from $(-9, -2)$ to $(6, -2)$. How many units does the hiker walk?
questions.solution: The points are on opposite sides of the y-axis: 9 units to the left and 6 units to the right. The distance is $9 + 6 = 15$ units.

questions.skill: Distance between points that share a coordinate
questions.stem: Which pair of points is exactly 10 units apart?
questions.solution: $(-2, 5)$ and $(8, 5)$ share a y-coordinate, and $2 + 8 = 10$. The other pairs are 9, 12 and 8 units apart.

questions.skill: Distance from a point to an axis
questions.stem: Which point is closest to the x-axis?
questions.solution: The distance from the x-axis is the size of the y-coordinate: 1, 5, 3 and 4 for the four points. $(8, -1)$ is closest.

questions.skill: Distance from a point to an axis
questions.stem: The point $(-9, -4)$ is some distance from the x-axis and some distance from the y-axis. What is the total of those two distances, in units?
questions.solution: The distance from the y-axis is $|-9| = 9$ and the distance from the x-axis is $|-4| = 4$. The total is $9 + 4 = 13$ units.

questions.skill: Distance from a point to an axis
questions.stem: A point is in Quadrant IV. It is 6 units from the x-axis and 2 units from the y-axis. What are its coordinates?
questions.solution: Distance 2 from the y-axis means $x = 2$ or $-2$, and Quadrant IV makes x positive, so $x = 2$. Distance 6 from the x-axis means $y = 6$ or $-6$, and Quadrant IV makes y negative, so $y = -6$.

questions.skill: Perimeter of a polygon on the coordinate plane
questions.stem: A fence goes all the way around a rectangular yard. On a map grid, the corners of the yard are $(-4, 1)$, $(3, 1)$, $(3, -5)$ and $(-4, -5)$, and each grid unit is 1 meter. How many meters of fence are needed?
questions.solution: The yard is $3 - (-4) = 7$ meters wide and $1 - (-5) = 6$ meters tall. The fence is $2 \times (7 + 6) = 26$ meters long.

questions.skill: Perimeter of a polygon on the coordinate plane
questions.stem: A triangle has vertices at $(-2, -1)$, $(1, -1)$ and $(1, 3)$. The side from $(-2, -1)$ to $(1, 3)$ is 5 units long. What is the perimeter of the triangle in units?
questions.solution: The horizontal side goes from $x = -2$ to $x = 1$, which is 3 units. The vertical side goes from $y = -1$ to $y = 3$, which is 4 units. The perimeter is $3 + 4 + 5 = 12$ units.

solve.work: Horizontal side 1 - (-2) = 3; vertical side 3 - (-1) = 4; slanted side 5. Perimeter 12.

questions.skill: Perimeter of a polygon on the coordinate plane
questions.stem: One side of a square goes from $(-3, 2)$ to $(-3, -4)$. What is the perimeter of the square in units?
questions.solution: The side is vertical, and its length is $2 - (-4) = 6$ units. The perimeter is $4 \times 6 = 24$ units.

questions.skill: Area of a rectangle or square on the coordinate plane
questions.stem: On a map grid, a rectangular park has corners at $(-6, -3)$, $(2, -3)$, $(2, 4)$ and $(-6, 4)$. What is the area of the park in square units?
questions.solution: The park is $2 - (-6) = 8$ units wide and $4 - (-3) = 7$ units tall. The area is $8 \times 7 = 56$ square units.

questions.skill: Area of a rectangle or square on the coordinate plane
questions.stem: A rectangle has sides parallel to the axes. Which pair of opposite corners gives a rectangle with an area of 24 square units?
questions.solution: The areas are $6 \times 4 = 24$, $5 \times 5 = 25$, $6 \times 5 = 30$ and $4 \times 8 = 32$ square units. Only $(0, 0)$ and $(6, 4)$ give 24.

questions.skill: Area of a rectangle or square on the coordinate plane
questions.stem: The sides of a rectangle are parallel to the axes. One of its diagonals runs from $(-6, -2)$ to $(1, 3)$. What is the area of the rectangle in square units?
questions.solution: The rectangle is $1 - (-6) = 7$ units wide and $3 - (-2) = 5$ units tall. The area is $7 \times 5 = 35$ square units.

questions.skill: Area of a triangle, parallelogram or trapezoid from its vertices
questions.stem: A parallelogram has vertices at $(0, 0)$, $(5, 0)$, $(7, 3)$ and $(2, 3)$. What is its area in square units?
questions.solution: The bottom side from $(0, 0)$ to $(5, 0)$ is the base, 5 units long. The top side is 3 units above it, so the height is 3. Area $= 5 \times 3 = 15$ square units.

questions.skill: Area of a triangle, parallelogram or trapezoid from its vertices
questions.stem: Find the area, in square units, of the triangle whose corners are $(-4, -2)$, $(2, -2)$ and $(-1, 5)$.
questions.solution: The base from $(-4, -2)$ to $(2, -2)$ is 6 units. The top point is $5 - (-2) = 7$ units above the base. Area $= \frac{1}{2} \times 6 \times 7 = 21$ square units.

questions.skill: Area of a triangle, parallelogram or trapezoid from its vertices
questions.stem: A triangle is drawn with its three corners at $(-5, 3)$, $(4, 3)$ and $(1, -2)$. How many square units of area does it cover?
questions.solution: The base from $(-5, 3)$ to $(4, 3)$ is 9 units. The third vertex is $3 - (-2) = 5$ units below the base. Area $= \frac{1}{2} \times 9 \times 5 = 22.5$ square units.

questions.skill: Finding a missing vertex or a point from conditions
questions.stem: A rectangle has sides parallel to the axes. Three of its vertices are $A(-6, -2)$, $B(-6, 3)$ and $C(1, 3)$. What are the coordinates of the fourth vertex, $D$?
questions.solution: $D$ is below $C$ and to the right of $A$. It shares the x-coordinate of $C$ (1) and the y-coordinate of $A$ ($-2$), so it is $(1, -2)$.

solve.work: AB vertical (x = -6), BC horizontal (y = 3). D has C's x and A's y: (1, -2).

questions.skill: Finding a missing vertex or a point from conditions
questions.stem: Two neighboring corners of a square are at $(2, -1)$ and $(2, 4)$. The square lies to the right of the line joining them. What is the x-coordinate of the other two corners?
questions.solution: The side joining the two corners is $4 - (-1) = 5$ units long, so the square is 5 units wide. Going 5 units right from $x = 2$ gives $x = 7$.

questions.skill: Finding a missing vertex or a point from conditions
questions.stem: Point $P$ is at $(-4, 2)$. It is on the same horizontal line as point $M$, and $P$ is 9 units to the right of $M$. What is the x-coordinate of $M$?
questions.solution: $M$ is 9 units to the left of $P$, so subtract 9 from the x-coordinate: $-4 - 9 = -13$.

questions.skill: Area of a rectangle from two opposite corners
questions.stem: A rectangle has two opposite corners at $(-4, 3)$ and $(2, -1)$, and its sides are parallel to the axes. What is the area of the rectangle in square units?
questions.solution: The width is $2 - (-4) = 6$ units and the height is $3 - (-1) = 4$ units. The area is $6 \times 4 = 24$ square units.

questions.skill: Area of a right triangle on the coordinate plane
questions.stem: A triangle has vertices at $(-3, -2)$, $(5, -2)$ and $(5, 4)$. What is its area in square units?
questions.solution: The side from $(-3, -2)$ to $(5, -2)$ is horizontal and is $5 - (-3) = 8$ units long. The side from $(5, -2)$ to $(5, 4)$ is vertical and is $4 - (-2) = 6$ units long. They meet at a right angle, so the area is $\frac{1}{2} \times 8 \times 6 = 24$ square units.

solve.work: Base along y = -2 from x = -3 to 5: 8. Height along x = 5 from y = -2 to 4: 6. Right triangle area = 1/2 x 8 x 6 = 24.

questions.skill: Finding the fourth vertex of a rectangle
questions.stem: Three vertices of a rectangle are $(-3, 4)$, $(5, 4)$ and $(5, -2)$. The sides are parallel to the axes. What is the fourth vertex?
questions.solution: The fourth vertex shares its x-coordinate with $(-3, 4)$, which is $-3$, and its y-coordinate with $(5, -2)$, which is $-2$. So it is $(-3, -2)$.

solve.work: Missing corner takes x from (-3, 4) and y from (5, -2): (-3, -2).

questions.skill: Naming the quadrant or axis of a point
questions.stem: Here are six points: $(0, 5)$, $(-3, 0)$, $(4, -4)$, $(-6, -2)$, $(0, 0)$ and $(1, 8)$. How many of them do not lie in any quadrant?
questions.solution: A point is in no quadrant when it is on an axis, which means at least one coordinate is 0. Those points are $(0, 5)$, $(-3, 0)$ and $(0, 0)$, so the answer is 3.

solve.work: Points on an axis lie in no quadrant: (0,5), (-3,0), (0,0). Count 3.

questions.skill: Naming the quadrant or axis of a point
questions.stem: The point $(x, y)$ is in Quadrant II. In which quadrant is the point $(x, -y)$? Quadrant I is where both coordinates are positive, and the quadrants are numbered I, II, III, IV going counterclockwise from there.
questions.solution: In Quadrant II, x is negative and y is positive, so $-y$ is negative. The new point has a negative x-coordinate and a negative y-coordinate, which is Quadrant III.

solve.work: Quadrant II: x < 0, y > 0. Then (x, -y) has x < 0 and -y < 0: Quadrant III.

questions.skill: Reading ordered pairs and plotting by moves
questions.stem: Ann starts at the point $(-6, 2)$. She moves 9 units right and 8 units down, and then 5 units left. What is the x-coordinate of the point where she stops?
questions.solution: Only the horizontal moves change the x-coordinate: $-6 + 9 = 3$, and $3 - 5 = -2$. Ann stops with an x-coordinate of $-2$.

questions.skill: Reading ordered pairs and plotting by moves
questions.stem: A point is 3 units to the left of the y-axis. It is twice as far below the x-axis as it is left of the y-axis. Which ordered pair names the point?
questions.solution: Left of the y-axis by 3 gives $x = -3$. Twice as far below the x-axis is $2 \times 3 = 6$ units below, so $y = -6$.

solve.work: 3 left: x = -3. Twice as far below: 6 below, y = -6. (-3, -6).

questions.skill: Reading ordered pairs and plotting by moves
questions.stem: Dana starts at $(-3, -3)$ on a grid. She moves 8 units right, 10 units up, 4 units left and 2 units down. Where does she end?
questions.solution: Horizontal: $-3 + 8 - 4 = 1$. Vertical: $-3 + 10 - 2 = 5$. Dana ends at $(1, 5)$.

questions.skill: Reflecting a point across the x-axis or the y-axis
questions.stem: When the point $(a, b)$ is reflected across the y-axis, the new point is $(-2, 7)$. What is the value of $a + b$?
questions.solution: Reflecting across the y-axis changes the sign of the x-coordinate, so $a = 2$. The y-coordinate does not change, so $b = 7$. Then $a + b = 9$.

questions.skill: Reflecting a point across the x-axis or the y-axis
questions.stem: Which point stays in exactly the same place when it is reflected across the x-axis?
questions.solution: A point stays put only if it is on the line of reflection. The points on the x-axis have a y-coordinate of 0, and $(6, 0)$ is the only one listed. For example, $(0, 6)$ moves to $(0, -6)$.

solve.work: Unchanged under x-axis reflection only if y = 0: (6, 0).

questions.skill: Reflecting a point across the x-axis or the y-axis
questions.stem: The point $P$ is reflected across the y-axis, and the new point has an x-coordinate of $-8$. The same point $P$ is reflected across the x-axis, and that new point has a y-coordinate of $-3$. What is the x-coordinate of $P$ minus the y-coordinate of $P$?
questions.solution: The y-axis reflection flipped the sign of x, so $P$ has $x = 8$. The x-axis reflection flipped the sign of y, so $P$ has $y = 3$. Then $8 - 3 = 5$.

solve.work: Across y-axis: -x = -8, so x = 8. Across x-axis: -y = -3, so y = 3. x - y = 5.

questions.skill: Reflections across both axes and what they preserve
questions.stem: The point $A$ is reflected across the x-axis, and the new point is then reflected across the y-axis. The final point is $(4, -7)$. What are the coordinates of $A$?
questions.solution: Work backwards. Undo the y-axis reflection: $(4, -7)$ becomes $(-4, -7)$. Undo the x-axis reflection: $(-4, -7)$ becomes $(-4, 7)$. Check: $(-4, 7)$ goes to $(-4, -7)$, then to $(4, -7)$.

solve.work: Both reflections negate both coordinates: A = (-4, 7). Check: (-4,7) -> (-4,-7) -> (4,-7).

questions.skill: Reflections across both axes and what they preserve
questions.stem: A point with a positive x-coordinate is reflected across the y-axis. The original point and the new point are 14 units apart. What is the x-coordinate of the original point?
questions.solution: The y-axis is halfway between the point and its reflection, and each is the same distance from it. So each is $14 \div 2 = 7$ units from the y-axis. The original x-coordinate is 7.

solve.work: (x, y) and (-x, y) are 2x apart: 2x = 14, x = 7.

questions.skill: Reflections across both axes and what they preserve
questions.stem: Which point stays in the same place when it is reflected across the x-axis and then across the y-axis?
questions.solution: Both reflections change signs, and only 0 is its own opposite. The point must have both coordinates 0. For example, $(0, 5)$ goes to $(0, -5)$ and then stays $(0, -5)$.

questions.skill: Distance between points that share a coordinate
questions.stem: A hiker walks from $(-7, -2)$ straight to $(-7, 5)$ and then straight to $(4, 5)$. How many units does the hiker walk in all?
questions.solution: The first part is vertical: from $-2$ to 5 is $2 + 5 = 7$ units. The second part is horizontal: from $-7$ to 4 is $7 + 4 = 11$ units. The total is $7 + 11 = 18$ units.

questions.skill: Distance between points that share a coordinate
questions.stem: The number $a$ is positive. How many units apart are the points $(-a, 4)$ and $(a, 4)$?
questions.solution: The points have the same y-coordinate and are on opposite sides of the y-axis, each $a$ units from it. The distance is $a + a = 2a$.

questions.skill: Distance between points that share a coordinate
questions.stem: A triangle has vertices $A(-3, 2)$, $B(5, 2)$ and $C(5, -4)$. What is the sum of the lengths of side $AB$ and side $BC$, in units?
questions.solution: Side $AB$ is horizontal: $3 + 5 = 8$ units. Side $BC$ is vertical: from 2 down to $-4$ is $2 + 4 = 6$ units. The sum is $8 + 6 = 14$ units.

questions.skill: Distance from a point to an axis
questions.stem: A point in Quadrant III has an x-coordinate of $-9$. The point is 4 units farther from the x-axis than it is from the y-axis. What is its y-coordinate?
questions.solution: The distance from the y-axis is 9, so the distance from the x-axis is $9 + 4 = 13$. In Quadrant III the y-coordinate is negative, so it is $-13$.

solve.work: Distance from y-axis 9; from x-axis 9 + 4 = 13. Quadrant III: y = -13.

questions.skill: Distance from a point to an axis
questions.stem: Which point is exactly as far from the x-axis as it is from the y-axis?
questions.solution: The point $(-6, 6)$ is 6 units from each axis. The others are 6 and 3, 4 and 8, and 7 and 0 units from the two axes.

questions.skill: Perimeter of a polygon on the coordinate plane
questions.stem: A shape on the coordinate plane has vertices at $(0, 0)$, $(6, 0)$, $(6, 2)$, $(3, 2)$, $(3, 5)$ and $(0, 5)$, joined in that order and then back to $(0, 0)$. What is its perimeter in units?
questions.solution: The sides have lengths 6, 2, 3, 3, 3 and 5 units. Their sum is $6 + 2 + 3 + 3 + 3 + 5 = 22$ units.

questions.skill: Perimeter of a polygon on the coordinate plane
questions.stem: Four rectangles have sides parallel to the axes and are given by two opposite corners. Which rectangle has the greatest perimeter?
questions.solution: The sizes are $12 \times 1$, $8 \times 3$, $5 \times 5$ and $8 \times 4$, with perimeters 26, 22, 20 and 24. The first, with corners $(-10, 0)$ and $(2, 1)$, is greatest.

questions.skill: Perimeter of a polygon on the coordinate plane
questions.stem: A rectangle has two vertices at $(-3, -1)$ and $(4, -1)$. Its perimeter is 30 units, and its other two vertices are above these two. What is the y-coordinate of the other two vertices?
questions.solution: The known side is $4 - (-3) = 7$ units long. Half the perimeter is 15, so the other side is $15 - 7 = 8$ units. Going up 8 from $y = -1$ gives $y = 7$.

questions.skill: Area of a rectangle or square on the coordinate plane
questions.stem: A square has two neighboring corners at $(-2, -5)$ and $(-2, 3)$. What is the area of the square in square units?
questions.solution: The two corners are joined by a side of length $3 - (-5) = 8$ units. The area is $8 \times 8 = 64$ square units.

questions.skill: Area of a rectangle or square on the coordinate plane
questions.stem: A shape is made of two rectangles that share part of a side and do not overlap. The first has opposite corners at $(0, 0)$ and $(6, 4)$. The second has opposite corners at $(6, 0)$ and $(9, 2)$. What is the total area in square units?
questions.solution: The first rectangle is $6 \times 4 = 24$ square units. The second is $(9 - 6) \times (2 - 0) = 3 \times 2 = 6$ square units. The total is $24 + 6 = 30$ square units.

questions.skill: Area of a rectangle or square on the coordinate plane
questions.stem: A rectangle has its two bottom vertices at $(-3, 1)$ and $(2, 1)$ and an area of 60 square units. Its top vertices are above the bottom ones. What is the y-coordinate of the top vertices?
questions.solution: The bottom side is $2 - (-3) = 5$ units long, so the height is $60 \div 5 = 12$ units. Going up 12 from $y = 1$ gives $y = 13$.

questions.skill: Area of a triangle, parallelogram or trapezoid from its vertices
questions.stem: A parallelogram has vertices at $(-2, -1)$, $(-2, 4)$, $(3, 6)$ and $(3, 1)$. What is its area in square units?
questions.solution: Two sides are vertical: one from $y = -1$ to $y = 4$, which is 5 units long, and the other from $y = 1$ to $y = 6$. Use the first as the base. The distance between the vertical lines $x = -2$ and $x = 3$ is 5, so the height is 5. Area $= 5 \times 5 = 25$ square units.

solve.work: Vertical sides x = -2 (from -1 to 4) and x = 3 (from 1 to 6), each 5 long; they are 5 apart. Area 5 x 5 = 25.

questions.skill: Area of a triangle, parallelogram or trapezoid from its vertices
questions.stem: A trapezoid has vertices at $(0, 0)$, $(8, 0)$, $(6, 4)$ and $(2, 4)$. What is its area in square units?
questions.solution: The parallel sides are the bottom, from $x = 0$ to $x = 8$ (8 units), and the top, from $x = 2$ to $x = 6$ (4 units). The height is 4. Area $= \frac{1}{2} \times (8 + 4) \times 4 = 24$ square units.

solve.work: Parallel sides 8 and 6 - 2 = 4; height 4. Area 1/2 x 12 x 4 = 24.

questions.skill: Area of a triangle, parallelogram or trapezoid from its vertices
questions.stem: A triangle has vertices at $(0, 6)$, $(0, -2)$ and $(5, 1)$. What is its area in square units?
questions.solution: The side from $(0, 6)$ to $(0, -2)$ is on the y-axis and is $6 + 2 = 8$ units long. The third point is 5 units from the y-axis. Area $= \frac{1}{2} \times 8 \times 5 = 20$ square units.

solve.work: Base on the y-axis 6 - (-2) = 8; height 5. Area 1/2 x 8 x 5 = 20.

questions.skill: Finding a missing vertex or a point from conditions
questions.stem: A parallelogram has vertices $A(0, 0)$, $B(5, 0)$, $C(7, 3)$ and $D$, listed in order around the shape. What are the coordinates of $D$?
questions.solution: Side $AB$ goes 5 units right, so the opposite side $DC$ must also go 5 units right. $D$ is 5 units left of $C$: $(7 - 5, 3) = (2, 3)$.

solve.work: AB goes 5 right, so DC goes 5 right: D = (7 - 5, 3) = (2, 3).

questions.skill: Finding a missing vertex or a point from conditions
questions.stem: A square has sides parallel to the axes and a side length of 6. Its lower left corner is at $(-4, -3)$. What is the sum of the x-coordinate and the y-coordinate of its upper right corner?
questions.solution: The upper right corner is 6 units right and 6 units up from the lower left: $(-4 + 6, -3 + 6) = (2, 3)$. The sum is $2 + 3 = 5$.

questions.skill: Finding a missing vertex or a point from conditions
questions.stem: Two vertices of a rectangle are at $(-2, 1)$ and $(4, 1)$. The rectangle has an area of 24 square units, and its other two vertices are below these. Which pair gives the other two vertices?
questions.solution: The known side is $4 - (-2) = 6$ units long, so the height is $24 \div 6 = 4$. Going down 4 from $y = 1$ gives $y = -3$. The pair at $y = 5$ is above the side.

questions.skill: Naming the quadrant or axis of a point
questions.stem: How many points with integer coordinates are in Quadrant II and have an $x$-coordinate of at least $-4$ and a $y$-coordinate of at most 3?
questions.solution: In Quadrant II, $x$ is negative and $y$ is positive. So $x$ can be $-4$, $-3$, $-2$ or $-1$, and $y$ can be 1, 2 or 3. That gives $4 \times 3 = 12$ points.

questions.skill: Distance from a point to an axis
questions.stem: A point in Quadrant III is 7 units from the $y$-axis and 4 units from the $x$-axis. What is the sum of its $x$-coordinate and its $y$-coordinate?
questions.solution: In Quadrant III both coordinates are negative. A point 7 units from the $y$-axis has $x = -7$, and a point 4 units from the $x$-axis has $y = -4$. The sum is $-7 + (-4) = -11$.

solve.work: Quadrant III: both negative. 7 from y-axis -> x=-7; 4 from x-axis -> y=-4. Sum -11.

questions.skill: Naming the solid a net folds into
questions.stem: A net is made of exactly 2 triangles and 3 rectangles joined along their edges. When it is folded up, which solid does it make?
questions.solution: A triangular prism has 2 triangular bases and 3 rectangular side faces. A rectangular prism has 6 rectangles, and the pyramids have only one base.

solve.work: Two triangular bases plus three rectangular lateral faces fold into a triangular prism (a triangular pyramid has 4 triangles; a square pyramid 1 square + 4 triangles; a rectangular prism 6 rectangles).

questions.skill: Volume of a rectangular prism
questions.stem: A box shaped like a rectangular prism is 5 centimeters long, 4 centimeters wide and 3 centimeters tall. What is its volume in cubic centimeters?
questions.solution: Volume is length times width times height: $5 \times 4 \times 3 = 60$ cubic centimeters.

questions.skill: Surface area of a cube
questions.stem: A cube has edges that are each 3 inches long. What is its surface area in square inches?
questions.solution: A cube has 6 faces. Each face is a square of area $3 \times 3 = 9$, so the surface area is $6 \times 9 = 54$ square inches. (27 is the volume, 36 counts only four faces, and 18 counts only two.)

questions.skill: Naming the solid a net folds into
questions.stem: Zoe cuts out a net made of 1 square and 4 triangles. After she folds it up and tapes the edges, what solid has she made?
questions.solution: A solid with one base and triangular faces that meet at a point is a pyramid. The base is a square, so the solid is a square pyramid. A prism would need two matching bases.

solve.work: 1 square base + 4 triangles meeting at a point = square pyramid.

questions.skill: Naming the solid a net folds into
questions.stem: Which solid can be folded from a net with 2 hexagons and 6 rectangles?
questions.solution: A prism has two matching bases joined by rectangles. The two hexagons are the bases and the 6 rectangles join their 6 sides, so the solid is a hexagonal prism. A pyramid would have triangles, not rectangles.

solve.work: 2 congruent hexagon bases + 6 rectangles (one per side) = hexagonal prism.

questions.skill: Naming the solid a net folds into
questions.stem: A net is made of 4 triangles that are all the same size and nothing else. Which solid does it fold into?
questions.solution: Four triangles make 4 faces. A triangular pyramid has a triangle for its base and 3 triangles that meet at a point, so all 4 faces are triangles. A square pyramid has a square face and a triangular prism has rectangles.

solve.work: 4 congruent triangles, no other faces = triangular pyramid (tetrahedron).

questions.skill: Naming the solid a net folds into
questions.stem: Which solid can be made by folding a net of 6 squares that are all the same size?
questions.solution: A cube has 6 faces and every face is a square the same size as the others. A square pyramid has only one square and 4 triangles, and the other two solids have triangular faces.

solve.work: 6 congruent squares fold into a cube.

questions.skill: Counting faces, edges and vertices of prisms and pyramids
questions.stem: A triangular prism has two triangle bases joined by rectangles. How many faces does it have in all?
questions.solution: The 2 triangle bases each have 3 sides, and each side is joined by one rectangle, so there are 3 rectangles. The solid has $2 + 3 = 5$ faces.

questions.skill: Counting faces, edges and vertices of prisms and pyramids
questions.stem: Which of these solids has exactly 6 faces?
questions.solution: A rectangular prism has 2 bases and 4 rectangles, which is 6 faces. A triangular pyramid has 4 faces, a triangular prism has $2 + 3 = 5$ faces and a pentagonal prism has $2 + 5 = 7$ faces.

solve.work: Rectangular prism 6; triangular prism 5; triangular pyramid 4; pentagonal prism 7.

questions.skill: Surface area of a cube
questions.stem: A wooden cube has edges of 4 centimeters. Every face is painted. What total area is painted, in square centimeters?
questions.solution: Each face is a square with area $4 \times 4 = 16$ square centimeters. A cube has 6 faces, so the painted area is $6 \times 16 = 96$ square centimeters.

questions.skill: Surface area of a cube
questions.stem: Each face of a cube has an area of 9 square inches. What is the surface area of the cube, in square inches?
questions.solution: A cube has 6 faces that all have the same area, so the surface area is $6 \times 9 = 54$ square inches. Using 4 faces would give 36, and 81 is $9 \times 9$.

questions.skill: Surface area of a rectangular prism
questions.stem: The faces of a rectangular prism come in three matching pairs. The areas of the three different faces are 12, 8 and 6 square centimeters. What is the surface area of the prism, in square centimeters?
questions.solution: Each of the three faces appears twice. The surface area is $2 \times (12 + 8 + 6) = 2 \times 26 = 52$ square centimeters.

questions.skill: Surface area of a rectangular prism
questions.stem: A rectangular prism is 5 inches long, 2 inches wide and 1 inch tall. Which expression gives its surface area in square inches?
questions.solution: The prism has three kinds of faces, each appearing twice: $5 \times 2$, $5 \times 1$ and $2 \times 1$. Adding the areas of all 6 faces gives the first expression. The product $5 \times 2 \times 1$ is the volume, and the other two expressions leave out faces or do not multiply to find areas.

questions.skill: Surface area of a rectangular prism
questions.stem: A small box is 5 centimeters long, 3 centimeters wide and 2 centimeters tall. How many square centimeters of paper cover the whole box?
questions.solution: The faces are $5 \times 3 = 15$, $5 \times 2 = 10$ and $3 \times 2 = 6$ square centimeters, each twice. The surface area is $2 \times (15 + 10 + 6) = 2 \times 31 = 62$ square centimeters.

questions.skill: Surface area of a rectangular prism
questions.stem: The top of a rectangular prism measures 6 centimeters by 3 centimeters. What is the combined area of the top and the bottom, in square centimeters?
questions.solution: The top and bottom are matching rectangles. Each has an area of $6 \times 3 = 18$ square centimeters, so together they cover $2 \times 18 = 36$ square centimeters.

questions.skill: Total area of the faces in a net
questions.stem: A net of a triangular prism has 2 triangles with an area of 6 square centimeters each and 3 rectangles with areas of 10, 12 and 14 square centimeters. What is the total area of the net, in square centimeters?
questions.solution: The triangles together have an area of $2 \times 6 = 12$ square centimeters. The rectangles together have $10 + 12 + 14 = 36$. The net has a total area of $12 + 36 = 48$ square centimeters.

questions.skill: Total area of the faces in a net
questions.stem: A net for a cube is made of 6 squares, and each square has sides of 4 centimeters. What is the total area of the net, in square centimeters?
questions.solution: Each square has an area of $4 \times 4 = 16$ square centimeters, and there are 6 of them, so the total area is $6 \times 16 = 96$ square centimeters. The number 64 is the volume, 24 is $6 \times 4$ and 16 is one face.

questions.skill: Total area of the faces in a net
questions.stem: A net for a box is made of six rectangles. Their areas are 20, 20, 15, 15, 12 and 12 square centimeters. What is the total area of the net, in square centimeters?
questions.solution: Add the areas of all six rectangles: $20 + 20 + 15 + 15 + 12 + 12 = 94$ square centimeters.

questions.skill: Surface area of a triangular prism
questions.stem: A triangular prism has triangle ends with sides of 3 centimeters, 4 centimeters and 5 centimeters. The prism is 6 centimeters long. What is the combined area of its three rectangular faces, in square centimeters?
questions.solution: The three rectangles are $3 \times 6 = 18$, $4 \times 6 = 24$ and $5 \times 6 = 30$ square centimeters. Together they are $18 + 24 + 30 = 72$ square centimeters. This is the same as the perimeter of the triangle times the length: $12 \times 6 = 72$.

questions.skill: Surface area of a pyramid
questions.stem: A triangular pyramid has four faces that are identical triangles. Each face has an area of 15 square centimeters. What is the surface area of the pyramid, in square centimeters?
questions.solution: The surface area is the total of the areas of all 4 faces: $4 \times 15 = 60$ square centimeters. The value 45 counts only 3 faces, 30 counts 2 and 15 counts 1.

questions.skill: Volume of a rectangular prism with whole-number edges
questions.stem: A storage cube has an edge of 4 feet. What is its volume, in cubic feet?
questions.solution: The volume of a cube is edge times edge times edge: $4 \times 4 \times 4 = 64$ cubic feet.

questions.skill: Volume of a rectangular prism with whole-number edges
questions.stem: A juice box is 10 centimeters long, 5 centimeters wide and 2 centimeters tall. What is its volume, in cubic centimeters?
questions.solution: Volume is length times width times height: $10 \times 5 \times 2 = 100$ cubic centimeters.

questions.skill: Volume of a rectangular prism with whole-number edges
questions.stem: A rectangular tank has a bottom with an area of 24 square meters. The tank is 5 meters tall. What is its volume, in cubic meters?
questions.solution: Volume is the area of the base times the height: $24 \times 5 = 120$ cubic meters.

questions.skill: Volume of a rectangular prism with whole-number edges
questions.stem: A box is packed with unit cubes in 3 layers. Each layer has 4 rows with 5 cubes in each row. How many cubes are in the box?
questions.solution: Each layer holds $4 \times 5 = 20$ cubes, and there are 3 layers, so the box holds $3 \times 20 = 60$ cubes. The value 12 comes from adding 3, 4 and 5, 20 is only one layer, and 23 adds the number of layers to one layer.

questions.skill: Volume of a rectangular prism with fractional edges
questions.stem: A thin box is $\frac{1}{2}$ foot long, $\frac{1}{2}$ foot wide and 4 feet tall. What is its volume, in cubic feet?
questions.solution: Volume is length times width times height: $\frac{1}{2} \times \frac{1}{2} \times 4 = \frac{1}{4} \times 4 = 1$ cubic foot.

questions.skill: Volume of a rectangular prism with fractional edges
questions.stem: A rectangular prism has a base with an area of $\frac{3}{4}$ square meter and a height of 8 meters. What is its volume, in cubic meters?
questions.solution: Volume is the area of the base times the height: $\frac{3}{4} \times 8 = 6$ cubic meters.

questions.skill: Volume of a rectangular prism with fractional edges
questions.stem: A rectangular prism is $2\frac{1}{2}$ inches long, 3 inches wide and 4 inches tall. Which expression gives its volume in cubic inches?
questions.solution: Volume is length times width times height, so multiply all three edges: $2\frac{1}{2} \times 3 \times 4$. Adding the edges does not find volume, dropping the $\frac{1}{2}$ changes the length, and adding the 4 at the end leaves out the height.

questions.skill: Counting unit cubes with fractional edges that fill a prism
questions.stem: A cube with 1-inch edges is filled with smaller cubes. Each small cube has an edge of $\frac{1}{2}$ inch. How many small cubes fill the large cube?
questions.solution: Along each 1-inch edge, 2 small cubes of $\frac{1}{2}$ inch fit. So the large cube holds $2 \times 2 \times 2 = 8$ small cubes.

questions.skill: Counting unit cubes with fractional edges that fill a prism
questions.stem: A cube with edges of 1 foot is filled exactly with small cubes whose edges are each $\frac{1}{3}$ foot. How many small cubes are needed?
questions.solution: Along each 1-foot edge, 3 small cubes fit. The large cube holds $3 \times 3 \times 3 = 27$ small cubes. The value 9 is one layer, 3 is one row, and $\frac{1}{27}$ is the volume of one small cube, not the number of cubes.

questions.skill: Choosing between surface area and volume, and their units
questions.stem: Mia wants to know how much wrapping paper she needs to cover a box. Which measure should she find?
choices: The surface area of the box
questions.answer: The surface area of the box
questions.solution: Wrapping paper covers the outside of the box, and the total area of all the faces is the surface area. Volume tells how much space is inside the box.

solve.answer: The surface area of the box

questions.skill: Choosing between surface area and volume, and their units
questions.stem: Which unit is best for measuring the volume of a rectangular prism?
questions.solution: Volume counts the cubes that fill a solid, so it is measured in cubic units such as cubic centimeters. Square centimeters measure area and centimeters measure length.

solve.work: Volume is in cubic units: cubic centimeters.

questions.skill: Choosing between surface area and volume, and their units
questions.stem: Which job needs a volume, not a surface area?
choices: Finding how much paint covers the outside of a shed
Finding how much sand fills a sandbox
Finding how much paper wraps a present
Finding how much cloth covers a box
questions.answer: Finding how much sand fills a sandbox
questions.solution: Filling a sandbox takes the space inside, which is volume. Painting a shed, wrapping a present and covering a box all cover an outside surface, which is surface area.

solve.answer: Finding how much sand fills a sandbox
solve.work: Filling a sandbox is volume; the others cover outsides (surface area).

questions.skill: Volume of a prism with fractional edges
questions.stem: A small cube has edges that are each $\frac{1}{2}$ inch long. What is its volume in cubic inches?
questions.solution: Volume is length times width times height: $\frac{1}{2} \times \frac{1}{2} \times \frac{1}{2} = \frac{1}{8}$ cubic inch.

questions.skill: Surface area of a rectangular prism
questions.stem: A rectangular prism is 6 centimeters long, 4 centimeters wide and 3 centimeters tall. What is its surface area in square centimeters?
questions.solution: There are three pairs of matching faces: $6 \times 4 = 24$, $6 \times 3 = 18$ and $4 \times 3 = 12$. Add them and double: $2 \times (24 + 18 + 12) = 108$ square centimeters.

questions.skill: Volume of a rectangular prism with fractional edges
questions.stem: A rectangular prism has a length of $2\frac{1}{2}$ feet, a width of $1\frac{1}{2}$ feet and a height of 2 feet. What is its volume in cubic feet?
questions.solution: Multiply the three edges: $\frac{5}{2} \times \frac{3}{2} \times 2 = \frac{30}{4} = 7\frac{1}{2}$ cubic feet.

questions.skill: Total area of the faces in a net
questions.stem: A net for a box has six rectangles: two that are 5 by 3, two that are 5 by 2 and two that are 3 by 2 (all measures in centimeters). What is the total area of the net in square centimeters?
questions.solution: Find the area of each kind of rectangle: $5 \times 3 = 15$, $5 \times 2 = 10$ and $3 \times 2 = 6$. There are two of each, so the total is $2 \times (15 + 10 + 6) = 62$ square centimeters. (31 counts each kind once, 30 is the volume, and 50 leaves out one pair of faces.)

questions.skill: Naming the solid a net folds into
questions.stem: Which set of shapes can be folded into a rectangular pyramid?
questions.solution: A rectangular pyramid has one rectangular base. Each of the 4 sides of the base is joined to one triangle, so it has 4 triangles. That makes 1 rectangle and 4 triangles. Two rectangles would make a second base, and 3 or 5 triangles would not match the 4 sides.

solve.work: Rectangular pyramid: 1 rectangular base + 1 triangle per side = 4 triangles.

questions.skill: Naming the solid a net folds into
questions.stem: One solid has a square base and all its other faces are triangles that meet at one point. A second solid has two triangular bases joined by three rectangles. Which pair of names matches the two solids?
questions.solution: A solid with one base and triangles meeting at a point is a pyramid, and its base is a square, so the first solid is a square pyramid. A solid with two matching triangle bases joined by rectangles is a triangular prism.

solve.work: Square base with triangles meeting at a point = square pyramid; 2 triangular bases + 3 rectangles = triangular prism.

questions.skill: Naming the solid a net folds into
questions.stem: A net is made of 1 pentagon and 5 triangles. What is the name of the solid it makes?
questions.solution: One base with triangles around it makes a pyramid. The base is a pentagon, which has 5 sides, and there is one triangle for each side. So the solid is a pentagonal pyramid.

questions.skill: Counting faces, edges and vertices of prisms and pyramids
questions.stem: Which statement about a pyramid is true?
choices: It has two bases that match
Every face except the base is a triangle
It has as many faces as its base has sides
questions.answer: Every face except the base is a triangle
questions.solution: A pyramid has one base, and its other faces are triangles that meet at one point. The two bases that match belong to a prism, whose side faces are rectangles. A pyramid has one more face than its base has sides, because the base is a face too.

solve.answer: Every face except the base is a triangle
solve.work: Pyramid: one base, lateral faces are triangles meeting at apex. True: every face except the base is a triangle. Others false (one base; sides not rectangles; faces = sides + 1).

questions.skill: Surface area of a cube
questions.stem: A cube-shaped storage box has edges that are each 12 inches long. How many square inches of plastic does it take to cover its whole outside surface?
questions.solution: One face is $12 \times 12 = 144$ square inches. The box has 6 faces, so the plastic covers $6 \times 144 = 864$ square inches.

questions.skill: Surface area of a cube
questions.stem: A large cube-shaped box has edges of 2.5 meters. What is its surface area, in square meters?
questions.solution: One face has an area of $2.5 \times 2.5 = 6.25$ square meters. There are 6 faces, so the surface area is $6 \times 6.25 = 37.5$ square meters. The number 15.625 is the volume, 25 uses only 4 faces and 15 is $6 \times 2.5$.

questions.skill: Surface area of a rectangular prism
questions.stem: A gift box is 12 inches long, 8 inches wide and 4 inches tall. How many square inches of wrapping paper are needed to cover the whole box with no overlap?
questions.solution: The faces are $12 \times 8 = 96$, $12 \times 4 = 48$ and $8 \times 4 = 32$ square inches, each twice. The paper needed is $2 \times (96 + 48 + 32) = 2 \times 176 = 352$ square inches.

questions.skill: Surface area of a rectangular prism
questions.stem: Ben finds the surface area of a box that is 7 centimeters long, 4 centimeters wide and 3 centimeters tall. He gets 84 square centimeters. What mistake did Ben make?
choices: He found the area of only the top and bottom
He found the volume instead of the surface area
He found the area of only the four side faces
He added the length, width and height
questions.answer: He found the volume instead of the surface area
questions.solution: Ben multiplied $7 \times 4 \times 3 = 84$, which is the volume. The surface area is $2 \times (28 + 21 + 12) = 122$ square centimeters. The top and bottom alone give 56, the four sides alone give 66, and adding the three edges gives 14, so none of those match his 84.

solve.answer: He found the volume instead of the surface area
solve.work: 7 x 4 x 3 = 84 = volume. True SA = 2(28+21+12) = 122; top+bottom 56; four sides 66; sum of dimensions 14. So he found the volume.

questions.skill: Surface area of a rectangular prism
questions.stem: A classroom is 8 meters long, 6 meters wide and 3 meters tall. The four walls will be painted. What is the total area of the walls, in square meters? (Ignore doors and windows.)
questions.solution: Two walls are $8 \times 3 = 24$ square meters each and two walls are $6 \times 3 = 18$ square meters each. The total is $2 \times 24 + 2 \times 18 = 48 + 36 = 84$ square meters. The number 132 also counts the ceiling, 180 counts all six faces, and 42 counts only one wall of each size.

questions.skill: Surface area of a rectangular prism
questions.stem: A rectangular prism is 8 centimeters long, 3 centimeters wide and 2 centimeters tall. What is its surface area, in square centimeters?
questions.solution: The faces are $8 \times 3 = 24$, $8 \times 2 = 16$ and $3 \times 2 = 6$ square centimeters, each twice. The surface area is $2 \times (24 + 16 + 6) = 2 \times 46 = 92$ square centimeters. The value 46 counts each pair once, 48 is the volume, and 44 leaves out the top and bottom.

questions.skill: Total area of the faces in a net
questions.stem: The net of a triangular prism has two right triangles with legs of 6 centimeters and 8 centimeters. It also has three rectangles that measure 6 by 12, 8 by 12 and 10 by 12 centimeters. What is the total area of the net, in square centimeters?
questions.solution: Each triangle has an area of $\frac{1}{2} \times 6 \times 8 = 24$ square centimeters, so the two triangles total 48. The rectangles are 72, 96 and 120, which total 288. The net has a total area of $48 + 288 = 336$ square centimeters.

solve.work: Triangles 2 x (1/2 x 6 x 8) = 48; rectangles 72 + 96 + 120 = 288; total 336.

questions.skill: Total area of the faces in a net
questions.stem: A net is made of 2 squares with sides of 3 centimeters and 4 rectangles that are each 3 centimeters by 7 centimeters. What is the total area of the net, in square centimeters?
questions.solution: Each square has an area of $3 \times 3 = 9$, so the two squares total 18. Each rectangle has an area of $3 \times 7 = 21$, so the four rectangles total 84. The net's area is $18 + 84 = 102$ square centimeters.

questions.skill: Surface area of a triangular prism
questions.stem: A tent is shaped like a triangular prism. Each triangular end has a base of 6 feet, a height of 4 feet and two slanted sides of 5 feet each. The tent is 9 feet long. How many square feet of fabric cover all five faces, including the floor?
questions.solution: Each triangular end has an area of $\frac{1}{2} \times 6 \times 4 = 12$ square feet, so the two ends total 24. Each slanted side is $5 \times 9 = 45$ square feet, so the two total 90. The floor is $6 \times 9 = 54$ square feet. The fabric needed is $24 + 90 + 54 = 168$ square feet.

solve.work: Ends 2 x (1/2 x 6 x 4) = 24; floor 6x9 = 54; slanted sides 2 x 5x9 = 90; total 168. (3-4-5 checks.)

questions.skill: Surface area of a triangular prism
questions.stem: A triangular prism has triangle ends with a base of 8 inches, a height of 3 inches and two other sides of 5 inches each. The prism is 10 inches long. What is its surface area, in square inches?
questions.solution: Each triangle has an area of $\frac{1}{2} \times 8 \times 3 = 12$ square inches, so the two triangles total 24. The three rectangles have a total area of $(8 + 5 + 5) \times 10 = 180$. The surface area is $24 + 180 = 204$ square inches. The value 180 leaves out the triangles, 192 counts only one triangle and 228 forgets the half in the triangle area.

solve.work: Ends 2 x (1/2 x 8 x 3) = 24; rectangles (8+5+5) x 10 = 180; total 204. (half-base 4, height 3, side 5: consistent.)

questions.skill: Surface area of a triangular prism
questions.stem: A box shaped like a triangular prism has right-triangle ends with legs of 5 centimeters and 12 centimeters and a longest side of 13 centimeters. The box is 20 centimeters long. What is the surface area of the box, in square centimeters?
questions.solution: Each triangle has an area of $\frac{1}{2} \times 5 \times 12 = 30$ square centimeters, so the two triangles total 60. The three rectangles have a total area of $(5 + 12 + 13) \times 20 = 600$. The surface area is $60 + 600 = 660$ square centimeters. The value 600 leaves out the triangles, 630 counts one triangle, and 720 forgets the half in the triangle area.

solve.work: Ends 2 x (1/2 x 5 x 12) = 60; rectangles (5+12+13) x 20 = 600; total 660.

questions.skill: Surface area of a pyramid
questions.stem: A square pyramid has a base with sides of 8 centimeters. Each of its four triangular faces has a base of 8 centimeters and a height of 5 centimeters. What is the surface area of the pyramid, in square centimeters?
questions.solution: The base has an area of $8 \times 8 = 64$ square centimeters. Each triangle has an area of $\frac{1}{2} \times 8 \times 5 = 20$, so the four triangles total 80. The surface area is $64 + 80 = 144$ square centimeters. The value 80 leaves out the base, 224 forgets the half in the triangle area and 84 counts only one triangle.

solve.work: Base 8x8 = 64; triangles 4 x (1/2 x 8 x 5) = 80; total 144.

questions.skill: Surface area of a pyramid
questions.stem: The roof of a gazebo is shaped like a square pyramid with no base. Each of its 4 triangular faces has a base of 10 feet and a height of 7 feet. What is the area of the roof, in square feet?
questions.solution: Each triangular face has an area of $\frac{1}{2} \times 10 \times 7 = 35$ square feet. The roof has 4 of them, so its area is $4 \times 35 = 140$ square feet.

questions.skill: Volume of a rectangular prism with whole-number edges
questions.stem: A moving box is 50 centimeters long, 30 centimeters wide and 40 centimeters tall. What is its volume, in cubic centimeters?
questions.solution: Volume is length times width times height: $50 \times 30 \times 40 = 1500 \times 40 = 60{,}000$ cubic centimeters.

questions.skill: Volume of a rectangular prism with whole-number edges
questions.stem: A rectangular prism is 7 inches long, 3 inches wide and 4 inches tall. What is its volume, in cubic inches?
questions.solution: Volume is length times width times height: $7 \times 3 \times 4 = 84$ cubic inches. The value 14 comes from adding the edges, 12 multiplies only two of them, and 122 is the surface area.

questions.skill: Volume of a rectangular prism with fractional edges
questions.stem: A rectangular prism is $\frac{1}{2}$ meter long, $\frac{3}{4}$ meter wide and 6 meters tall. What is its volume, in cubic meters?
questions.solution: Multiply the three edges: $\frac{1}{2} \times \frac{3}{4} \times 6 = \frac{3}{8} \times 6 = \frac{18}{8} = 2\frac{1}{4}$ cubic meters. The value $\frac{3}{8}$ leaves out the height, 3 leaves out the width, and $7\frac{1}{4}$ adds the three edges.

questions.skill: Volume of a rectangular prism with fractional edges
questions.stem: A closet is $3\frac{1}{2}$ feet wide, 2 feet deep and 7 feet tall. What volume does the closet enclose, in cubic feet?
questions.solution: Multiply the three edges: $3\frac{1}{2} \times 2 = 7$, and then $7 \times 7 = 49$ cubic feet.

questions.skill: Volume of a rectangular prism with fractional edges
questions.stem: A box is $\frac{1}{2}$ foot long, $\frac{1}{3}$ foot wide and 3 feet tall. What is its volume, in cubic feet?
questions.solution: Multiply the edges: $\frac{1}{2} \times \frac{1}{3} \times 3 = \frac{1}{6} \times 3 = \frac{1}{2}$ cubic foot. The value $\frac{1}{6}$ leaves out the height, $\frac{3}{2}$ leaves out the width, and $3\frac{5}{6}$ adds the edges.

questions.skill: Volume of a rectangular prism with fractional edges
questions.stem: A carton is 1.2 meters long, 0.5 meter wide and 0.5 meter tall. What is its volume, in cubic meters?
questions.solution: Multiply the three edges: $1.2 \times 0.5 = 0.6$, and then $0.6 \times 0.5 = 0.3$ cubic meter.

questions.skill: Counting unit cubes with fractional edges that fill a prism
questions.stem: A rectangular prism is 2 inches long, 1 inch wide and $\frac{3}{4}$ inch tall. It is filled exactly with cubes that have edges of $\frac{1}{4}$ inch. How many cubes fill it?
questions.solution: Each $\frac{1}{4}$-inch cube fits 4 times in one inch. Along the length there are $2 \times 4 = 8$ cubes and along the width there are $1 \times 4 = 4$. The height of $\frac{3}{4}$ inch is 3 cubes. The number of cubes is $8 \times 4 \times 3 = 96$.

questions.skill: Counting unit cubes with fractional edges that fill a prism
questions.stem: A box is 3 feet long, 2 feet wide and 1 foot tall. How many cubes with edges of $\frac{1}{2}$ foot fit in the box exactly?
questions.solution: Each foot holds 2 cubes of $\frac{1}{2}$ foot. The box holds $3 \times 2 = 6$ cubes along the length, $2 \times 2 = 4$ across the width and $1 \times 2 = 2$ up the height. That is $6 \times 4 \times 2 = 48$ cubes.

questions.skill: Finding a missing edge from a volume or surface area
questions.stem: A rectangular prism has a volume of 90 cubic inches. It is 6 inches long and 5 inches wide. How tall is it, in inches?
questions.solution: Volume is length times width times height. The base has an area of $6 \times 5 = 30$ square inches, so the height is $90 \div 30 = 3$ inches.

questions.skill: Finding a missing edge from a volume or surface area
questions.stem: The surface area of a cube is 96 square inches. How long is each edge, in inches?
questions.solution: A cube has 6 equal faces, so one face has an area of $96 \div 6 = 16$ square inches. A square with an area of 16 has sides of 4 inches, because $4 \times 4 = 16$. The value 16 is the area of one face, not the edge.

questions.skill: Choosing between surface area and volume, and their units
questions.stem: Which tells how much paint is needed to cover the outside of a cube-shaped box, and in what units?
questions.solution: Paint covers the outside faces, so the measure is surface area. Area is measured in square units. Volume is measured in cubic units and tells how much space is inside.

solve.work: Covering the outside = surface area, square units.

questions.skill: Comparing the surface areas or volumes of two solids
questions.stem: Prism A is 4 centimeters by 4 centimeters by 1 centimeter. Prism B is 2 centimeters by 4 centimeters by 2 centimeters. Which statement is true?
choices: The prisms have the same surface area because their volumes are equal
Prism B has the greater surface area
Prism A has the greater volume
Prism A has the greater surface area
questions.answer: Prism A has the greater surface area
questions.solution: Both volumes are 16 cubic centimeters. Prism A has a surface area of $2 \times (16 + 4 + 4) = 48$ square centimeters. Prism B has $2 \times (8 + 4 + 8) = 40$ square centimeters. So the volumes are equal, but Prism A has the greater surface area.

solve.answer: Prism A has the greater surface area
solve.work: A: V 16, SA 2(16+4+4) = 48. B: V 16, SA 2(8+4+8) = 40. A has greater SA; volumes equal.

questions.skill: Surface area of a rectangular prism
questions.stem: A closed box has a square base that measures 4 centimeters on each side. The box is 9 centimeters tall. What is its surface area in square centimeters?
questions.solution: The top and bottom are each $4 \times 4 = 16$, together 32. The four sides are each $4 \times 9 = 36$, together 144. The total is $32 + 144 = 176$ square centimeters. Leaving out the top and bottom gives 144, and counting only one of them gives 160.

solve.work: Two square faces: 2 x 16 = 32. Four side faces 4 x 9 = 36 each: 144. Total 176.

questions.skill: Surface area of a triangular prism
questions.stem: A triangular prism has two identical right-triangle bases with legs of 3 centimeters and 4 centimeters and a longest side of 5 centimeters. The prism is 10 centimeters long. What is its surface area in square centimeters?
questions.solution: The two triangular bases have area $2 \times \left(\frac{1}{2} \times 3 \times 4\right) = 12$. The three rectangular faces are $3 \times 10 = 30$, $4 \times 10 = 40$ and $5 \times 10 = 50$, which total $120$. The surface area is $12 + 120 = 132$ square centimeters.

solve.work: Two triangles: 2 x (1/2 x 3 x 4) = 12. Three rectangles: 3x10 + 4x10 + 5x10 = 120. Total 132.

questions.skill: Counting unit cubes with fractional edges that fill a prism
questions.stem: A box is 2 inches long, $1\frac{1}{2}$ inches wide and 1 inch tall. It is filled exactly with small cubes whose edges are each $\frac{1}{2}$ inch long. How many small cubes fill the box?
questions.solution: Count the cubes along each edge: $2 \div \frac{1}{2} = 4$ along the length, $1\frac{1}{2} \div \frac{1}{2} = 3$ along the width and $1 \div \frac{1}{2} = 2$ along the height. The number of cubes is $4 \times 3 \times 2 = 24$.

questions.skill: Surface area of a square pyramid from its faces
questions.stem: A square pyramid has a square base with sides of 6 centimeters. Its four triangular faces each have a base of 6 centimeters and a height of 5 centimeters. What is the surface area of the pyramid in square centimeters?
questions.solution: The base is $6 \times 6 = 36$. Each triangle is $\frac{1}{2} \times 6 \times 5 = 15$, so the four triangles are $60$. The total is $36 + 60 = 96$ square centimeters. (60 leaves out the base, 66 uses only one triangle, and 156 forgets the one half.)

solve.work: Base 6 x 6 = 36. Each triangle 1/2 x 6 x 5 = 15; four = 60. Total 96.

questions.skill: Naming the solid a net folds into
questions.stem: The net of a prism has 8 faces in all. What shape are the two bases of the prism?
questions.solution: A prism has 2 bases, and every other face is a rectangle joining one side of a base. So the number of rectangles equals the number of sides of a base. $8 - 2 = 6$ rectangles, so each base has 6 sides and is a hexagon.

solve.work: Prism faces = 2 bases + n rectangles. 2 + n = 8 so n = 6: hexagon.

questions.skill: Counting faces, edges and vertices of prisms and pyramids
questions.stem: A prism has 10 faces in all. How many sides does each of its two bases have?
questions.solution: A prism has 2 bases, and every other face is a rectangle joining one side of a base. The other $10 - 2 = 8$ faces are rectangles, so each base has 8 sides.

solve.work: 10 faces - 2 bases = 8 rectangles, so each base has 8 sides.

questions.skill: Surface area of a cube
questions.stem: A cube-shaped tank has no lid. Each edge is 3 meters long. How many square meters of glass are needed for its bottom and four sides?
questions.solution: Each face is $3 \times 3 = 9$ square meters. The bottom and four sides make 5 faces, so the glass needed is $5 \times 9 = 45$ square meters.

questions.skill: Surface area of a rectangular prism
questions.stem: An open box with no lid is 10 centimeters long, 6 centimeters wide and 4 centimeters tall. How many square centimeters of cardboard are needed to make it?
questions.solution: The cardboard covers the bottom and four sides. The bottom is $10 \times 6 = 60$. Two sides are $10 \times 4 = 40$ each and two sides are $6 \times 4 = 24$ each. The total is $60 + 80 + 48 = 188$ square centimeters. The number 248 includes a lid, 140 leaves out two sides and 128 leaves out the bottom.

solve.work: Bottom 10x6 = 60; long sides 2(10x4) = 80; short sides 2(6x4) = 48; total 188.

questions.skill: Surface area of a rectangular prism
questions.stem: A rectangular prism is 3.5 centimeters long, 2 centimeters wide and 1.5 centimeters tall. What is its surface area, in square centimeters?
questions.solution: The faces are $3.5 \times 2 = 7$, $3.5 \times 1.5 = 5.25$ and $2 \times 1.5 = 3$ square centimeters, each twice. The surface area is $2 \times (7 + 5.25 + 3) = 2 \times 15.25 = 30.5$ square centimeters. The value 15.25 counts each pair once, 10.5 is the volume, and 27.5 doubles only two of the three kinds of face.

questions.skill: Surface area of a rectangular prism
questions.stem: A low cabinet is 4 feet wide, 3 feet deep and 2 feet tall. Every face is painted except the bottom and the back. The back is the face that is 4 feet wide and 2 feet tall. How many square feet are painted?
questions.solution: All six faces together have an area of $2 \times (12 + 8 + 6) = 52$ square feet. The bottom is $4 \times 3 = 12$ square feet and the back is $4 \times 2 = 8$ square feet. The painted area is $52 - 12 - 8 = 32$ square feet.

solve.work: Top 4x3 = 12; front 4x2 = 8; two ends 3x2 = 6 each = 12. Bottom and back not painted. 12 + 8 + 12 = 32.

questions.skill: Total area of the faces in a net
questions.stem: The net of a closed box has a total area of 340 square centimeters. The top and the bottom are each 10 centimeters by 6 centimeters. What is the combined area of the four side faces, in square centimeters?
questions.solution: The top and the bottom each have an area of $10 \times 6 = 60$ square centimeters, so together they have 120. The four side faces make up the rest: $340 - 120 = 220$ square centimeters.

questions.skill: Surface area of a triangular prism
questions.stem: A triangular prism has right-triangle ends with legs of 1.5 centimeters and 2 centimeters and a longest side of 2.5 centimeters. The prism is 6 centimeters long. What is its surface area, in square centimeters?
questions.solution: Each triangle has an area of $\frac{1}{2} \times 1.5 \times 2 = 1.5$ square centimeters, so the two total 3. The rectangles have a total area of $(1.5 + 2 + 2.5) \times 6 = 36$. The surface area is $3 + 36 = 39$ square centimeters. The value 36 leaves out the triangles, 37.5 counts one triangle, and 42 forgets the half in the triangle area.

solve.work: Ends 2 x (1/2 x 1.5 x 2) = 3; rectangles (1.5+2+2.5) x 6 = 36; total 39.

questions.skill: Surface area of a triangular prism
questions.stem: The triangular ends of a prism each have a base of 10 centimeters, a height of 12 centimeters and two equal sides of 13 centimeters. The prism is 8 centimeters long. What is its surface area, in square centimeters?
questions.solution: Each triangular end has an area of $\frac{1}{2} \times 10 \times 12 = 60$ square centimeters, so the two ends total 120. The perimeter of the triangle is $10 + 13 + 13 = 36$ centimeters, so the three rectangles total $36 \times 8 = 288$. The surface area is $120 + 288 = 408$ square centimeters.

solve.work: Ends 2 x (1/2 x 10 x 12) = 120; rectangles (10+13+13) x 8 = 288; total 408. (5-12-13 consistent.)

questions.skill: Surface area of a triangular prism
questions.stem: The ends of a triangular prism are right triangles with legs of 9 centimeters and 12 centimeters and a longest side of 15 centimeters. The prism is 7.5 centimeters long. What is its surface area, in square centimeters?
questions.solution: Each triangle has an area of $\frac{1}{2} \times 9 \times 12 = 54$ square centimeters, so the two total 108. The triangle's perimeter is $9 + 12 + 15 = 36$ centimeters, so the three rectangles total $36 \times 7.5 = 270$. The surface area is $108 + 270 = 378$ square centimeters.

questions.skill: Surface area of a triangular prism
