questions.skill: Reading bar heights and totals in a histogram
questions.stem: A histogram of 20 values has these bars: 20 to 29, 3 values; 30 to 39, 9 values; 40 to 49, 6 values; 50 to 59, 2 values. Which statement is true?
choices: The histogram shows that 9 of the values are exactly 30
The most values are in the interval 40 to 49
There are only 4 values in the data set
15 of the 20 values are from 30 to 49
questions.answer: 15 of the 20 values are from 30 to 49
questions.solution: The bars for 30 to 39 and 40 to 49 hold $9 + 6 = 15$ values, so 15 of the 20 values are from 30 to 49. A histogram shows how many values are in an interval, not exact values. The tallest bar is 30 to 39, and there are 4 bars but 20 values.

solve.answer: 15 of the 20 values are from 30 to 49
solve.work: Total 3+9+6+2 = 20. 30-49: 9+6 = 15, true. Most values are in 30-39 (not 40-49); there are 20 values; a histogram cannot show exact values.

questions.skill: Reading bar heights and totals in a histogram
questions.stem: A histogram of the heights of 40 sunflowers has these bars: 100 to 119 cm, 6 sunflowers; 120 to 139 cm, 14 sunflowers; 140 to 159 cm, 12 sunflowers; 160 to 179 cm, 8 sunflowers. What percent of the sunflowers are 120 to 139 cm tall?
questions.solution: The bar for 120 to 139 cm has 14 of the 40 sunflowers. $\frac{14}{40} = \frac{35}{100} = 35\%$.

questions.skill: Placing values in histogram intervals
questions.stem: A coach records how many minutes 15 players practiced: 12, 25, 31, 8, 19, 22, 45, 30, 17, 28, 35, 41, 9, 26, 33. A histogram uses the intervals 0 to 9, 10 to 19, 20 to 29, 30 to 39 and 40 to 49. How many values are in the bar for 20 to 29?
questions.solution: The practice times from 20 to 29 are 25, 22, 28 and 26. That is 4 values, so the bar for 20 to 29 has height 4.

questions.skill: Placing values in histogram intervals
questions.stem: A histogram of lengths in centimeters uses the intervals 0 up to 5, 5 up to 10 and 10 up to 15. Each interval includes its left end but not its right end. A length of exactly 10 cm is counted in which bar?
choices: It is not counted in any bar
questions.solution: The interval 5 up to 10 does not include 10, because it leaves out its right end. The interval 10 up to 15 includes its left end, 10, so a length of exactly 10 cm goes in that bar.

solve.work: Intervals include the left end: 10 is in [10, 15), not in [5, 10).

questions.skill: Placing values in histogram intervals
questions.stem: A teacher's quiz scores run from 21 to 58. She makes a histogram with equal intervals of width 10 that start at 20: 20 to 29, 30 to 39, and so on. How many bars does the histogram need?
questions.solution: The scores need the intervals 20 to 29, 30 to 39, 40 to 49 and 50 to 59. The lowest score, 21, is in the first and the highest, 58, is in the last, so 4 bars are needed.

questions.skill: Describing the shape and spread of a histogram
questions.stem: A histogram has five bars. Their heights, from left to right, are 2, 4, 6, 9 and 12, and the smallest values are on the left. Which statement describes it?
choices: Skewed to the right, because the bars get taller toward the right
Skewed to the left: most values are large, with a tail toward smaller values
Symmetric, because the bars are in order
It has a gap in the middle
questions.answer: Skewed to the left: most values are large, with a tail toward smaller values
questions.solution: The tallest bar is on the far right, so most of the values are large, and the bars thin out toward the left. The tail points to the left, toward smaller values, so it is skewed to the left. Skew is named for the direction of the tail, not the tall bars.

solve.answer: Skewed to the left: most values are large, with a tail toward smaller values
solve.work: Heights rise to the right (peak at large values), so the tail is toward smaller values: skewed left. Option 3 is the common misconception; no gap; not symmetric.

questions.skill: Describing the shape and spread of a histogram
questions.stem: Which set of bar heights, from left to right, makes a histogram that is skewed to the right?
questions.solution: A histogram skewed to the right has its tall bars on the left and a tail toward the right. Heights 10, 7, 4, 2, 1 fall off to the right. The set 2, 5, 9, 5, 2 is symmetric, 1, 2, 4, 7, 10 is skewed to the left, and 6, 6, 6, 6, 6 is flat.

solve.work: 10,7,4,2,1: peak on the left, tail to the right = skewed right. 1,2,4,7,10 is skewed left; 2,5,9,5,2 symmetric; 6s flat.

questions.skill: Describing the shape and spread of a histogram
questions.stem: A histogram of 24 values has these bars: 0 to 9, 6 values; 10 to 19, 9 values; 20 to 29, 0 values; 30 to 39, 0 values; 40 to 49, 9 values. Which statement describes the data?
choices: There is one cluster and no gaps
All of the values are between 20 and 39
There are two clusters, separated by a gap from 20 to 39
The 9 values in the bar for 40 to 49 are an outlier
questions.answer: There are two clusters, separated by a gap from 20 to 39
questions.solution: Most of the values are in two groups: 0 to 19 and 40 to 49. The bars for 20 to 29 and 30 to 39 are empty, so there is a gap from 20 to 39. Nine values is far too many to be a single outlier.

solve.answer: There are two clusters, separated by a gap from 20 to 39
solve.work: Total 6+9+0+0+9 = 24. Values in 0-19 and 40-49 with empty bars 20-39: two clusters with a gap from 20 to 39. Nine values are a cluster, not an outlier.

questions.skill: Finding the median from a display
questions.stem: A dot plot shows the minutes that 10 students spent on a puzzle. The stacks of dots are: 4 minutes, 2 dots; 5 minutes, 3 dots; 6 minutes, 3 dots; 7 minutes, 2 dots. What is the median number of minutes?
questions.solution: List the 10 values in order: 4, 4, 5, 5, 5, 6, 6, 6, 7, 7. With 10 values, the median is halfway between the 5th and 6th values, 5 and 6. The median is $(5 + 6) \div 2 = 5.5$ minutes.

questions.skill: Finding the median from a display
questions.stem: A histogram shows 41 values. When the values are listed in order from least to greatest, the median is the value in which position? Count the smallest value as position 1.
questions.solution: With an odd number of values, the median is the middle one. There are 20 values below it and 20 above it, so it is in position $20 + 1 = 21$.

questions.skill: Finding the median from a display
questions.stem: A box plot is made from 60 different times, in minutes, and its median is 52. How many of the times are less than 52 minutes?
questions.solution: The median splits the ordered data in half. Half of the 60 times are below it, and the times are all different, so $60 \div 2 = 30$ times are less than 52 minutes.

solve.work: 60 distinct values: median is the mean of the 30th and 31st, which differ, so 52 lies strictly between them. 30 values are below 52.

questions.skill: Finding the five key values of a data set
questions.stem: The 12 ordered values of a data set are 3, 5, 6, 8, 9, 11, 12, 14, 15, 17, 18, 21. What is the third quartile?
questions.solution: The upper half is the last 6 values: 12, 14, 15, 17, 18, 21. Its median is halfway between the 3rd and 4th of these, 15 and 17, so the third quartile is $(15 + 17) \div 2 = 16$.

questions.skill: Finding the five key values of a data set
questions.stem: A park ranger counts the birds seen on 10 days: 28, 15, 22, 35, 18, 40, 25, 31, 20, 27. Which list gives the minimum, first quartile, median, third quartile and maximum, in that order?
questions.solution: Order the data: 15, 18, 20, 22, 25, 27, 28, 31, 35, 40. The median is halfway between 25 and 27, which is 26. The lower half 15, 18, 20, 22, 25 has median 20, and the upper half 27, 28, 31, 35, 40 has median 31. With the minimum 15 and the maximum 40, the list is 15, 20, 26, 31, 40.

questions.skill: Finding the five key values of a data set
questions.stem: Eight students scored 17, 9, 23, 12, 30, 15, 26, 20 on a quiz. What is the interquartile range (IQR) of the scores?
questions.solution: Order the scores: 9, 12, 15, 17, 20, 23, 26, 30. The lower half is 9, 12, 15, 17, with median $(12 + 15) \div 2 = 13.5$. The upper half is 20, 23, 26, 30, with median $(23 + 26) \div 2 = 24.5$. The IQR is $24.5 - 13.5 = 11$.

questions.skill: Reading range and IQR from a box plot
questions.stem: A box plot has a minimum of 5, a first quartile of 18, a median of 25, a third quartile of 29 and a maximum of 47. How much greater is the range than the interquartile range?
questions.solution: The range is $47 - 5 = 42$. The IQR is $29 - 18 = 11$. The range is $42 - 11 = 31$ greater than the IQR.

questions.skill: Reading range and IQR from a box plot
questions.stem: A box plot of the number of visitors to a museum each day has a minimum of 30, a first quartile of 45, a median of 50, a third quartile of 70 and a maximum of 72. Which statement is true?
questions.solution: The IQR is $70 - 45 = 25$, so the statement that the IQR is 25 is true. The range is $72 - 30 = 42$, not 25, the IQR is not 42, and the median is 50, not 70.

solve.work: IQR = 70-45 = 25; range = 72-30 = 42; median 50. Only "IQR is 25" is true.

questions.skill: Share of the data in a part of a box plot
questions.stem: A box plot is made from the scores of 80 students. The four parts of a box plot are minimum to first quartile, first quartile to median, median to third quartile, and third quartile to maximum. Each part holds one quarter of the scores. How many scores are between the median and the third quartile?
questions.solution: One quarter of the 80 scores are between the median and the third quartile: $80 \div 4 = 20$ scores.

questions.skill: Share of the data in a part of a box plot
questions.stem: A data set has 36 different values, and its first quartile is 40. How many of the values are less than 40?
questions.solution: One quarter of the values are below the first quartile: $36 \div 4 = 9$ values.

solve.work: 36 distinct values; lower half is 18 values; Q1 is the mean of the 9th and 10th, which differ, so 40 lies strictly between them: 9 values below 40 (one quarter of 36).

questions.skill: Comparing the center and spread of two displays
questions.stem: Team A's race times have a median of 12 minutes and a range of 8 minutes. Team B's race times have a median of 15 minutes and a range of 5 minutes. Which statement is true?
choices: Team B's typical time is greater, and its times are more spread out
Team A's typical time is greater, and its times are less spread out
The two teams' times are equally spread out
Team B's typical time is greater, but its times are less spread out
questions.answer: Team B's typical time is greater, but its times are less spread out
questions.solution: The median shows the center: 15 is greater than 12, so Team B's typical time is greater. The range shows the spread: 5 is less than 8, so Team B's times are less spread out.

solve.answer: Team B's typical time is greater, but its times are less spread out
solve.work: B median 15 > A median 12 (typical time greater); B range 5 < A range 8 (less spread out).

questions.skill: Comparing the center and spread of two displays
questions.stem: Set X is 12, 15, 18, 21, 24. Set Y is 10, 17, 18, 19, 26. Both sets have a median of 18. How much greater is the range of Set Y than the range of Set X?
questions.solution: The range of Set X is $24 - 12 = 12$. The range of Set Y is $26 - 10 = 16$. Set Y's range is $16 - 12 = 4$ greater.

questions.skill: Reading displays with unusual scales or layouts
questions.stem: A box plot is drawn standing up, so that larger values are higher on the page. The bottom whisker ends at 14, the bottom of the box is at 22, the line in the box is at 30, the top of the box is at 41 and the top whisker ends at 58. What is the interquartile range?
questions.solution: The box runs from the first quartile, 22, to the third quartile, 41. The IQR is $41 - 22 = 19$. Turning the box plot to stand up does not change how it is read.

solve.work: Box from Q1 = 22 to Q3 = 41: IQR = 19.

questions.skill: Reading displays with unusual scales or layouts
questions.stem: A dot plot has a number line labeled 0, 10, 20, 30 and 40, with one tick midway between each pair of labels. The stacks of dots are above the ticks for 15 (3 dots), 20 (2 dots) and 35 (1 dot). What is the range of the data?
questions.solution: The tick midway between 10 and 20 is 15, and the tick midway between 30 and 40 is 35. The smallest value is 15 and the largest is 35, so the range is $35 - 15 = 20$.

solve.work: Midway ticks are 5, 15, 25, 35. Data from 15 to 35: range 20.

questions.skill: Choosing a display and knowing what it shows
questions.stem: Which question can a histogram answer that a box plot cannot?
choices: How many values are in the interval 20 to 29?
questions.answer: How many values are in the interval 20 to 29?
questions.solution: The height of a histogram bar tells how many values are in its interval. A box plot shows the median, the quartiles and the IQR, but not how many values fall in a particular interval.

solve.answer: How many values are in the interval 20 to 29?
solve.work: A box plot shows Q3, the median and the IQR, but not counts in an interval; a histogram with that interval does.

questions.skill: Comparing the spread of two box plots
questions.stem: Class A's test scores have these five key values: smallest 50, first quartile 62, median 70, third quartile 78, largest 90. Class B's have: smallest 40, first quartile 60, median 70, third quartile 84, largest 100. How much greater is Class B's IQR than Class A's IQR?
questions.solution: Class A's IQR is $78 - 62 = 16$. Class B's IQR is $84 - 60 = 24$. The difference is $24 - 16 = 8$.

solve.work: Class A IQR = 78 - 62 = 16. Class B IQR = 84 - 60 = 24. Difference 24 - 16 = 8.

questions.skill: Counting the values in the tallest bar when building a histogram
questions.stem: Thirteen quiz scores are: 47, 52, 58, 61, 63, 65, 68, 72, 75, 79, 83, 88, 91. Jin makes a histogram with the bins 40 to 49, 50 to 59, 60 to 69, 70 to 79, 80 to 89 and 90 to 99. How many scores are in the tallest bar?
questions.solution: Count the scores in each bin: 40 to 49 has 1, 50 to 59 has 2, 60 to 69 has 4 (61, 63, 65, 68), 70 to 79 has 3, 80 to 89 has 2 and 90 to 99 has 1. The tallest bar is 60 to 69, with 4 scores.

questions.skill: Comparing center and spread of two dot plots
questions.stem: Plot A shows the values 5, 5, 6, 6, 6, 7, 7. Plot B shows the values 2, 4, 6, 6, 6, 8, 10. Which statement is true?
choices: Plot A has a greater median than Plot B
The two plots have the same range
Both have a median of 6, but Plot B is more spread out
Plot A is more spread out than Plot B
questions.answer: Both have a median of 6, but Plot B is more spread out
questions.solution: Both sets have 7 values and the middle (4th) value is 6, so both medians are 6. Plot A has a range of $7 - 5 = 2$ and Plot B has a range of $10 - 2 = 8$, so Plot B is more spread out.

solve.answer: Both have a median of 6, but Plot B is more spread out
solve.work: A: median 6 (4th of 7), range 7 - 5 = 2. B: median 6, range 10 - 2 = 8. Same median, B more spread out. Other options false.

questions.skill: Reading counts and totals from a dot plot
questions.stem: A dot plot shows the ages of 20 campers: 9 years, 2 dots; 10 years, 4 dots; 11 years, 6 dots; 12 years, 5 dots; 13 years, 3 dots. What percent of the campers are at least 12 years old?
questions.solution: "At least 12" means the stacks at 12 and 13 years: $5 + 3 = 8$ campers. Then $\frac{8}{20} = \frac{40}{100} = 40\%$.

questions.skill: Reading counts and totals from a dot plot
questions.stem: A dot plot shows how many hours of television 25 students watched yesterday. The stacks that can be read are: 0 hours, 4 dots; 1 hour, 7 dots; 3 hours, 6 dots; 4 hours, 3 dots. The stack above 2 hours is hidden, but the plot has 25 dots in all. How many dots are in the hidden stack?
questions.solution: The stacks that can be read hold $4 + 7 + 6 + 3 = 20$ dots. The plot has 25 dots in all, so the hidden stack has $25 - 20 = 5$ dots.

questions.skill: Clusters, gaps, peaks and outliers in a dot plot
questions.stem: A dot plot has one cluster of dots from 20 to 24, a gap from 25 to 29, and a second cluster from 30 to 32. Which list of values could it show?
questions.solution: All of the values must be 20 to 24 or 30 to 32, with none from 25 to 29. Only one list does that. One of the other lists has values at 26, 27 and 28, in the gap. Another has its second cluster at 40 to 42. The last has no values from 30 to 32 at all.

solve.work: Option 1: values 20-24, none 25-29, then 30-32. Option 2 second cluster is at 40-42; option 3 has 26-28 in the gap; option 4 has no second cluster.

questions.skill: Clusters, gaps, peaks and outliers in a dot plot
questions.stem: A dot plot shows these 8 values, with one dot for each: 4, 5, 5, 6, 7, 7, 7, 9. Which new dot, added to the plot, would leave the range of the data unchanged?
questions.solution: The range now is $9 - 4 = 5$. A dot at 8 lies between the smallest value, 4, and the largest, 9, so the range stays 5. A dot at 3 or at 10 or 12 would make the data stretch further, and the range would grow.

solve.work: Range = 9-4 = 5. A dot at 8 stays inside 4..9, range 5. Dots at 10, 3, 12 give ranges 6, 6, 8.

questions.skill: Constructing a dot plot from a list of data
questions.stem: A teacher lists the scores of 18 students on a 10-point quiz: 7, 9, 8, 7, 10, 9, 7, 6, 8, 9, 7, 10, 8, 9, 7, 5, 9, 8. She makes a dot plot with one dot for each student. For how many different scores will the dot plot have a stack of 3 or more dots?
questions.solution: Count each score: 5 appears once, 6 once, 7 five times, 8 four times, 9 five times and 10 twice. The scores 7, 8 and 9 each have 3 or more dots, so the answer is 3.

questions.skill: Constructing a dot plot from a list of data
questions.stem: A dot plot has these stacks of dots: 2, 2 dots; 3, 3 dots; 5, 1 dot; 6, 2 dots. Which list of values could NOT have been used to make this dot plot?
questions.solution: The plot needs two 2s, three 3s, one 5 and two 6s, which is 8 values and no others. The list 3, 2, 6, 3, 4, 2, 6, 3 has a 4 and no 5, so it cannot make this plot. The other three lists have exactly the right numbers of 2s, 3s, 5s and 6s.

solve.work: Plot: 2x2, 3x3, 5x1, 6x2. Option 1 has a 4 and no 5, so it could NOT make the plot. Options 2, 3, 4 each have two 2s, three 3s, one 5, two 6s.

questions.skill: Reading bar heights and totals in a histogram
questions.stem: A histogram of 25 test scores has these bars: 70 to 79, 6 scores; 80 to 89, 10 scores; 90 to 99, 9 scores. All scores are whole numbers. What is the smallest number of scores that could be above 85?
questions.solution: All 9 scores in the bar for 90 to 99 are above 85. The 10 scores in the bar for 80 to 89 could all be 85 or lower, since the histogram does not say exactly which values they are. So at least 9 scores are above 85, and 9 is the smallest possible number.

solve.work: All 9 scores in 90-99 are above 85. The 10 scores in 80-89 could all be 80-85, so none of them need be above 85. Smallest = 9.

questions.skill: Reading bar heights and totals in a histogram
questions.stem: A histogram of 34 values has five bars. The three tallest bars hold 10, 8 and 6 values. The other two bars are the same height. How many values are in each of the other two bars?
questions.solution: The three tallest bars hold $10 + 8 + 6 = 24$ values. That leaves $34 - 24 = 10$ values for the other two bars, which are equal, so each holds $10 \div 2 = 5$ values. This is shorter than the 6 of the third tallest bar, as it should be.

solve.work: 34-(10+8+6) = 10, split equally: 5 each (less than 6, so consistent with the three tallest).

questions.skill: Placing values in histogram intervals
questions.stem: Twenty students recorded the minutes they walked to school: 14, 22, 5, 31, 18, 27, 9, 36, 12, 24, 3, 19, 28, 41, 16, 25, 7, 33, 21, 11. A histogram uses the intervals 0 to 9, 10 to 19, 20 to 29, 30 to 39 and 40 to 49. How many more values are in the tallest bar than in the shortest bar?
questions.solution: Sort the times into the intervals. 0 to 9 has 4 values, 10 to 19 has 6, 20 to 29 has 6, 30 to 39 has 3 and 40 to 49 has 1. The tallest bar has 6 values and the shortest has 1, so the difference is $6 - 1 = 5$.

solve.issues: Minor wording: two bars (10-19 and 20-29) tie as tallest at 6, so "the tallest bar" is not unique; the difference 6-1 = 5 is unaffected.

questions.skill: Placing values in histogram intervals
questions.stem: These 12 values are put in a histogram with the intervals 0 to 4, 5 to 9, 10 to 14 and 15 to 19: 2, 8, 14, 9, 3, 11, 5, 17, 9, 12, 6, 10. Which list gives the bar heights, from the first interval to the last?
questions.solution: Sort each value into its interval. 0 to 4: 2 and 3. 5 to 9: 8, 9, 5, 9 and 6. 10 to 14: 14, 11, 12 and 10. 15 to 19: 17. The heights are 2, 5, 4 and 1, which add to 12. The other lists do not count every value, or put a value in the wrong bar.

questions.skill: Describing the shape and spread of a histogram
questions.stem: A histogram of 20 ages has these bars: 0 to 9, 2; 10 to 19, 9; 20 to 29, 6; 30 to 39, 2; 40 to 49, 1. Which statement is true?
choices: It is skewed to the right, and 15 of the 20 ages are from 10 to 29
It is skewed to the left, and 15 of the 20 ages are from 10 to 29
It is skewed to the right, and 9 of the 20 ages are from 10 to 29
It is symmetric, and 15 of the 20 ages are from 10 to 29
questions.answer: It is skewed to the right, and 15 of the 20 ages are from 10 to 29
questions.solution: The bars for 10 to 19 and 20 to 29 hold $9 + 6 = 15$ ages. The peak is in the second bar and the bars thin out to the right (6, 2, 1) much more slowly than to the left (2), so the long tail is on the right: skewed to the right.

solve.answer: It is skewed to the right, and 15 of the 20 ages are from 10 to 29
solve.work: Total 2+9+6+2+1 = 20. Peak at 10-19, tail 6,2,1 to the right: skewed right. 10-29: 9+6 = 15. Option 1.

questions.skill: Describing the shape and spread of a histogram
questions.stem: A histogram of exam scores uses the intervals 40 to 49, 50 to 59, 60 to 69, 70 to 79, 80 to 89 and 90 to 99. The first bar that holds any scores is 50 to 59, and the last bar that holds any scores is 80 to 89. All scores are whole numbers. What is the greatest possible range of the scores?
questions.solution: The range is largest when the lowest score is as low as possible, 50, and the highest score is as high as possible, 89. The greatest possible range is $89 - 50 = 39$.

solve.work: Smallest possible score 50, largest possible 89: range 89-50 = 39.

questions.skill: Describing the shape and spread of a histogram
questions.stem: A histogram has these bars: 0 to 9, 0 values; 10 to 19, 3 values; 20 to 29, 9 values; 30 to 39, 8 values; 40 to 49, 0 values. All the values are whole numbers. What is the least possible range of the data?
questions.solution: The smallest value is in the bar for 10 to 19, and the largest is in the bar for 30 to 39. The range is smallest when the lowest value is as high as possible, 19, and the highest value is as low as possible, 30. The least possible range is $30 - 19 = 11$.

solve.work: Minimum is in 10-19 (at most 19), maximum is in 30-39 (at least 30). Least range = 30-19 = 11.

questions.skill: Finding the median from a display
questions.stem: A dot plot of the number of visitors to a library each hour, over 24 hours, has these stacks of dots: 0 visitors, 4 dots; 1 visitor, 8 dots; 2 visitors, 4 dots; 3 visitors, 4 dots; 4 visitors, 3 dots; 5 visitors, 1 dot. What is the median number of visitors?
questions.solution: There are 24 values, so the median is halfway between the 12th and 13th values. The stacks hold 4 values at 0 and then 8 at 1, so the first 12 values are 0s and 1s and the 12th value is 1. The 13th value is the first one at 2. The median is $(1 + 2) \div 2 = 1.5$.

questions.skill: Finding the median from a display
questions.stem: A histogram of 29 values has these bars: 0 to 9, 12 values; 10 to 19, 5 values; 20 to 29, 4 values; 30 to 39, 4 values; 40 to 49, 4 values. Dana says the median must be in the tallest bar. Which statement is correct?
choices: Dana is right: the median is in 0 to 9, which is the tallest bar
Dana is wrong: the median is in 20 to 29, the middle bar
Dana is right, because the median is the value that occurs most often
Dana is wrong: the tallest bar is 0 to 9, but the median is in 10 to 19
questions.answer: Dana is wrong: the tallest bar is 0 to 9, but the median is in 10 to 19
questions.solution: With 29 values, the median is the 15th value in order. The bar for 0 to 9 holds the first 12 values, and the bar for 10 to 19 holds values 13 to 17, so the 15th value is in 10 to 19. The tallest bar is 0 to 9, so Dana is wrong. The median is the middle value, not the most common one.

solve.answer: Dana is wrong: the tallest bar is 0 to 9, but the median is in 10 to 19
solve.work: Total 12+5+4+4+4 = 29; median is the 15th value. 0-9 holds positions 1-12, 10-19 holds 13-17, so the median is in 10-19, not the tallest bar 0-9.

questions.skill: Finding the five key values of a data set
questions.stem: Here are 15 numbers of minutes, in the order they were collected: 21, 6, 15, 28, 9, 13, 19, 4, 25, 10, 16, 7, 23, 12, 18. When finding the quartiles, leave the median out and use the 7 values below it and the 7 values above it. What is the interquartile range (IQR)?
questions.solution: Order the data: 4, 6, 7, 9, 10, 12, 13, 15, 16, 18, 19, 21, 23, 25, 28. The median is the 8th value, 15. The 7 values below it are 4, 6, 7, 9, 10, 12, 13, with middle value 9, so the first quartile is 9. The 7 values above it are 16, 18, 19, 21, 23, 25, 28, with middle value 21, so the third quartile is 21. The IQR is $21 - 9 = 12$.

questions.skill: Finding the five key values of a data set
questions.stem: Sixteen runners finished a race in these ordered times, in minutes: 12, 14, 15, 16, 18, 19, 20, 22, 24, 25, 27, 28, 30, 33, 35, 40. Which list gives the minimum, first quartile, median, third quartile and maximum, in that order?
questions.solution: The median is halfway between the 8th and 9th values, 22 and 24, so it is 23. The lower half has 8 values, and its median is halfway between 16 and 18, which is 17. The upper half has 8 values, and its median is halfway between 28 and 30, which is 29. With the minimum 12 and the maximum 40, the list is 12, 17, 23, 29, 40.

questions.skill: Finding the five key values of a data set
questions.stem: The ordered scores of 8 players are 5, 8, 10, a missing score, 16, 19, 22 and 30. The median score is 14. What is the missing score?
questions.solution: With 8 scores, the median is halfway between the 4th and 5th scores, which are the missing score and 16. So the missing score plus 16 is $2 \times 14 = 28$, and the missing score is $28 - 16 = 12$. This fits, since 12 is between 10 and 16.

solve.work: Median = (missing + 16)/2 = 14, so missing = 12, which fits between 10 and 16.

questions.skill: Reading range and IQR from a box plot
questions.stem: A box plot has an interquartile range of 14. Its first quartile is 31, its median is 37, and its whiskers run from 22 to 60. What is the third quartile?
questions.solution: The IQR is the third quartile minus the first quartile, so the third quartile is the first quartile plus the IQR: $31 + 14 = 45$.

solve.work: Q3 = Q1 + IQR = 31 + 14 = 45 (between median 37 and max 60).

questions.skill: Reading range and IQR from a box plot
questions.stem: A data set has 12 values. Its largest value is changed from 50 to 80, and it is still the largest value. Which of these changes?
questions.solution: The range is the largest value minus the smallest, so it grows by 30. The median is found from the 6th and 7th values, and the quartiles from the middle values of each half: the 3rd and 4th values, and the 9th and 10th values. None of those is the largest value, so the median, the quartiles and the IQR stay the same.

solve.work: With 12 values, Q1 uses 3rd/4th, median 6th/7th, Q3 9th/10th; the 12th value only affects the maximum, so only the range changes.

questions.skill: Share of the data in a part of a box plot
questions.stem: A box plot is made from 52 different values. How many of the values are greater than the first quartile?
questions.solution: One quarter of the values, $52 \div 4 = 13$, are less than the first quartile. The other three quarters are greater: $52 - 13 = 39$ values.

solve.work: 52 distinct values; lower half 26; Q1 is the mean of the 13th and 14th, strictly between them. 13 values are below Q1, so 52-13 = 39 are greater.

questions.skill: Share of the data in a part of a box plot
questions.stem: In a box plot, the first quartile is 20, the median is 24 and the third quartile is 40. Which statement is true?
choices: More values lie from 24 to 40 than from 20 to 24
The values from 24 to 40 are more spread out than the values from 20 to 24
Half of the values lie from 20 to 24
The median is halfway between the two quartiles
questions.answer: The values from 24 to 40 are more spread out than the values from 20 to 24
questions.solution: The part of the box from 20 to 24 and the part from 24 to 40 each hold one quarter of the values. The second part is 16 units long and the first is only 4 units long, so the same number of values is spread over a longer stretch. The median, 24, is closer to 20 than to 40, so it is not halfway between them.

solve.answer: The values from 24 to 40 are more spread out than the values from 20 to 24
solve.work: Each of 20-24 and 24-40 holds about a quarter of the values, but 24-40 is wider (16 vs 4), so those values are more spread out. Not half in 20-24; not more values; halfway would be 30.

questions.skill: Share of the data in a part of a box plot
questions.stem: In a box plot, exactly one quarter of the values are above the third quartile. Kayla counts 15 values above the third quartile. How many values are in the data set?
questions.solution: The 15 values are one quarter of the data, so the whole data set is 4 times as large: $15 \times 4 = 60$ values.

solve.work: 15 is one quarter, so the total is 15 x 4 = 60.

questions.skill: Comparing the center and spread of two displays
questions.stem: Class A's scores have a minimum of 60, a first quartile of 70, a median of 75, a third quartile of 80 and a maximum of 90. Class B's scores have a minimum of 40, a first quartile of 65, a median of 75, a third quartile of 78 and a maximum of 95. Which statement is true?
choices: Class A's scores are more spread out, with a greater range and a greater IQR
The classes have the same spread because they have the same median
Class B's scores are more spread out, with a greater range and a greater IQR
Class B's scores are less spread out because its maximum is greater
questions.answer: Class B's scores are more spread out, with a greater range and a greater IQR
questions.solution: Class A's range is $90 - 60 = 30$ and its IQR is $80 - 70 = 10$. Class B's range is $95 - 40 = 55$ and its IQR is $78 - 65 = 13$. Class B has both the greater range and the greater IQR, so its scores are more spread out. The same median only means the same center.

solve.answer: Class B's scores are more spread out, with a greater range and a greater IQR
solve.work: A: range 90-60 = 30, IQR 80-70 = 10. B: range 95-40 = 55, IQR 78-65 = 13. B is more spread on both.

questions.skill: Comparing the center and spread of two displays
questions.stem: Dot plot X has one dot at each of these values: 10, 12, 14, 14, 16, 18, 19. Dot plot Y has one dot at each of these values: 7, 8, 9, 10, 11, 12. How much greater is the median of X than the median of Y?
questions.solution: X has 7 values, so its median is the 4th value, 14. Y has 6 values, so its median is halfway between the 3rd and 4th values, 9 and 10, which is 9.5. The difference is $14 - 9.5 = 4.5$.

solve.work: X (7 values) median = 4th = 14. Y (6 values) median = (9+10)/2 = 9.5. 14-9.5 = 4.5.

questions.skill: Comparing the center and spread of two displays
questions.stem: Two histograms use the same five intervals, and each shows 20 values. Histogram P has bar heights 2, 5, 6, 5 and 2, from left to right. Histogram Q has bar heights 8, 2, 0, 2 and 8. Which statement is true?
choices: P is more spread out, because its bars are taller in the middle
Q is more spread out, because more of its values are in the outer bars
P and Q have the same spread, because they have the same intervals
Q is less spread out, because its middle bar is empty
questions.answer: Q is more spread out, because more of its values are in the outer bars
questions.solution: In P, 12 of the 20 values are in the three middle bars and only 4 are in the two outer bars. In Q, 16 of the 20 values are in the outer bars, so many values are far from the middle. That makes Q more spread out. Having the same intervals does not make the spread the same.

solve.answer: Q is more spread out, because more of its values are in the outer bars
solve.work: P (2,5,6,5,2) piles values in the middle; Q (8,2,0,2,8) puts 16 of 20 in the outer bars, far from the centre, so Q is more spread out.

questions.skill: Comparing the center and spread of two displays
questions.stem: Box plot A has a minimum of 10, a first quartile of 18, a median of 25, a third quartile of 33 and a maximum of 40. Box plot B has a first quartile of 14 and an interquartile range twice as large as A's. What is B's third quartile?
questions.solution: A's IQR is $33 - 18 = 15$. B's IQR is twice that, $2 \times 15 = 30$. B's third quartile is its first quartile plus its IQR: $14 + 30 = 44$.

questions.skill: Reading displays with unusual scales or layouts
questions.stem: A line plot of the lengths of 11 leaves, in centimeters, uses a number line marked every 0.5. The stacks of dots are: 2.5 cm, 1 dot; 3 cm, 2 dots; 3.5 cm, 4 dots; 4 cm, 3 dots; 6.5 cm, 1 dot. What is the median length, in centimeters?
questions.solution: With 11 values, the median is the 6th value in order. The first stack gives value 1 (2.5 cm), the next stack gives values 2 and 3 (3 cm), and the next gives values 4 to 7 (3.5 cm). So the 6th value is 3.5 cm.

questions.skill: Reading displays with unusual scales or layouts
questions.stem: A histogram of the weights of 80 puppies has a vertical scale labeled "percent of puppies" instead of a count. The four bars read 10%, 25%, 40% and 25%. How many more puppies are in the tallest bar than in the shortest bar?
questions.solution: The tallest bar is 40% of 80 puppies, which is $0.4 \times 80 = 32$ puppies. The shortest bar is 10% of 80, which is $0.1 \times 80 = 8$ puppies. The difference is $32 - 8 = 24$ puppies.

solve.work: Bars sum to 100%. Tallest 40% = 32 puppies, shortest 10% = 8; 32-8 = 24.

questions.skill: Choosing a display and knowing what it shows
questions.stem: A box plot has a minimum of 12, a first quartile of 20, a median of 25, a third quartile of 31 and a maximum of 40. Which of these can NOT be found from the box plot alone?
choices: The number of values in the data set
questions.answer: The number of values in the data set
questions.solution: The range is $40 - 12 = 28$, the IQR is $31 - 20 = 11$, and the median is 25. A box plot shows only five key values, and data sets of different sizes can have the same five key values, so it does not show how many values there are.

solve.answer: The number of values in the data set
solve.work: The five-number summary gives range (28), median (25), IQR (11), but not how many values there are.

questions.skill: Finding a mean
questions.stem: What is the mean of the numbers 4, 6, 8, 10 and 12?
questions.solution: Add the numbers: $4 + 6 + 8 + 10 + 12 = 40$. Divide by how many there are: $40 \div 5 = 8$.

questions.skill: Finding a median of an unordered list
questions.stem: What is the median of the numbers 9, 3, 12, 5 and 6?
questions.solution: Put the numbers in order: 3, 5, 6, 9, 12. The middle number is 6. (7 is the mean, 12 is the middle of the unordered list, and 9 is the range.)

questions.skill: The mean as a fair share
questions.stem: Four friends have 3, 5, 6 and 10 stickers. They put all the stickers together and share them equally. How many stickers does each friend get?
questions.solution: There are $3 + 5 + 6 + 10 = 24$ stickers in all. Shared equally among 4 friends, each gets $24 \div 4 = 6$ stickers. This is the mean.

solve.work: Total 3 + 5 + 6 + 10 = 24; 24 / 4 = 6 each (the mean as fair share).

questions.skill: The mean as a balance point or fair share
questions.stem: Three baskets hold 4, 7 and 10 apples. Apples are moved from basket to basket until every basket holds the same number. How many apples are in each basket?
questions.solution: Together there are $4 + 7 + 10 = 21$ apples. Shared equally among 3 baskets, each holds $21 \div 3 = 7$ apples. This equal share is the mean.

questions.skill: The mean as a balance point or fair share
questions.stem: Which statement describes the mean of a data set as its balance point?
choices: The mean is the value that appears most often in the data set
The mean is the middle value when the data are put in order
The total distance of the values above the mean equals the total distance of the values below the mean
The mean is the distance from the least value to the greatest value
questions.answer: The total distance of the values above the mean equals the total distance of the values below the mean
questions.solution: If the data were weights on a see-saw, the mean is the point where it balances: the distances of the values above it add up to the same total as the distances of the values below it. The value that appears most often is the mode, the middle value is the median, and the distance from the least to the greatest value is the range.

solve.answer: The total distance of the values above the mean equals the total distance of the values below the mean
solve.work: The balance-point view: the sum of distances above the mean equals the sum of distances below it. The others describe median, mode, range.

questions.skill: The mean as a balance point or fair share
questions.stem: Four stacks of 1, 3, 5 and 7 cubes are leveled so that every stack is the same height. How many cubes are in each stack?
questions.solution: There are $1 + 3 + 5 + 7 = 16$ cubes in all. Four equal stacks hold $16 \div 4 = 4$ cubes each.

questions.skill: The mean as a balance point or fair share
questions.stem: A data set has a mean of 8. One value in the set is 5. How many units below the mean is that value?
questions.solution: The value 5 is $8 - 5 = 3$ units below the mean of 8.

questions.skill: The mean as a balance point or fair share
questions.stem: A data set has the values 2, 6 and 10, and its mean is 6. Which statement is true?
choices: The 2 is 4 below the mean and the 10 is 6 above it, so they balance each other
The 2 is 4 below the mean and the 10 is 4 above it, so they balance each other
The 2 is 6 below the mean and the 10 is 4 above it, so they balance each other
The 2 and the 10 are both 4 above the mean, so they balance each other
questions.answer: The 2 is 4 below the mean and the 10 is 4 above it, so they balance each other
questions.solution: $6 - 2 = 4$, so the 2 is 4 below the mean. $10 - 6 = 4$, so the 10 is 4 above the mean. Equal distances on the two sides balance each other. The 6 itself is exactly at the mean.

solve.answer: The 2 is 4 below the mean and the 10 is 4 above it, so they balance each other
solve.work: 2 is 6-2 = 4 below; 10 is 10-6 = 4 above; they balance. Third option.

questions.skill: Finding a mean
questions.stem: Find the mean of the numbers 3, 8, 4 and 9.
questions.solution: Add the numbers: $3 + 8 + 4 + 9 = 24$. Divide by how many numbers there are: $24 \div 4 = 6$.

questions.skill: Finding a mean
questions.stem: Rosa read 12, 15 and 18 pages on three nights. What was the mean number of pages she read per night?
questions.solution: She read $12 + 15 + 18 = 45$ pages in 3 nights. The mean is $45 \div 3 = 15$ pages per night.

questions.skill: Finding a mean
questions.stem: Which expression gives the mean of 6, 10 and 14?
questions.solution: To find a mean, add all the values and divide by how many values there are. There are 3 values, so the mean is $\frac{6+10+14}{3} = 10$.

solve.work: Mean = sum of the 3 values divided by 3: (6+10+14)/3.

questions.skill: Finding a mean
questions.stem: The high temperatures on four days were 70, 74, 76 and 80 degrees. What was the mean high temperature, in degrees?
questions.solution: The temperatures add up to $70 + 74 + 76 + 80 = 300$. Dividing by 4 days gives $300 \div 4 = 75$ degrees.

questions.skill: Finding a mean
questions.stem: A student's five quiz scores out of 10 were 8, 10, 10, 9 and 8. What is the mean score?
questions.solution: The scores add up to $8 + 10 + 10 + 9 + 8 = 45$. Divide by 5 quizzes: $45 \div 5 = 9$.

questions.skill: Finding a mean
questions.stem: Which number is the mean of 10, 20, 30 and 80?
questions.solution: The numbers add up to $10 + 20 + 30 + 80 = 140$, and $140 \div 4 = 35$. The number 25 is the median, 140 is the total, and 28 comes from dividing by 5 instead of 4.

questions.skill: Finding a median
questions.stem: The ages of five cousins are 8, 9, 11, 12 and 15. What is the median age?
questions.solution: The ages are already in order. The middle of 5 values is the 3rd value, which is 11.

questions.skill: Finding a median
questions.stem: Which number is the median of 11, 3, 14, 5 and 8?
questions.solution: Put the numbers in order: 3, 5, 8, 11, 14. The median is the middle one, 8. The number 14 is what you get by picking the middle of the list as written, 8.2 is the mean, and 11 is just the first number listed.

questions.skill: Finding a median
questions.stem: Seven students' scores, in order, were 3, 3, 4, 6, 7, 9 and 10. What is the median score?
questions.solution: With 7 values in order, the median is the 4th value, which is 6.

questions.skill: Finding a median
questions.stem: What is the median of 2, 4, 6 and 8?
questions.solution: There are 4 numbers, so the median is halfway between the two middle ones, 4 and 6: $(4 + 6) \div 2 = 5$.

questions.skill: Finding a median
questions.stem: Which number is the median of the data 15, 15, 16, 18 and 20?
questions.solution: The data are in order and there are 5 values, so the median is the 3rd value, 16. The number 15 appears most often, and 16.8 is the mean.

questions.skill: Finding a median
questions.stem: Nine plants have heights, in centimeters, of 4, 5, 5, 6, 7, 8, 8, 9 and 12. What is the median height, in centimeters?
questions.solution: With 9 values in order, the median is the 5th value. Counting 4, 5, 5, 6, 7 gives 7.

questions.skill: Using a mean to find a missing value or a total
questions.stem: The mean of 3 numbers is 10. Two of the numbers are 8 and 12. What is the third number?
questions.solution: Three numbers with a mean of 10 add up to $3 \times 10 = 30$. The two known numbers add up to $8 + 12 = 20$, so the third is $30 - 20 = 10$.

questions.skill: Using a mean to find a missing value or a total
questions.stem: Four friends have a mean of 6 stickers each. How many stickers do they have in all?
questions.solution: Mean $\times$ number of friends gives the total: $4 \times 6 = 24$ stickers.

questions.skill: Using a mean to find a missing value or a total
questions.stem: Tom's mean score on 2 quizzes is 9. His first score is 8. What is his second score?
questions.solution: Two scores with a mean of 9 add up to $2 \times 9 = 18$. His first score is 8, so the second is $18 - 8 = 10$.

questions.skill: How adding, removing or changing a value affects the mean and median
questions.stem: Priya's quiz scores are 7, 8 and 9, and her mean is 8. On her next quiz she scores 10. What happens to her mean?
questions.solution: The new score of 10 is greater than the old mean of 8, so it pulls the mean up. The new mean is $(7 + 8 + 9 + 10) \div 4 = 8.5$.

solve.work: New total 34 over 4 = 8.5 > 8, so it goes up.

questions.skill: How adding, removing or changing a value affects the mean and median
questions.stem: Every value in a data set is increased by 5. The mean of the old data set was 12. What is the mean of the new data set?
questions.solution: Adding 5 to every value moves the balance point up by 5 too, so the new mean is $12 + 5 = 17$.

solve.work: Adding 5 to every value adds 5 to the mean: 17.

questions.skill: How adding, removing or changing a value affects the mean and median
questions.stem: The median of the five ages 14, 18, 21, 25 and 32 is 21. If the 32 is changed to 90, what is the new median?
questions.solution: The middle value is still the 3rd one in order, 21. Changing the greatest value does not change which value is in the middle, so the median stays 21.

questions.skill: Comparing the variability of two data sets
questions.stem: A data set is 12, 18, 7, 25 and 14. What is its range?
questions.solution: The range is the greatest value minus the least value: $25 - 7 = 18$.

questions.skill: Comparing the variability of two data sets
questions.stem: Which data set is the most spread out?
questions.solution: The ranges are $80 - 5 = 75$, $43 - 40 = 3$, $35 - 20 = 15$ and $40 - 10 = 30$. The set with the greatest range, 75, is the most spread out.

solve.work: Ranges 30, 15, 75, 3 (equally spaced sets, so any spread measure agrees). Most spread: 5, 30, 55, 80.

questions.skill: Comparing the variability of two data sets
questions.stem: The tallest tree in a park is 31 feet high and the shortest is 12 feet high. What is the range of the tree heights, in feet?
questions.solution: The range is the greatest value minus the least value: $31 - 12 = 19$ feet.

questions.skill: Choosing the best measure of center
questions.stem: Aiden's test scores are 80, 82, 84, 85 and 86. None of the scores is unusually high or low. Which statement is true?
choices: Only the median can describe a typical score
Only the mean can describe a typical score
Neither the mean nor the median can describe a typical score
Both the mean and the median describe a typical score well
questions.answer: Both the mean and the median describe a typical score well
questions.solution: The scores are close together, with no unusual value, so the mean (83.4) and the median (84) are close and both describe a typical score well.

solve.answer: Both the mean and the median describe a typical score well
solve.work: Mean 417/5 = 83.4, median 84; no outlier, so both describe a typical score well.

questions.skill: Choosing the best measure of center
questions.stem: Five students get weekly allowances, in dollars, of 5, 6, 6, 7 and 40. Which measure of center better describes a typical allowance, and why?
choices: The median, because the 40 is much greater than the other values and pulls the mean up
The mean, because every value counts and the 40 shows what is typical
The mean, because it is the middle value of the data
The median, because it is the average of all the values
questions.answer: The median, because the 40 is much greater than the other values and pulls the mean up
questions.solution: The median is 6, which is close to most allowances. The mean is 12.8, pulled up by the single value 40, so it describes none of the students well. The median is the middle value; the mean is the average of all the values.

solve.answer: The median, because the 40 is much greater than the other values and pulls the mean up
solve.work: Mean 64/5 = 12.8, pulled up by 40; median 6 is typical. Second option.

questions.skill: Choosing the best measure of center
questions.stem: Which of these is changed the least when one extremely large value is added to a data set?
choices: The total of all the values
questions.solution: One extremely large value adds a lot to the total, so it moves the mean and the range a lot. The median is only the middle value, so it moves very little.

solve.work: An extreme value changes range, mean and total a lot; the median shifts at most by half a step between neighbours.

questions.skill: Choosing the best measure of center
questions.stem: Which of these is the middle value of a data set when the values are put in order?
questions.solution: The median is the middle value when the data are in order. The mean is the total divided by the number of values, and the range is the greatest value minus the least.

questions.skill: Median of an even number of values
questions.stem: What is the median of the numbers 25, 12, 30, 18, 15 and 20?
questions.solution: Put the numbers in order: 12, 15, 18, 20, 25, 30. With six numbers, the median is halfway between the two middle ones: $(18 + 20) \div 2 = 19$.

questions.skill: Finding a missing value from a mean
questions.stem: Dev took five tests and his mean score was 82. His first four scores were 78, 85, 90 and 80. What was his fifth score?
questions.solution: A mean of 82 over 5 tests means the total is $5 \times 82 = 410$. The first four scores add to $78 + 85 + 90 + 80 = 333$. The fifth score is $410 - 333 = 77$.

solve.work: Total needed 5 x 82 = 410. First four: 78 + 85 + 90 + 80 = 333. Fifth = 410 - 333 = 77.

questions.skill: Choosing the better measure of center when there is an outlier
questions.stem: Five students' walking times to school, in minutes, are 6, 7, 8, 9 and 60. Which measure best describes a typical walking time, and why?
choices: The mean, because it uses every value
The mean, because outliers do not affect it
The median, because the value 60 pulls the mean up
The range, because it uses the smallest and largest values
questions.answer: The median, because the value 60 pulls the mean up
questions.solution: The median is 8 minutes. The mean is $90 \div 5 = 18$ minutes, which is larger than four of the five times because the 60 pulls it up. The median describes a typical time better here.

solve.answer: The median, because the value 60 pulls the mean up
solve.work: Mean = 90 / 5 = 18, pulled up by the outlier 60; median 8 is typical. Range is spread, not centre; outliers do affect the mean.

questions.skill: The mean as a balance point or fair share
questions.stem: A data set of four values has a mean of 20. Three of the values are 13, 17 and 26. How many units above the mean is the fourth value?
questions.solution: Four values with a mean of 20 add up to $4 \times 20 = 80$. The three known values add up to $13 + 17 + 26 = 56$, so the fourth value is $80 - 56 = 24$. That is $24 - 20 = 4$ units above the mean.

solve.work: Total = 4*20 = 80. 13+17+26 = 56. Fourth = 24, which is 24-20 = 4 above the mean. (Check deviations: -7, -3, +6, +4 sum to 0.)

questions.skill: The mean as a balance point or fair share
questions.stem: Jada's four test scores are 70, 80, 90 and 100, and their mean is 85. Which statement is true?
choices: The scores above 85 are 25 points away from 85 in all, and the scores below 85 are 15 points away in all
The scores above 85 are 10 points away from 85 in all, and the scores below 85 are 30 points away in all
The scores above 85 are 20 points away from 85 in all, and the scores below 85 are 30 points away in all
The scores above 85 are 20 points away from 85 in all, and the scores below 85 are also 20 points away in all
questions.answer: The scores above 85 are 20 points away from 85 in all, and the scores below 85 are also 20 points away in all
questions.solution: The scores above 85 are 90 and 100, which are $5 + 15 = 20$ points away. The scores below 85 are 70 and 80, which are $15 + 5 = 20$ points away. The mean is the balance point, so the two totals are equal.

solve.answer: The scores above 85 are 20 points away from 85 in all, and the scores below 85 are also 20 points away in all

questions.skill: The mean as a balance point or fair share
questions.stem: Six students scored 3, 4, 4, 5, 6 and 8 points in a game. All of the points are pooled and then shared equally by the six students. How many points does each student get?
questions.solution: The pool holds $3 + 4 + 4 + 5 + 6 + 8 = 30$ points. Shared equally among 6 students, each gets $30 \div 6 = 5$ points.

questions.skill: The mean as a balance point or fair share
questions.stem: Four plants are 6, 7, 8 and 15 centimeters tall. Suppose the plants all had the same height and the total of their heights stayed the same. How many centimeters tall would each plant be?
questions.solution: The total height is $6 + 7 + 8 + 15 = 36$ centimeters. Shared equally by 4 plants, each is $36 \div 4 = 9$ centimeters tall. (7.5 is the median, 15 is the tallest plant and 36 is the total.)

questions.skill: The mean as a balance point or fair share
questions.stem: A data set with five values has a mean of 12. The values that are below 12 are a total of 9 units away from 12. In all, how many units away from 12 are the values that are above 12?
questions.solution: The mean is the balance point, so the total distance of the values above it equals the total distance of the values below it. The values above 12 are a total of 9 units away.

solve.work: At the mean, total distance above equals total distance below, so 9.

questions.skill: Finding a mean
questions.stem: Students were asked how many pets they have. Three students have 1 pet, 4 students have 2 pets, 2 students have 3 pets and 1 student has 4 pets. What is the mean number of pets per student?
questions.solution: The number of students is $3 + 4 + 2 + 1 = 10$. The total number of pets is $3 \times 1 + 4 \times 2 + 2 \times 3 + 1 \times 4 = 3 + 8 + 6 + 4 = 21$. The mean is $21 \div 10 = 2.1$ pets per student.

questions.skill: Finding a mean
questions.stem: Four hikes were 1.5, 2, 3.5 and 5 miles long. What is the mean length of the hikes, in miles?
questions.solution: The lengths add up to $1.5 + 2 + 3.5 + 5 = 12$ miles. Dividing by 4 hikes gives $12 \div 4 = 3$ miles.

questions.skill: Finding a mean
questions.stem: The weights of six packages, in pounds, are 12, 15, 9, 20, 14 and 8. What is the mean weight, in pounds?
questions.solution: The weights add up to $12 + 15 + 9 + 20 + 14 + 8 = 78$ pounds. Dividing by 6 packages gives $78 \div 6 = 13$ pounds.

questions.skill: Finding a mean
questions.stem: Over one week, Mei counted her steps each day. In thousands of steps, the counts were 8, 6, 9, 7, 10, 8 and 8. What was the mean number of steps per day, in thousands?
questions.solution: The counts add up to $8+6+9+7+10+8+8 = 56$ thousand steps over 7 days. The mean is $56 \div 7 = 8$ thousand steps.

questions.skill: Finding a mean
questions.stem: Which data set has a mean of 9?
questions.solution: A mean of 9 with 4 values means a total of 36. $5+7+10+14 = 36$. The other sets add up to 37, 34 and 39.

questions.skill: Finding a median
questions.stem: Six students counted the pencils in their cases: 9, 4, 12, 7, 15 and 6. What is the median number of pencils?
questions.solution: Put the counts in order: 4, 6, 7, 9, 12, 15. With 6 values, the median is halfway between the 3rd and 4th values, 7 and 9: $(7 + 9) \div 2 = 8$.

questions.skill: Finding a median
questions.stem: In a survey, 2 students ran 1 lap, 5 students ran 2 laps, 4 students ran 3 laps and 3 students ran 4 laps. What is the median number of laps?
questions.solution: There are $2 + 5 + 4 + 3 = 14$ students. In order, the 1st and 2nd values are 1, the 3rd to 7th are 2, and the 8th to 11th are 3. The median is halfway between the 7th and 8th values, 2 and 3, which is 2.5. The number 2 is the lap count most students ran.

questions.skill: Finding a median
questions.stem: The data are in order: 3, 5, x, 11 and 14. The median is 9. What is the value of x?
questions.solution: With 5 values, the median is the 3rd value, which is x. The median is 9, so x = 9.

solve.work: 5 ordered values, median is the 3rd, so x = 9 (and 5 <= 9 <= 11).

questions.skill: Finding a median
questions.stem: Eight runners finished a race in 31, 28, 35, 30, 29, 33, 36 and 32 seconds. What is the median time, in seconds?
questions.solution: In order, the times are 28, 29, 30, 31, 32, 33, 35, 36. With 8 values, the median is halfway between the 4th and 5th values, 31 and 32: $(31 + 32) \div 2 = 31.5$. The number 31.75 is the mean.

questions.skill: Finding a median
questions.stem: A cafe counted its customers each hour: 12, 18, 15, 22, 18, 9 and 25. What is the median number of customers per hour?
questions.solution: In order, the counts are 9, 12, 15, 18, 18, 22, 25. With 7 values, the median is the 4th value, 18.

questions.skill: Using a mean to find a missing value or a total
questions.stem: In six games, a player scored a mean of 14 points per game. In the first five games the player scored 10, 15, 12, 18 and 13 points. How many points did the player score in the sixth game?
questions.solution: Six games with a mean of 14 add up to $6 \times 14 = 84$ points. The first five games gave $10+15+12+18+13 = 68$ points, so the sixth game was $84 - 68 = 16$ points.

questions.skill: Using a mean to find a missing value or a total
questions.stem: The mean of four numbers is 15. One of the numbers is 24, and the other three are all equal. What is each of the three equal numbers?
questions.solution: Four numbers with a mean of 15 add up to $4 \times 15 = 60$. Without the 24, the other three add up to $60 - 24 = 36$, so each is $36 \div 3 = 12$.

questions.skill: Using a mean to find a missing value or a total
questions.stem: A teacher says her 27 students solved a mean of 7 problems each in a week. How many problems did the students solve in all?
questions.solution: Total = mean $\times$ number of students $= 27 \times 7 = 189$ problems.

questions.skill: Using a mean to find a missing value or a total
questions.stem: Five students have a mean of 14 books each. Four of the students have 10, 12, 15 and 18 books. How many books does the fifth student have?
questions.solution: Five students with a mean of 14 have $5 \times 14 = 70$ books in all. The four known students have $10 + 12 + 15 + 18 = 55$ books, so the fifth has $70 - 55 = 15$ books.

questions.skill: Using a mean to find a missing value or a total
questions.stem: The mean of four numbers is 7.5. Three of the numbers are 6, 9 and 4. What is the fourth number?
questions.solution: Four numbers with a mean of 7.5 add up to $4 \times 7.5 = 30$. The known numbers add up to $6 + 9 + 4 = 19$, so the fourth is $30 - 19 = 11$.

questions.skill: How adding, removing or changing a value affects the mean and median
questions.stem: The mean of five numbers is 8. Every number is doubled. What is the mean of the new numbers?
questions.solution: Doubling every number doubles their total and so doubles the mean: $8 \times 2 = 16$.

solve.work: Doubling every value doubles the total and the mean: 16.

questions.skill: How adding, removing or changing a value affects the mean and median
questions.stem: The numbers 4, 6, 8, 10 and 12 have a mean of 8. The 12 is changed to 27. What is the new mean?
questions.solution: The new numbers 4, 6, 8, 10 and 27 add up to 55, and $55 \div 5 = 11$. (The total went up by $27 - 12 = 15$, so the mean went up by $15 \div 5 = 3$.)

questions.skill: How adding, removing or changing a value affects the mean and median
questions.stem: A data set is 6, 7, 8, 9 and 10. The value 40 is added to the set. Which statement is true?
choices: The mean goes up by more than the median does
The median goes up by more than the mean does
The mean and the median both stay the same
The mean and the median go up by the same amount
questions.answer: The mean goes up by more than the median does
questions.solution: Before: the mean is 8 and the median is 8. After: the mean is $80 \div 6 \approx 13.3$ and the median is $(8 + 9) \div 2 = 8.5$. The mean rose by about 5.3, but the median rose by only 0.5.

solve.answer: The mean goes up by more than the median does
solve.work: Old mean 8, median 8. New: total 80/6 = 13.33 (up 5.33); median (8+9)/2 = 8.5 (up 0.5). Mean rises more.

questions.skill: How adding, removing or changing a value affects the mean and median
questions.stem: The ages of five aunts and uncles are 30, 34, 38, 41 and 45. A sixth relative who is 52 years old joins the list. What is the median age of the six?
questions.solution: The six ages in order are 30, 34, 38, 41, 45, 52. The median is halfway between the 3rd and 4th values, 38 and 41: $(38 + 41) \div 2 = 39.5$.

questions.skill: Comparing the variability of two data sets
questions.stem: Data set P is 14, 18, 22, 25, 31. Data set Q is 20, 22, 25, 27, 29. How many units greater is the range of P than the range of Q?
questions.solution: The range of P is $31 - 14 = 17$. The range of Q is $29 - 20 = 9$. The difference is $17 - 9 = 8$.

questions.skill: Comparing the variability of two data sets
questions.stem: Over five days, Route 1 took 24, 25, 25, 26 and 25 minutes. Over the same five days, Route 2 took 15, 35, 22, 30 and 23 minutes. Which statement is supported by the data?
choices: The two routes have the same mean time, but Route 1's times vary more
The two routes have the same mean time, but Route 2's times vary more
Route 2 has the greater mean time and the times vary less
Route 1 has the greater mean time and the times vary more
questions.answer: The two routes have the same mean time, but Route 2's times vary more
questions.solution: Both routes have a mean of 25 minutes ($125 \div 5$). Route 1's times are close together (range 2), and Route 2's are spread out (range 20), so Route 2 varies more.

solve.answer: The two routes have the same mean time, but Route 2's times vary more
solve.work: Route 1 total 125, mean 25, values 24-26. Route 2: 15+35+22+30+23 = 125, mean 25, range 20. Same mean, Route 2 varies more.

questions.skill: Comparing the variability of two data sets
questions.stem: Data set A has a range of 12. Data set B has a range twice as large as the range of A. The least value in B is 5. What is the greatest value in B?
questions.solution: The range of B is $2 \times 12 = 24$. The greatest value is the least value plus the range: $5 + 24 = 29$.

questions.skill: Choosing the best measure of center
questions.stem: The yearly pay of seven workers at a shop, in thousands of dollars, is 28, 30, 30, 32, 33, 35 and 150. The mean is about 48 and the median is 32. Which statement is best?
choices: The median is better, because the 150 pulls the mean far above the pay of most workers
The mean is better, because it uses every value and is the greater number
The mean and the median describe a typical pay equally well
Neither is useful, because the seven pay values are different
questions.answer: The median is better, because the 150 pulls the mean far above the pay of most workers
questions.solution: Six of the seven workers earn between 28 and 35 thousand dollars, so a typical pay is about 32. The one pay of 150 pulls the mean up to about 48, which is higher than what any of those six earn.

solve.answer: The median is better, because the 150 pulls the mean far above the pay of most workers
solve.work: Sum 338/7 = 48.3 (about 48); median 32. The 150 is an outlier pulling the mean above 6 of 7 workers, so the median is better.

questions.skill: Choosing the best measure of center
questions.stem: For which data set is the median a better description of the center than the mean?
questions.solution: In the first set the value 90 is far from the others, so the mean (21.2) is higher than four of the five values, while the median (4) is typical. The other sets have values close together, so the mean and the median agree.

solve.work: Only 3, 4, 4, 5, 90 has an outlier (mean 21.2 vs median 4). Others are symmetric, mean = median.

questions.skill: Choosing the best measure of center
questions.stem: A student's five math quiz scores are 40, 78, 80, 82 and 85. The mean is 73 and the median is 80. Which measure better describes this student's typical score, and why?
choices: The mean of 73, because it is the middle score when the scores are in order
The median of 80, because the one very low score of 40 pulls the mean below the other four scores
The median of 80, because it is the total of all five scores divided by 5
The mean of 73, because it is higher than most of the five scores
questions.answer: The median of 80, because the one very low score of 40 pulls the mean below the other four scores
questions.solution: Four of the five scores are between 78 and 85, so a typical score is about 80. The very low score of 40 pulls the mean down to 73, which is below four of the five scores. The median is the middle score; the mean is the total divided by 5.

solve.answer: The median of 80, because the one very low score of 40 pulls the mean below the other four scores
solve.work: Mean 365/5 = 73, median 80. Outlier 40 pulls mean below the other four scores (78,80,82,85); median is typical.

questions.skill: How adding a value changes a mean
questions.stem: The mean of 5 numbers is 20. A sixth number, 32, is added to the set. What is the mean of all 6 numbers?
questions.solution: The first 5 numbers add to $5 \times 20 = 100$. With 32 added the total is $132$ for 6 numbers, and $132 \div 6 = 22$.

questions.skill: How an outlier changes the mean
questions.stem: A data set is 4, 5, 6, 7 and 8. The 8 is changed to 38. By how much does the mean increase?
questions.solution: The original total is $30$, so the mean is $30 \div 5 = 6$. The new total is $60$, so the new mean is $60 \div 5 = 12$. The mean increases by $12 - 6 = 6$.

solve.work: Sum rises by 38 - 8 = 30; mean rises by 30 / 5 = 6 (from 6 to 12).

questions.skill: Building a data set with a given mean and median
questions.stem: Which set of numbers has a mean of 10 and a median of 8?
questions.solution: For $6, 8, 8, 12, 16$: the total is 50, so the mean is $50 \div 5 = 10$, and the middle number is 8. The set $8, 8, 9, 12, 13$ has mean 10 but median 9; $5, 8, 10, 13, 14$ has mean 10 but median 10; and $4, 6, 8, 9, 10$ has median 8 but a mean of 7.4.

solve.work: A: sum 50, mean 10, median 9. B: sum 50, mean 10, median 10. C: sum 37, mean 7.4. D: 6+8+8+12+16 = 50, mean 10, median 8. Only D.

questions.skill: The mean as a balance point or fair share
questions.stem: Five values have a mean of 30. Four of them are 4 below the mean, 7 below the mean, 6 above the mean and 3 above the mean. Where is the fifth value?
questions.solution: The distances must balance. Below the mean: $4 + 7 = 11$. Above the mean so far: $6 + 3 = 9$. The fifth value must add $11 - 9 = 2$ more on the above side, so it is 2 above the mean (the value 32).

solve.work: Deviations must sum to 0: -4 -7 +6 +3 = -2, so the fifth deviation is +2: 2 above the mean (value 32).

questions.skill: The mean as a balance point or fair share
questions.stem: Which data set has a mean of 6?
questions.solution: The mean is the total divided by the number of values. $3+5+6+7+9 = 30$ and $30 \div 5 = 6$. The other sets add up to 31, 32 and 29, so their means are 6.2, 6.4 and 5.8. All four sets have a median of 6, but only one has a mean of 6.

questions.skill: The mean as a balance point or fair share
questions.stem: Ali levels five stacks of 3, 4, 9, 2 and 7 cubes by moving cubes from taller stacks onto shorter ones until all five stacks are the same height. What is the fewest number of cubes he has to move?
questions.solution: There are $3+4+9+2+7 = 25$ cubes, so each stack ends with $25 \div 5 = 5$ cubes. The stack of 9 gives away $9 - 5 = 4$ cubes and the stack of 7 gives away $7 - 5 = 2$ cubes, so $4 + 2 = 6$ cubes move.

solve.work: Total 3+4+9+2+7 = 25; level height 5. Excess above 5: 9 has 4, 7 has 2; total 6 cubes must move (each moved cube leaves a tall stack). Fewest = 6.

questions.skill: The mean as a balance point or fair share
questions.stem: Six friends share their trading cards equally, and each ends up with 14 cards. Before sharing, five of them had 9, 12, 20, 15 and 8 cards. How many cards did the sixth friend have before sharing?
questions.solution: Six friends with 14 cards each have $6 \times 14 = 84$ cards in all. The five known friends had $9 + 12 + 20 + 15 + 8 = 64$ cards, so the sixth had $84 - 64 = 20$ cards.

questions.skill: Finding a mean
questions.stem: A shop sold 36, 42, 29, 51 and 38 sandwiches on five days. What is the mean number of sandwiches sold per day?
questions.solution: The sales add up to $36 + 42 + 29 + 51 + 38 = 196$. Dividing by 5 days gives $196 \div 5 = 39.2$. The number 38 is the median, 49 comes from dividing by 4, and 196 is the total.

questions.skill: Finding a mean
questions.stem: On a quiz scored out of 10, 2 students scored 6, 3 students scored 7, 4 students scored 8 and 1 student scored 9. What is the mean score?
questions.solution: There are $2 + 3 + 4 + 1 = 10$ students. The total of the scores is $2 \times 6 + 3 \times 7 + 4 \times 8 + 1 \times 9 = 12 + 21 + 32 + 9 = 74$, so the mean is $74 \div 10 = 7.4$. The number 7.5 is the mean of 6, 7, 8 and 9, and 8 is the score that most students got.

questions.skill: Finding a mean
questions.stem: Find the mean of the six numbers 98, 103, 101, 97, 99 and 102.
questions.solution: The numbers add up to $98 + 103 + 101 + 97 + 99 + 102 = 600$, and $600 \div 6 = 100$. A shortcut: each number is a small step from 100 (-2, +3, +1, -3, -1, +2), and those steps add up to 0.

questions.skill: Finding a mean
questions.stem: The rainfall on five days, in centimeters, was 0.4, 1.2, 0.8, 2 and 0.6. What was the mean rainfall per day, in centimeters?
questions.solution: The rainfall adds up to $0.4 + 1.2 + 0.8 + 2 + 0.6 = 5$ centimeters. Dividing by 5 days gives $5 \div 5 = 1$ centimeter per day.

questions.skill: Finding a mean
questions.stem: Which number is the mean of 1.5, 2.5, 4 and 8?
questions.solution: The numbers add up to $1.5 + 2.5 + 4 + 8 = 16$, and $16 \div 4 = 4$. The number 3.25 is the median, 16 is the total, and 3.2 comes from dividing by 5.

questions.skill: Finding a median
questions.stem: A data set has 10 values. When they are put in order, the 5th value is 14 and the 6th value is 19. What is the median?
questions.solution: With 10 values, the median is halfway between the 5th and 6th values: $(14 + 19) \div 2 = 16.5$.

questions.skill: Finding a median
questions.stem: Which data set has a median of 12?
questions.solution: For the first set there are 6 values, so the median is halfway between the 3rd and 4th: $(11 + 13) \div 2 = 12$. The other sets have medians 14, 12.5 and 13, even though some of them contain a 12.

questions.skill: Finding a median
questions.stem: The four numbers 5, 8, n and 20 are in order, so n is between 8 and 20. Their median is 11. What is n?
questions.solution: With 4 values, the median is halfway between the 2nd and 3rd values: $(8 + n) \div 2 = 11$. So $8 + n = 22$ and $n = 14$.

questions.skill: Finding a median
questions.stem: A survey of 25 students asked how many siblings each has. Six students have 0 siblings, 9 students have 1 sibling, 7 students have 2 siblings and 3 students have 3 siblings. What is the median number of siblings?
questions.solution: With 25 values in order, the median is the 13th value. The first 6 values are 0, and the next 9 values (the 7th to 15th) are 1, so the 13th value is 1.

solve.work: 6+9+7+3 = 25; median is the 13th. Values 0 occupy 1-6, value 1 occupies 7-15. 13th = 1.

questions.skill: Finding a median
questions.stem: A set of 9 numbers has a median of 25. Which statement must be true?
choices: When the numbers are put in order, the 4th number is 25
When the numbers are put in order, the 5th number is 25
The number 25 appears more than once
questions.answer: When the numbers are put in order, the 5th number is 25
questions.solution: With 9 values, the median is the 5th value when they are in order, so the 5th number must be 25. The others need not be true: the numbers could add up to anything, and 25 could appear only once.

solve.answer: When the numbers are put in order, the 5th number is 25
solve.work: With 9 ordered values the median is the 5th, so the 5th is 25. Sum 225 would need mean 25, not required; repetition not required.

questions.skill: Using a mean to find a missing value or a total
questions.stem: The mean of 6 numbers is 9. When a seventh number is added, the mean of the 7 numbers is 10. What is the seventh number?
questions.solution: The first 6 numbers add up to $6 \times 9 = 54$. All 7 numbers add up to $7 \times 10 = 70$. The seventh number is $70 - 54 = 16$.

questions.skill: Using a mean to find a missing value or a total
questions.stem: The mean of 8 numbers is 12. One number is removed, and the mean of the remaining 7 numbers is 11. What number was removed?
questions.solution: The 8 numbers add up to $8 \times 12 = 96$. The remaining 7 numbers add up to $7 \times 11 = 77$. The number removed is $96 - 77 = 19$.

questions.skill: Using a mean to find a missing value or a total
questions.stem: After four quizzes, Omar's mean score is 82. What score does he need on the fifth quiz to raise his mean to 84?
questions.solution: After four quizzes, his scores add up to $4 \times 82 = 328$. For a mean of 84 after five quizzes, they must add up to $5 \times 84 = 420$. He needs $420 - 328 = 92$ on the fifth quiz.

questions.skill: Using a mean to find a missing value or a total
questions.stem: A class of 10 students has a mean score of 70 on a test. A second class of 15 students has a mean score of 80 on the same test. What is the mean score of all 25 students together?
questions.solution: The first class's scores add up to $10 \times 70 = 700$ and the second class's to $15 \times 80 = 1200$. Together, $700 + 1200 = 1900$ over 25 students gives $1900 \div 25 = 76$. It is not 75, because the larger class counts for more.

questions.skill: How adding, removing or changing a value affects the mean and median
questions.stem: The mean weight of 6 puppies is 15 pounds. The heaviest puppy, which weighs 25 pounds, is sold. What is the mean weight, in pounds, of the 5 puppies that are left?
questions.solution: The 6 puppies weigh $6 \times 15 = 90$ pounds in all. Without the 25-pound puppy, the other 5 weigh $90 - 25 = 65$ pounds, so their mean is $65 \div 5 = 13$ pounds.

questions.skill: How adding, removing or changing a value affects the mean and median
questions.stem: The data set is 2, 4, 6, 8 and 10. Which change leaves the median the same but raises the mean?
questions.solution: Changing 10 to 30 leaves 6 in the middle, so the median is still 6, and the total rises from 30 to 50, so the mean rises. Changing 2 to 0 keeps the median but lowers the mean. Changing 6 to 9 makes the median 8, and changing 8 to 3 makes the median 4.

solve.work: 10->30: median 6, mean 10 (up). 6->9: median 8. 2->0: mean down. 8->3: median 4. Only the first.

questions.skill: How adding, removing or changing a value affects the mean and median
questions.stem: The mean of a data set is 5. Every value is multiplied by 3, and then 2 is added to every result. What is the mean of the new data set?
questions.solution: Multiplying every value by 3 multiplies the mean by 3, giving 15. Adding 2 to every value adds 2 to the mean. The new mean is $3 \times 5 + 2 = 17$.

questions.skill: How adding, removing or changing a value affects the mean and median
questions.stem: Five numbers have a mean of 20. Two of them, 8 and 12, are replaced by 15 and 25. What is the mean of the new set of five numbers?
questions.solution: The original total is $5 \times 20 = 100$. Taking out $8 + 12 = 20$ and putting in $15 + 25 = 40$ makes the total $100 - 20 + 40 = 120$. The new mean is $120 \div 5 = 24$.

questions.skill: How adding, removing or changing a value affects the mean and median
questions.stem: The mean of four numbers is 10. A fifth number is added to the set, and the mean of the five numbers is still 10. What is the fifth number?
questions.solution: The four numbers add up to $4 \times 10 = 40$. Five numbers with a mean of 10 add up to $5 \times 10 = 50$. The fifth number is $50 - 40 = 10$: a new value equal to the mean leaves the mean unchanged.

questions.skill: Comparing the variability of two data sets
questions.stem: The data are 3, 5, 6, 8, 9, 11, 12 and 15. The first quartile is the median of the lower half of the data, and the third quartile is the median of the upper half. What is the interquartile range (IQR), which is the third quartile minus the first quartile?
questions.solution: The lower half is 3, 5, 6, 8, with median $(5 + 6) \div 2 = 5.5$. The upper half is 9, 11, 12, 15, with median $(11 + 12) \div 2 = 11.5$. The IQR is $11.5 - 5.5 = 6$.

questions.skill: Comparing the variability of two data sets
questions.stem: Set X is 2, 6, 10, 14, 18. Set Y is 6, 8, 10, 12, 14. Which statement is true?
choices: Set Y is more spread out: its range is 8, compared with 16 for Set X
The sets are equally spread out, because both have a mean of 10 and a median of 10
Set X is more spread out, because its median is greater than the median of Set Y
Set X is more spread out: its range is 16, compared with 8 for Set Y
questions.answer: Set X is more spread out: its range is 16, compared with 8 for Set Y
questions.solution: Both sets have a mean of 10 and a median of 10, so their centers are the same. The range of X is $18 - 2 = 16$ and the range of Y is $14 - 6 = 8$, so X varies more.

solve.answer: Set X is more spread out: its range is 16, compared with 8 for Set Y
solve.work: Range X = 16, range Y = 8; both have mean and median 10. X is more spread out.

questions.skill: Comparing the variability of two data sets
questions.stem: A data set is 15, 18, 20, 22 and 25. A new value, 30, is added to the set. By how many units does the range increase?
questions.solution: Before, the range is $25 - 15 = 10$. After adding 30, the range is $30 - 15 = 15$. It increases by $15 - 10 = 5$.

questions.skill: Comparing the variability of two data sets
questions.stem: The 11 values 4, 6, 7, 9, 10, 12, 13, 15, 16, 18 and 21 are in order. The first quartile is the median of the lower half (not counting the middle value), and the third quartile is the median of the upper half (not counting the middle value). What is the interquartile range, which is the third quartile minus the first quartile?
questions.solution: The middle value is the 6th, which is 12. The lower half is 4, 6, 7, 9, 10, with median 7. The upper half is 13, 15, 16, 18, 21, with median 16. The IQR is $16 - 7 = 9$.

questions.skill: Choosing the best measure of center
questions.stem: Kara has the data 2, 3, 3, 4, 4 and 5. She adds the value 40. Because 40 is so much greater than the other values, she decides that the median is the better measure of center. What is the median of the seven values?
questions.solution: In order, the seven values are 2, 3, 3, 4, 4, 5, 40. The median is the 4th value, which is 4. (The mean would be about 8.7, higher than six of the seven values.)

questions.skill: Choosing the best measure of center
questions.stem: In one year, 9 students had 0, 0, 0, 0, 1, 1, 2, 2 and 12 absences. The mean is 2 and the median is 1. A parent says a typical student misses about 2 days. Which response is best?
choices: The mean of 2 is more typical, because it uses every value and the 12 is part of the data
The mean of 2 is more typical, because it is the middle value of the data
The median of 1 is more typical, because it is the greatest value that most students have
The median of 1 is more typical, because the 12 raises the mean above what most students have
questions.answer: The median of 1 is more typical, because the 12 raises the mean above what most students have
questions.solution: Eight of the nine students have 2 or fewer absences, and half of them have 0 or 1. The one student with 12 pulls the mean up to 2. The median, the middle value, is 1, so it is the better description of a typical student.
